author: Sophia Sheera
title: Nobel Prize-Winning Economists Back First Billionaire Tax in US
content:
Six Nobel Prize-winning economists have signed an open letter supporting what could be the first billionaire wealth tax in the US, if voters approve it this November. 


The economists, including former chief economist of the World Bank, Joseph Stiglitz, say that a one-time 5% tax on billionaire residents of California could kickstart wealth distribution in the US and across the world. 


Tech entrepreneurs based in and around Silicon Valley have

spent at least $120m

 lobbying against the tax, known as Proposition 40, since January. Google co-founder Segrey Brin has donated $102m to an opposition group funding an advertising blitz against the ballot. 


In an

open letter

 published on Saturday, the six economists said the one-off tax could be the first step towards reining in billionaire power. 


“If the state that houses some of the country’s most powerful billionaires votes to tax their wealth, it will kickstart a movement to tax ultra-high-net-worth individuals in other states – and eventually at the federal level and in other countries,” they wrote. 


“As Californians head to the polls, their vote may well come to be seen as a turning point in the battle between democracy and oligarchy.”


They added that billionaires accounted for only 1% of donations during the 2000 federal election cycle, a figure which had jumped to 19% by 2024. 


Alongside Stiglitz, the letter was signed by MIT professors Peter Diamond, Daron Acemoglu, Abhijeet Banerjee and Esther Duflo as well as City University of New York professor and journalist Paul Krugman. 


California’s billionaires were taxed on only 1.9% of their collective $1.4tn wealth gain between 2019 and 2024 – a percentage far lower than that paid by ordinary Californians. 


The one-off tax, which would raise about $100bn, would offset cuts to Medicaid and food assistance produced by President Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act in 2025. 


Jensen Huang, CEO of the world’s most valuable company, Nvidia, previously told Bloomberg he would be “

perfectly fine

” with the 5% levy. With a net worth of $159bn, Huang alone could face a tax of $7bn. 


One of the letter’s signatories, Daron Acemoglu, spoke about the

dangers of big tech oligopolies

 on Downstream yesterday with Novara Media’s Aaron Bastani.

title: ᐊᓄᕆᒨᖅᑐᒥ ᐸᐅᕋᐅᑎᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᕙᓪᓕᐊᕗᖅ ᑲᑉᐱᕼᐃᓕᖅᑑᖅ ᒎᓗᒧᑦ ᐅᔭᕋᖕᓂᐊᕐᕕᖓᓄᑦ
content:
For the English version of this story, please see

Kitikmeot Inuit Association, Tugliq Energy to receive $20M loan for wind project

.


ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᓄᓇᓖᑦ ᐊᑐᖅᐸᒃᑕᖏᓐᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᔪᓐᓇᖁᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᒃᑯᕕᖓ ᐊᑐᖅᑐᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᕗᖅ $20 ᒥᓕᐊᓐᓂ ᒪᓐᑐᕆᐋᓪᒧᑦ-ᑐᙵᕕᓕᖕᒥ ᑲᒻᐸᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᕿᑎᕐᒥᐅᑦ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᖏᑦᑕ ᓇᖕᒥᓂᕆᔭᐅᔪᒧᑦ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᓚᖓ ᐊᓄᕆᒨᖅᑐᒧᑦ ᐆᒻᒪᖅᑯᑎᓕᕆᕝᕕᖕᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᐅᔪᒧᑦ ᐊᒡᓂᑯ ᐄᒍᓪ ᐅᔭᕋᖕᓂᐊᕐᕕᒃ ᓕᑎᒥᑦᑯᑦ ᑲᑉᐱᕼᐃᓕᖅᑑᖅ ᒎᓗᒧᑦ ᐅᔭᕋᖕᓂᐊᕐᕕᖓᓄᑦ ᐃᓂᒋᔭᖓᓂ ᖃᓂᒋᔮᓂ.


ᑮᓇᐅᔭᒃᑯᕕᒃ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐊᑐᖅᑐᐊᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᓯᑎᐱᕆ 9−ᒥ ᑐᓴᒐᒃᓴᓕᐊᖑᔪᒥ.


ᓯᕗᓪᓕᖅᐸᐅᔪᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᐅᔪᒥ ᑕᑯᓂᐊᖅᐳᖅ 4.2-ᒥᐊᒐᐅᐊᑦ ᐊᓄᕆᒨᖅᑐᒥ ᐸᐅᕋᐅᑎᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ 4-ᒥᐊᒐᐅᐊᑦ ᐆᒻᒪᖅᑯᑎᒧᑦ ᑐᖅᑯᖅᑕᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᔾᔪᓯᐅᔪᒥ ᐃᓕᔭᐅᔪᒥ ᓴᓂᓕᐊᓂ ᐅᔭᕋᖕᓂᐊᕐᕕᖓᓄᑦ, ᐃᓂᖃᖅᑐᒥ 125 ᑭᓛᒥᑐᐸᓗᖕᓂ ᓂᒋᖅᐸᓯᐊᓂ ᐃᖃᓗᒃᑑᑦᑎᐊᕐᒥ.


ᓂᕆᐅᒋᔭᐅᕗᖅ ᑐᓂᓯᓂᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂ 20 ᐳᓴᓐᑎᒥ ᑲᑉᐱᕼᐃᓕᖅᑑᑉ ᐆᒻᒪᖅᑯᑎᖏᓐᓂ ᐱᔭᕆᐊᓕᖏᓐᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐊᓄᕌᕐᔪᐊᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᐊᒻᒪ ᒥᒃᖠᒋᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᓗᓂ ᐅᔭᕋᖕᓂᐊᕐᕕᐅᑉ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᑕᒫᒥ ᐅᖅᓱᐊᓗᑐᐃᓐᓇᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᑐᕐᓂᖏᓐᓂ 7 ᐳᓴᓐᑎᒧᑦ, ᐅᖃᐅᓯᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᐊᒡᓂᑯ ᐄᒍᓪᑯᓐᓂ.


“ᑕᑉᐹᓂ ᐊᓄᕆᖃᕐᔪᐊᖅᑐᐊᓗᒃ,” ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐊᒡᓂᑯ ᐄᒍᓪ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᑉ-ᑐᖏᓕᖓ ᑯᕆᒡᑕᕗ ᐋᑕᒻᔅ ᐅᖃᓘᑎᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᐱᖅᓱᖅᑕᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᕕᖓᓂᑦ ᑐᕌᓐᑎᒥ. “ᐅᓇ ᖁᕕᐊᔾᔪᑎᒋᕐᔪᐊᖅᐸᕗᑦ ᐱᒋᐊᕐᓂᕐᒥᕐ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᕐᒥ ᐸᐅᕋᐅᑎᒥᒃ. ᐸᕐᓇᒃᐳᒍᑦ ᓴᓇᓂᕐᒥ ᑎᓴᒪᒃᑲᓐᓂᕐᓂ.”


ᓅᓐᓂᖅ ᐅᖅᓱᐊᓗᑐᐃᓐᓇᒥᒃ ᐊᓄᕆᒨᖅᑐᒥ ᐆᒻᒪᖅᑯᑎᓄᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᐊᑐᓗᐊᙱᑎᑦᑎᓂᖅᓴᐅᔾᔮᙱᒃᑲᓗᐊᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᐅᔭᕋᖕᓂᐊᕐᕕᖕᒧᑦ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᕐᒥ, ᐋᑕᒻᔅ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐊᒡᓂᑯ ᐄᒍᓪ ᖁᕕᐊᓱᒃᐳᖅ ᐃᑲᔪᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᒥᒃᖠᒋᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᓄᓇᕘᑉ ᐊᑐᓕᒪᓂᖓᓂ ᐅᖅᓱᐊᓗᑐᐃᓐᓇᕐᒥᑦ.


“ᓲᕐᓗ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᖅᐹᒥᒃ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᑎᑐᑦ, ᓯᕗᓪᓕᖅᐹᖑᔪᒥ ᐊᓄᕆᒨᖅᑐᒥ ᐸᐅᕋᐅᑎᒥ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᐅᕙᑦᑎᓐᓂ ᑐᓂᓯᓪᓚᕆᖕᓂᐊᖅᑐᖅ ᐱᕕᒃᓴᖃᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑐᑭᓯᓪᓚᑦᑖᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᐱᔪᓐᓇᕐᓂᑦᑎᓐᓂ,” ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᐅᔪᖅ ᐊᓯᐊᓂ ᐱᕚᓪᓕᕈᑎᖃᕐᓂᐊᕆᕗᖅ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᕿᑎᕐᒥᐅᑦ ᑎᒥᖁᑎᖓ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᔨᒻᒪᕆᒃ ᑕᐃᕕᑦ ᐅᒥᓪᒍᐃᑦᑐᖅ: ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᒃᓴᓂ ᐱᕕᒃᓴᖃᕐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐃᓄᖕᓄᑦ.


“ᐅᒃᐱᕈᓱᒃᐳᒍᑦ ᐅᓇ ᐱᒋᐊᕐᓂᐅᓂᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᖏᓂᖅᓴᐅᔪᒥ ᑲᑎᖅᓱᖅᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᑐᖅᑯᖅᑕᐅᓯᒪᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐱᕈᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᑎᑕᐅᔪᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑮᓇᐅᔾᔭᒃᓴᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᒃᑐᐃᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐃᓗᐊᓂ ᐊᕕᒃᑐᖅᓯᒪᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᒐᓴᓄᑦ ᑎᑭᑉᐸᓪᓕᐊᔪᓄᑦ,” ᐅᒥᓪᒍᐃᑦᑐᖅ ᑎᑎᕋᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᑐᓴᒐᒃᓴᓕᐊᖑᔪᒥ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᓄᓇᓖᑦ ᐊᑐᖅᐸᒃᑕᖏᓐᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᔪᓐᓇᖁᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᒃᑯᕕᖓᓐᓂ


ᕼᐃᓗᕆ ᑖᑦᓱᕐ, ᑮᓇᐅᔭᒃᑯᕕᐅᑉ ᐃᓱᒻᒥᖅᑐᐃᔨᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᑉ-ᑐᖏᓕᖓ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑳᖅᓯᒪᔪᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᓄᓇᓖᑦ ᐊᑐᖅᐸᒃᑕᖏᓐᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᔪᓐᓇᖁᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᑲᑎᖅᓱᖅᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᑐᖅᑯᖅᑕᐅᓯᒪᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐱᕈᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᑎᑕᐅᔪᓂ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᖓ ᒐᕙᒪᑐᖃᒃᑯᑦ ᑎᒥᐅᕗᖅ ᑕᐅᑐᒃᑕᑐᐊᖃᑲᐃᓐᓇᖅᑐᒥ ᐊᒃᑐᐃᓂᐅᔪᓂ, ᓲᕐᓗ ᒥᒃᖠᒋᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᓯᓚᕐᔪᐊᑉ ᐅᔅᓯᒃᓯᕙᓪᓕᐊᔾᔪᑎᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᓯᐊᖅᑭᔪᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑮᓇᐅᔾᔭᒃᓴᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᓚᐅᖃᑕᐅᓂᕐᒥ ᐃᓄᖕᓂ, ᖃᑭᓇᓱᐊᕐᓂᐅᙱᑦᑐᒧᑦ.


“ᓴᖑᓴᕋᐃᓐᓂᖅᓴᐅᕗᒍᑦ ᐊᑭᓕᖅᓱᐃᑎᑦᑎᓂᑦᑎᓐᓂ,” ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ. “ᑮᓇᐅᔭᑦ ᐅᑎᖅᑎᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᖃᖅᐳᑦ, ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᐅᕙᓃᙱᓚᒍᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᐅᕐᕌᓗᒐᓱᙱᓐᓂᕐᒧᑦ.”


“ᐊᓄᕆᖃᑦᑎᐊᕈᕕᑦ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑦᑎᒍᓂ ᐆᒻᒪᖅᑯᑎᕐᔪᐊᓂ, ᐊᑭᓕᖅᑕᐅᔪᓐᓇᖅᐳᒍᑦ ᕿᓚᒻᒥᐅᓂᖅᓴᐅᔪᒥ, ᑕᐃᒫᒃ ᓴᖑᓴᕋᐃᓐᓂᖃᕐᔪᐊᖅᐳᒍᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓵᙵᔭᐅᔾᔪᑎᖃᖅᑎᑦᑎᕙᙱᓚᒍᑦ ᓂᐅᕕᖅᐸᒃᑐᓂ, ᓵᙵᔭᐅᔾᔪᑎᖃᖅᑎᑦᑎᕙᙱᓚᒍᑦ ᐊᑐᖅᑐᐊᖅᑎᑕᑦᑎᓐᓂ ᑖᔅᓱᒥᖓ ᐱᔾᔪᑎᓕᖕᒥ.”


ᑲᑉᐱᕼᐃᓕᖅᑑᖅ ᐅᔭᕋᖕᓂᐊᕐᕕᖓ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᐅᕗᖅ ᐊᒡᓂᑯ ᐄᒍᓪᑯᑦ ᐱᖓᓱᓂ ᒎᓗᒧᑦ ᐅᔭᕋᖕᓂᐊᕐᕕᖏᓐᓂ ᓄᓇᕗᒻᒥ. ᐊᐃᑉᐸᖏᑦ ᒪᕐᕉᒃ ᐊᐳᖅᑎᓈᖅᑐᖅ ᕐᕕᒃ, ᐃᓂᖃᖅᑐᖅ ᖃᒪᓂᑦᑐᐊᑉ ᖃᓂᒋᔭᖓᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᖃᓗᒑᕐᔪᒃ ᕐᕕᒃ, ᐃᓂᖃᖅᑐᖅ ᑲᖏᖅᖠᓂᐅᑉ ᖃᓂᒋᔭᖓᓂ.


ᐸᐅᕋᐅᑎ ᑐᓂᔭᐅᓵᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᑲᑉᐱᕼᐃᓕᖅᑑᖅ ᐃᓂᒋᔭᖓᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑐᒃᓴᐅᑕᐅᕗᖅ ᐆᒻᒪᖅᑯᓯᐅᓕᕐᓂᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᓂᐅᓂᐊᖅᑐᒥ.

author: Mag
title: Venezuela: Nicht nur Arbeiter:innen des öffentlichen Sektors und v.a. des Bildungswesens protestieren zur Verteidigung von Löhnen und Tarifrechten
content:
Dossier


„

Die venezolanischen Gewerkschaften des öffentlichen Sektors haben am Dienstag eine Kundgebung abgehalten, um höhere Gehälter und die Achtung der Arbeitnehmerrechte zu fordern. Der Marsch im Zentrum von Caracas richtete sich gegen eine Richtlinie des Nationalen Haushaltsamtes (ONAPRE), sie setzt eine Reihe von Tarifrechten außer Kraft und sieht u.a. die 50-prozentige Kürzung von Lohnzuschlägen für Erfahrung oder Bildungsniveau vor, die zu einer Abflachung der Gehaltstabellen führt. (…) Rentner des öffentlichen Dienstes, Krankenschwestern, Lehrer und Universitätsangestellte waren einige der Sektoren, die bei der Kundgebung stark vertreten waren. Eine weitere Gewerkschaft, die an dem Marsch teilnahm, vertrat die Beschäftigten von SUPRA, dem Abfallentsorgungsunternehmen in Caracas. (…) Die Gewerkschaft SUPRA hat in den letzten Wochen eine Reihe von Protesten veranstaltet und zeitweise den Sitz des städtischen Unternehmens am Stadtrand von Caracas besetzt.

..“ Aus dem engl.

Artikel von Ricardo Vaz am 14.7.2022 in venezuelanalysis.com


, siehe weitere Infos zu den anhaltenden Protesten:


24. September: Demonstration in Caracas und in allen 24 Bundesstaaten Venezuelas, um – nach 4 Jahren – erneut die Erhöhung der Löhne und Renten zu fordern


„

Seit nunmehr vier Jahren gab es keine Erhöhung der Löhne, Gehälter oder

Renten mehr. Dagegen steigen täglich die Preise für Lebensmittel,

Medikamente, Dienstleistungen und Transport. Unterdessen wird das Land

ausgeplündert und unter den Regierenden, der US-Regierung und ihren

Ölkonzernen aufgeteilt. Die Arbeitnehmer verfügen nicht über ein

existenzsicherndes Einkommen, und wir können diese Situation nicht

länger hinnehmen. Lasst uns für Löhne kämpfen und der Verweigerung

unserer Rechte ein Ende setzen!

“ span.

Aufruf von CNCTL bei Laboursolidarity


 (maschinenübersetzt) auch zur Kundgebung zur Unterstützung der Forderungen der pensionierten Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer des staatlichen Telekommunikationsunternehmens CANTV am Freitag, dem 4. September, auf der Plaza Caracas vor dem Arbeitsministerium mit Original und Videos


Nach anhaltenden Protesten kündigt die Präsidentin Venezuelas eine Erhöhung von Mindestlohn und Renten an, die am 1. Mai breit gegen die „Verhöhnung“ mobilisiert


Arbeiter protestieren in Caracas nach einer Lohnerhöhung


„

Mehr als tausend Arbeitnehmer demonstrierten am Freitag, dem 1. Mai, in der venezolanischen Hauptstadt, um gegen eine am Vortag angekündigte Lohnerhöhung zu protestieren, die sie als „Verhöhnung“ betrachten.


Das sogenannte „umfassende Mindesteinkommen“ wurde von 190 Dollar auf 240 Dollar pro Monat angehoben, was einer Steigerung von 26 % entspricht, wie die amtierende Präsidentin Venezuelas, Delcy Rodríguez, am Donnerstag mitteilte, ohne weitere Einzelheiten zu nennen.

Dieses Einkommen besteht aus einem Prämienmodell, das sich nicht auf die Sozialversicherungsbeiträge der Arbeitnehmer auswirkt und daher weder bei der Berechnung der Altersrente noch bei der Berechnung von Sozialleistungen berücksichtigt wird. Der seit 2022 eingefrorene Mindestlohn liegt unter 30 Cent, ein lächerlicher Betrag in einem Land mit galoppierender Inflation.


Unter dem Slogan „Zulagen sind kein Lohn“ marschierten am Freitag etwa 1.500 Arbeitnehmer, Gewerkschafter und Rentner rund vier Kilometer durch die Innenstadt von Caracas. Dutzende Bereitschaftspolizisten sperrten einige Straßen ab, es kam jedoch zu keinen Zusammenstößen. „Das ist ein Hohn, das ist Betrug“, sagte Franklin Velásquez, ein 61-jähriger Gewerkschaftsführer. „Heute wissen wir Arbeitnehmer in Venezuela nicht, wie hoch der Mindestlohn ist, und das ist, ich wiederhole es, ein Hohn“, fügte er hinzu.

Die Regierung greift auf Gutscheine zurück, um das Einkommen der Arbeitnehmer zu verbessern, die den niedrigsten Mindestlohn der Region beziehen, der seit vier Jahren eingefroren ist. (…)


Die erste Anpassung nach dem Sturz von Nicolás Maduro bleibt jedoch hinter den Kosten für einen Grundnahrungsmittelkorb für eine fünfköpfige Familie zurück, die sich auf fast 700 Dollar im Monat belaufen. (…)


Kleinere Demonstrationen wurden laut AFP auch an anderen Orten des Landes verzeichnet, beispielsweise in der Grenzstadt San Cristóbal und in Barinas, einer ehemaligen Hochburg des Chavismus. „Die Arbeitnehmer dürfen nicht länger die Last einer Krise tragen, die sie nicht verursacht haben“, erklärte der Gewerkschafter José Patines aus der Heimat des beliebten verstorbenen …

author: Sergey Eledinov and Konstantin Terentev
title: There’s No Conspiracy in the Sahel — There’s a Gap, and Bamako Knows How to Use It
content:
A familiar claim keeps surfacing in the rhetoric of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger’s ruling juntas, echoed enthusiastically by Russian state media: the West is deliberately working to destabilise the Sahel’s military governments. It’s a tidy story. It bundles sanctions, frozen aid and diplomatic isolation into a single narrative of conspiracy. But look closely at who is actually doing what, and what looks like a strategy of destabilisation turns out to be the side effect of something else entirely — and the chief beneficiary of the gap between intention and outcome is not some abstract “West” or abstract “Moscow”, but Bamako, which reads that mismatch more accurately than any outside player.


Bamako, Mali.


A real dependency, just not the one people assume


The dependency of the Alliance of Sahel States on Russian military backing is well documented: public defence agreements, official statements, the visible reshuffling of security infrastructure on the ground. After France’s Barkhane force withdrew from Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger in 2022–2023, and the US shut its Agadez base in 2024, the Wagner Group stepped into the role of security guarantor, formally folding into Africa Corps under Russia’s defence ministry in 2025.


Call it a trade, though not as one-sided as it is usually described. The juntas get military backing — uneven on the battlefield, as the April 2026 offensive by JNIM and the Azawad Liberation Front, which retook Kidal, made painfully clear — but it was the only option left once France and the US pulled out. Moscow gets a geopolitical asset: a foothold, leverage against the West, proof that Russia still matters in Africa even while fighting a

war in Ukraine

. But the arrangement was never static. From the start, Bamako understood that dependency on Russia need not mean exclusivity, and it behaved accordingly.


From that dependency, a syllogism follows easily: if the West is squeezing Russia globally, and Sahelian regimes are tied to Russia’s presence, then pressure on Moscow should ripple outward and hit those regimes too. The logic holds. The problem is the leap from effect to intent. The only way to tell them apart is to look at how the actors involved actually behaved — and how Mali’s own government responded.


Sanctions hit somewhere other than people assume


Between 2020 and 2024, the US, EU and UK rolled out sanctions against Wagner-linked companies and individuals across Africa: gold-mining operations in the Central African Republic (Midas Ressources, Diamville, Industrial Resources), figures tied to the Mali operation, including its coordinator

Andrei Ivanov

, and Sudan-based entities like Meroe Gold and M Invest. In January 2023,

the US Treasury designated Wagner a transnational criminal organisation

, framing the goal as countering “Russia’s destabilising activities in Africa” — a response to Russian activity, not an independent plan aimed at Sahelian states.


None of these measures targeted the governments of Mali, Burkina Faso or Niger directly. The only way to test intent is to look at how the same actors behaved in investment and diplomacy — and, by extension, at what Bamako itself managed to extract from that behaviour.


You don’t invest in what you’re trying to wreck — and Bamako knows it


If destabilising the AES regimes were an actual policy goal, you’d expect some consistency: sanctions, isolation, a refusal to engage. The 2020–2026 record shows the opposite.


The clearest case is the United States. On 27 February 2026,

the Treasury lifted sanctions

 on three senior Malian officials — Defence Minister Sadio Camara, Air Force chief of staff Alou Boï Diarra, and his deputy Adama Bagayoko — all three sanctioned since 2023 for facilitating Wagner’s operations. According to

The Africa Report

, and independently confirmed by

africa-eye.com

, the immediate trigger was the search for Kevin Rideout, an American pilot kidnapped by jihadists near Niamey in October 2025 and believed held in Mali. In the same period, a State Department official met Mali’s foreign minister, Abdoulaye Diop, in Bamako, and

Reuters reported

 Washington was nearing a deal that would let US aircraft and drones resume intelligence-gathering flights over Malian territory against groups linked to al-Qaeda — Washington was seeking to restart operations that had earlier been suspended. One and the same government ran a sanctions track and a rapprochement track in the same window — and Mali’s side …

author: dev
title: CRISPR, thérapie génique et OGM humains
content:
Fin mars 2025, une fillette de 6 ans décède suite à l'injection d'une thérapie génique expérimentale en Chine. Comment faire sens de cet événement ? Deuxième billet des Chroniques du bio-technofascisme en cours

 [

1

]

.


Plusieurs

articles

 parus cet été relatent l'histoire de la mort d'une petite fille de 6 ans, sous le pseudonyme de Mei, lors d'un traitement de thérapie génique personnalisée et expérimentale dans l'hôpital Xinhua, affilié à l'université Jiaotong de Shanghaï. Bien qu'ayant eu lieu en mars 2025, l'affaire n'est révélée qu'en juillet 2026, dans une

enquête

 de

Science et Retraction Watch

.


Les thérapies géniques


Le principe de la thérapie génique est simple : certaines maladies, comme la mucoviscidose, seraient dues à une mutation unique de l'ADN, située dans un seul gène. Remplacer ou modifier ce gène pour lui redonner sa forme

normale

 guérirait la maladie. Un simple jeu de Lego ou de mécanique où il s'agirait de changer une pièce du système, comme un carburateur, pour que tout rentre dans l'ordre.


La méthode générale de la thérapie génique est d'injecter, dans les cellules ciblées, des molécules qui découpent l'ADN à des endroits spécifiques et qui réparent cet ADN, par exemple en y insérant un nouveau morceau. À toutes les étapes, la précision est évidemment cruciale.


Les premières tentatives de thérapie génique datent des années 1990, dans le contexte d'optimisme technologique démesuré du projet de séquençage du génome humain. À cette époque, les technologies utilisées pour modifier l'ADN sont celles de la recombinaison génétique, ou la transgénèse, développées à partir des années 1970. Dans les années 2010, le système CRISPR, plus rapide et plus précis, est adopté par toute la communauté scientifique et l'industrie pharmaceutique, notamment pour le développement de thérapies géniques.


Les risques liés aux thérapies géniques CRISPR sont connus et identifiés. Ils sont de deux types. Tout d'abord, l'intervention sur l'ADN par le système CRISPR n'est jamais 100 % précise et peut provoquer des dommages imprévisibles – la thérapie peut provoquer des mutations génétiques qui peuvent être fatales. Ensuite, toute thérapie génique se heurte au problème du transport du système CRISPR dans les cellules dont l'ADN doit être modifié. En effet, il serait délétère et par ailleurs impossible techniquement de modifier l'ADN de toutes les cellules d'un enfant ou d'un adulte. Pour une maladie du foie, il faut cibler les cellules du foie, et pour une maladie du cerveau, celles du cerveau. Pour assurer ce transport, les scientifiques utilisent des virus désactivés et modifiés. Ici, le risque est que le virus provoque une réaction immunitaire et inflammatoire – la réaction classique d'un corps qui rencontre un virus.


Ces risques ne sont pas hypothétiques. Chaque cas tragique de la mort d'une personne lors d'un essai de thérapie génique est l'occasion de rappeler qu'elle n'est pas la première. Le cas de

Jesse Gelsinger

 en 1999 aux États-Unis est le plus connu. La mort de l'adolescent de 18 ans lors d'un des premiers essais de thérapie génique freine fortement les ardeurs ubuesques de la décennie du Projet Génome Humain. D'autant que les chercheurs ont fauté de manière grave en ne mentionnant pas, lors de la demande de consentement, des résultats inquiétants venant d'essais sur primates non-humains. Mais suite à l'essor de CRISPR, les essais cliniques se multiplient de nouveau. Et les drames aussi. Pour l'année 2025, deux autres

enfants

 sont morts dans des circonstances similaires en Chine, et au moins quatre aux États-Unis. Certes, il y a aussi des succès. Le plus récent, et le plus similaire au cas de Mei, étant celui de Baby KJ en 2025, né avec une maladie génétique rare, le déficit en CPS15, et traité aussi par une thérapie génique personnalisée. Mais ces succès ponctuels, dans des cas très particuliers, ne peuvent pas masquer la pauvreté des résultats de la recherche effrénée sur les thérapies géniques. Après plus de 35 ans de recherche et des millions, voire des milliards, d'euros dépensés, la première et unique thérapie génique officiellement approuvée comme traitement l'a été cette année, aux États-unis.


Le décès de Mei


Mei était atteinte du syndrome de Snijders Blok-Campeau, une maladie génétique extrêmement rare (237 cas recensés dans le monde) qui affecte les neurones. Le syndrome est à l'origine de

retards

 développementaux et de troubles cognitifs plus ou moins sévères …

author: Simon Childs
title: Labour Rehires Senior Rightwinger Whose Unit Bungled Antisemitism Complaints
content:
A Labour rightwinger who ran the party’s complaints department at the time it bungled numerous antisemitism complaints has been rehired to his previous job.


John Stolliday has been reinstated as head of Labour’s governance and legal unit (GLU) – the body responsible for dealing with complaints.


The role was advertised in the normal way; however, party general secretary Hollie Ridley –

a close ally of Keir Starmer

 – is understood to have made the appointment in what multiple sources told Novara Media is a factional move before her

departure from her role

, which will follow the party’s upcoming conference in Liverpool.


In a post on LinkedIn in July, Stolliday said: “Honoured and delighted to have been made executive director of governance and legal at the Labour party – the party I have worked at on and off for over 15 years since I started there in 2004 – and to lead the governance unit which I worked in for so many years.”


Stolliday was director of governance and legal from December 2016 to June 2018, a period in which Jeremy Corbyn was Labour leader and in which the party was mired in antisemitism allegations. The crisis would

dominate media coverage

 of Labour in the build up to the 2019 election and pave the way for Corbyn’s downfall. 


The crisis culminated in a report by the Equalities and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) which found that Labour had breached the Equality Act in two cases, and concluded that it could have dealt with antisemitism more effectively “if the leadership had chosen to do so”. The EHRC investigation did not make any findings against Stolliday.


Stolliday’s rehiring to his previous role astonished one source who previously worked within the party.


“The party seems to be ignoring that there’s inherent risk in rehiring someone who was a director at the time of the EHRC’s focus of investigation,” the source told Novara Media. 


“If you were making reasonable decisions and not evidently political ones, you wouldn’t in a million years rehire someone who is in control in a period of such failure.”


Following Stolliday’s departure from the role in 2018, a number of improvements were made to the complaints process. 


“After the amount of time and effort that we’d put into sorting things out, to hand the keys back to someone who crashed the car in the first place was pretty galling,” the source said.


Among the findings in the EHRC report was inadequate training for individuals dealing with antisemitism complaints, as well as “evidence of a significant number of complaints relating to antisemitism that were not investigated at all”. In particular, the party would routinely not investigate social media activity that involved “mere ‘likes’ or reposts”.


This policy led to some shocking examples of antisemitism not being dealt with, the source said. “Someone could share seven posts of Holocaust denial and if they didn’t add a remark saying, ‘I agree with this, this is great’, they [the GLU] would ignore it.”


“I know there was one instance of a person sharing virulent Holocaust denial – things like ‘Auschwitz had swimming pools, the six million [deaths] number is false’ – and they didn’t get suspended because they followed this policy of not taking action if someone hadn’t commented on it.”


Responding to the EHRC investigation at the time,

the party said

 the policy had been wrong and hadn’t been applied since mid 2018.


Leaked emails

 between Stolliday and another senior member of the GLU also showed that during this time, the party took over a year to suspend a member who had defended British fascists involved in the Battle of Cable Street in 1936, and eight months to suspend a council candidate who claimed the Holocaust was a “hoax”.


Stolliday’s previous tenure at Labour’s GLU came while he was part of the party’s “senior management team”, a group of

high-ranking officials

 who were bitterly opposed to Corbyn’s leadership.


A

leaked document

 produced during Corbyn’s leadership claimed that “an abnormal intensity of factional opposition to the party leader” had “inhibited the proper functioning of the Labour party bureaucracy” and contributed to “a litany of mistakes” in dealing with antisemitism.


The document became the subject of a legal case in which the claimants, including Stolliday, alleged it contained defamatory allegations. As it wasn’t possible to identify the source of the leak, the claim was pursued against Labour itself. The party settled out of …

author: dev
title: S'il-vous-plaît... dessine-moi un humain !
content:
9 septembre


Dépossédés de notre discernement


résolument tenus dans nos peurs distillées


solidement emmurés aux recoins amoindris de nos conforts


édifiés sur le colonialisme souverain


être sages, ordonnés et propres, chut... il ne faut pas déranger


pour finalement tout accepter


aujourd'hui un sommet international sur l'espace


conquête irresponsable, indésirable


pleurez pierrots, poètes et chats noirs


l'IA dans nos quotidiens de mises au travail et d'intimités


demain de plus grands centres de loisirs et d'attractions


des loups qu'on fusille sans limites


des incompétents aux postes clefs


et les chiens de garde


de la macronie au fascisme c'est tout cousu de fils barbelés


rouillés de surcroît


le tour de vis qui manquait au capitalisme


pour anéantir ce qui fait la vie


il n'y a pas autres à espérer ?


les ravages écologiques, les désastres humanitaires


l'essentiel de nos existences bafoué


les génocides et nos silences partisans


« ils » avancent assurés des cœurs malicieusement infectés


sur des savoirs démultipliés qui nous dépossèdent davantage


et cette fausse tranquillité quémandée aux marchands du temple


quel pacte mortifère avons donc nous signé ?


mais comment faisons-nous ?


S'il-vous-plaît... dessine-moi un humain !

 [

1

]


Au choeur de l'aube


la puissance de l'imaginaire, de la poésie et des solidarités inter-espèces donnent au réel une autre consistance, le silence et les mots s'étoffent et font de l'ombre aux calculs, aux prémices d'une façon de connaître englobant tout ce qui est autre.


Oust le superflu et les peurs assassinent, oust le travail vidé de sens et les factures emprisonnantes, oust la médiocrité et les sombres laboratoires, les images qui défilent sur les écrans et les paroles idiotes, oust... Sortons ! Embrassons nos fragilités, nos expériences communes et nos forces vives ! Que désirons-nous main-tenant ?


Entendons ce souffle qui se propage depuis les profondeurs du monde et nous fait frisonner, cet infime mouvement de notre émoi. Le vol en sarabande des étourneaux l'avait murmuré à nos yeux, nous sommes intotalisables, insaisissables. Nous sommes ensemble.


Stéphanie Chanvallon


[

1

]

« S'il vous plaît... dessine-moi un mouton » éveilla Antoine de Saint-Expéry égaré dans le désert. Il fit alors la rencontre du Petit Prince avant de s'essayer à des dessins.

author: dev
title: Prendre place, ouvrir l'espace, donner de la voix
content:
Elle prend place dans le fauteuil du présentateur télé. Elle s'assied, et plonge son regard bleu dans le cadran de la caméra. Elle nous regarde. Elle prend une grande inspiration, une deuxième, puis se lance dans la lecture du texte qu'elle a confié à la personne qui s'occupe du prompteur, juste avant l'émission. « Tu as pris une décision, cette fois-ci tu vas parler. » Et l'actrice de théâtre, en grève de l'industrie cinématographique, lentement, sans perdre des yeux sa cible télévisuelle, trace une ligne directe entre les violences qu'elle a subies toute enfant dans le milieu du cinéma et le génocide en cours en Palestine. Sa flèche relie deux vérités impossibles à entendre dans nos sociétés blanches, patriarcales et capitalistes : l'inceste comme fait social majeur ; la guerre génocidaire comme exercice normal du pouvoir colonial.


L'intervention de deux minutes est immédiatement retirée par France Télévision sur son site et devient impossible à revisionner. Sur la parole de l'actrice s'abat en un claquement de doigt la main de l'État. Censure.

Tu ne parleras pas

. Impossible à ouïr, que le massacre du « cosmos de l'enfance », décrit par Adèle Haenel, relève du même circuit pulsionnel que le massacre d'un peuple. La courroie libidinale et pseudo rationnelle qui vise à faire prendre l'agression pour de la séduction et le génocide pour de la légitime défense, est mise à nue en quelques mots, en deux minutes. La flèche est tirée et le récit majoritaire s'avoue comme tel en sortant tous ses boucliers : il n'y aura pas de réplique mais un couperet, pas de place pour l'improvisation, toute « carte blanche » ne sera jamais qu'un effet de discours, nullement une réalité. Si on refuse de s'habituer à la violence, si elle surprend toujours, on n'est finalement pas surprises : l'ordre se réaffirme et réenfonce sous la chappe de plomb la belle tête qui voulait en sortir.


Adèle Haenel était invitée à la télé à l'occasion de la sortie de

Viser juste

, son premier livre paru aux éditions de L'Arche, dans la collection « Des écrits pour la parole ». Rien n'est anodin ici, ni le titre de la collection où l'actrice choisit de publier sa voix, ni le choix de cette maison d'édition indépendante, essentiellement dédiée aux textes de théâtre, et maison historique des traductions françaises des pièces, journaux et poèmes de Bertolt Brecht, grand écrivain et penseur des liens entre le théâtre et la révolution.


Viser juste

 se présente sous la forme d'une enquête sur les modes de silenciation et d'invisibilisation de la parole d'une enfant victime d'abus sexuels dans le milieu du cinéma. Tout son effort consiste à démasquer la psyché du violeur, sorte de pointe aigüe de la psyché masculine majoritaire ; à montrer ce que c'est, un enfant détruit ; comment fonctionne le système d'impunité des agresseurs – dont l'autrice fait les frais dès les premiers mots autour de la parution de son livre, donc – ; comment il est possible d'en rire ; comment la joie et l'amour sont des puissances inouïes de reconstruction.


Le texte avance de manière chronologique. Il s'ouvre sur un plateau de théâtre où, lors d'une fête de fin d'année, une enfant fait l'expérience de sa nécessité de s'exprimer. Il se poursuit par la rencontre de cette enfant avec un réalisateur qui organise méticuleusement ses agressions sexuelles sur elle, ne connaissant nul frein car les parents se constituent complices par leur silence. Le texte ne nous lâche la main qu'une fois dessinée une possible reconstruction par l'amour et la philosophie, et l'horizon de désirabilité collectif dans lequel cette reconstruction s'inscrit.


Les scènes, autant de scripts pour un plateau (de théâtre ou de cinéma), sont entrecoupées de prises de parole à la première personne, dans lesquelles une narratrice commente ce qui vient d'être joué. Ces séquences réflexives empruntent à la philosophie et à la philosophie féministe en particulier, elles réaccordent ce qui est vécu par l'enfant à un espace et à une structure globales d'énonciation, de hiérarchie des vies et des imaginaires, elles remettent le sens d'aplomb, le langage sur son axe.


Viser juste

 est écrit en partenariat avec Gisèle Vienne, qui travaille depuis plus de 20 ans la question du langage, son émission et sa réception, notamment du point de vue des enfants et des adolescents. C'est dire que la parole portée par ce livre est une parole incarnée, une parole d'interprète, faite par et pour la scène, dont chaque mot est pensé …

author: Unknown
title: 257 people abducted in Syria since the beginning of 2026
content:
The Syrian Committees for the Defense of Democratic Freedoms and Human Rights issued a written statement on August 30, the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances.


The statement said that abductions and cases of enforced detention continue to be reported across Syria. It warned that the loss of contact with detainees and the lack of information about their whereabouts pose a serious threat to their lives.


According to the committees, 257 people have been documented as forcibly abducted since the start of the year. The statement also said that Israeli forces had abducted 52 people.


The committees called on all government-affiliated and non-governmental actors responsible for abductions to disclose the whereabouts and fate of those being held and to end practices that, they said, violate fundamental rights and freedoms.


They also called on the International Committee of the Red Cross and other relevant international organizations to secure access to detention facilities, investigate cases of enforced detention, and establish the fate and whereabouts of detainees and abducted persons.

author: Unknown
title: University student Necme Amini sentenced to death in Iran
content:
23-year-old university student Necme Amini has been sentenced to death in the Iranian city of Mashhad. The student, who was detained during protests in January 2026, announced in a voice message sent from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad that the verdict had been issued on 16 September.


The website “Voice of Iranian Prisoners” published Necme Amini’s voice message on 19 September. The student said that she had been sentenced to death after approximately eight months of uncertainty and called for a fair trial and the right to defend herself.


In her message, Amini appealed to lawyers, legal experts, human rights activists and international organizations, asking them to investigate and follow up on her case.


Previously sentenced to 12 years and 6 months in prison


Branch 1 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court had sentenced Necme Amini to 12 years, 6 months and 1 day in prison on charges of “insulting the Prophet.”


According to reports, the student was detained on 28 February 2026, at Ferdowsi Bazaar in Mashhad and taken to Vakilabad Prison. Sources said that she was denied the right to meet with a lawyer of her own choosing during her detention.


Information regarding Amini's case and the death sentence handed down against her has not yet been confirmed by Iran’s official judicial authorities.


Beyan Qaderî detained in Piranshahr


Thirty-eight-year-old Beyan Qaderî, who lives in the Pasveh district of Piranshar, was also detained on 19 September after going to a security agency. According to human rights sources, Qaderî was transferred to Urmia following her detention and is being held at a detention center belonging to Iranian security forces. However, her exact location is unknown.


Family home searched


It was reported that Iranian security forces searched Beyan Qaderî’s family home one day before her detention. The security forces also reportedly detained and interrogated Qaderî’s elderly father for several hours.


Following her father’s release, Beyan Qaderî was reportedly instructed to go to a security agency and identify herself. She went to the agency as instructed and was subsequently detained. No information has yet been released regarding the charges brought against her.

author: Unknown
title: Karagöz: Prisoners want the process to move forward
content:
Nearly two years into the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began with Abdullah Öcalan’s call, debate continues over steps to implement the framework law and the situation of political prisoners.


Nearly a month has passed since the legislation, adopted by Parliament with the votes of 470 MPs and widely known as the “framework law,” came into force. The Freedom Movement described the law as inadequate but nevertheless regarded it as a step. However, delays in taking concrete steps to implement the law are increasing concerns among prisoners and their families about the process.


Expectations for steps regarding the situation of political prisoners continue, while rights violations, decisions by the Administrative and Observation Boards, and postponements of release also remain on the agenda.


Nurten Karagöz, Co-Chair of the Marmara Association for Solidarity and Assistance with Families of Prisoners and Convicts (MATUHAY-DER), spoke to ANF about developments in prisons over the month since the framework law came into force and the approach of prisoners’ families to the process.


Prolonging the process is causing distrust among prisoners’ families


Nurten Karagöz said families expect the requirements of the law to be fulfilled: “Of course, what I am saying does not reflect only my own views; the feedback we receive from families is also along these lines. We are an association that works in solidarity with prisoners’ families. Naturally, we are in very close contact with them; we meet and visit one another regularly. What they are saying is this: while they had expected their children to regain their freedom, the fact that the process has dragged on for so long is creating serious distrust among them as well.


The families’ demand at this point is clear: if a law has been passed, the state should stand behind it and fulfil its requirements. It should do so as soon as possible so that families can be reunited with their children and this deadlock can genuinely be overcome. There is a deadlock, or at least a situation in which things are moving too slowly, and families say this needs to be overcome as soon as possible.”


Prisoners want the way opened for the process


Nurten Karagöz said prisoners do not view the issue solely in terms of their own release, but want the way to be opened for the process. Karagöz also said: “Let me put it this way: prisoners were, of course, expecting their friends to be released with this law. But they are not at the point of saying, ‘We expected releases, but even if that does not happen, we are fed up now, just let us out.’ As I mentioned earlier, their demands are also focused on opening the way for the process. Of course, delays in this process are creating a heavy psychological burden both on prisoners and their families.


On the other hand, we see that instead of unlawful practices in prisons decreasing with this process, they have actually begun to increase. Postponements of release, arbitrary practices and torture have become increasingly widespread. This leads us to the conclusion that each prison has effectively created its own set of rules and is applying them. Yet there should, of course, be one law applicable throughout this country. This is precisely what we mean by arbitrary practices.


Unfortunately, Administrative and Observation Boards still exist in prisons. As we have said many times before, these are bodies with no real legal validity, and the entire issue has been left to their discretion. On the one hand, the state says society should live together and be built on a sense of fraternity; on the other, it unfortunately continues torture, unlawful practices and postponements of release in prisons, while expecting society not to react as though this were somehow part of democratization. That is simply not possible. A democratic society, and every institution and individual struggling for it, must of course respond to this, and such a response is entirely natural.”


We are ready to support prisoners and families when releases begin


Nurten Karagöz said they are preparing for possible releases as the process moves forward and added: “We are an association for solidarity and assistance with the families of prisoners and convicts. If releases begin, and we hope and wish they begin as soon as possible, we are prepared. As an association, we have made our preparations and are ready to welcome every one of our friends who is released. We have also made …

author: Unknown
title: Defending Kurdistan under fire
content:
The Middle East is passing through a ring of fire in which conflict, political crisis and economic devastation caused by the Third World War are intertwined. At every stage in which the war expands or contracts, basic conditions for survival such as security, shelter and food are turning into areas of severe crisis. The security of existence of the peoples of the region, particularly the Kurds, is coming under increasing threat.


Attacks carried out by states and non-state actors are deepening the security crisis in the Middle East, while the devastation caused by war is driving millions of people into refugee camps, amid ruins or onto migration routes. Conflicts over water, energy and trade routes, along with the disruption of supply chains caused by capitalist plunder and war, are further deepening the economic crisis.


New hegemonic ambitions in the region by the nation-state centres that divided Kurdistan are making this picture even more complex and dangerous. At a time when efforts are underway to reshape the balance of power in the Middle East and Kurdistan has become one of the key arenas of regional power struggles, the long-standing political governance crisis in Southern Kurdistan (Başur) and the failure to form a government are converging with new risks.


Crisis of status and existence in Southern Kurdistan


For Southern Kurdistan, the central issue is not merely the formation of a government and the appointment of ministers to the 10th Cabinet. There is a need for a new strategic assessment suited to the changing political and security balance, an analysis of the risks, and a comprehensive programme capable of responding to them.


Southern Kurdistan is entering a period in which the security architecture that emerged after the 1991 Gulf War and the federal status guaranteed by the 2005 Iraqi Constitution are undergoing a serious rupture.


Preparations by the US-led international coalition forces to end their military mission in Iraq are one of the most significant elements of this transformation. As 30 September approaches, the future of non-state armed forces in Iraq, the consolidation of weapons under state authority, and the approach of Iran-aligned groups to this process are among the main issues under discussion.


The withdrawal of the coalition, along with the removal of air defence systems such as Patriot batteries and C-RAM systems deployed particularly in and around Erbil (Hewlêr), is also creating a new situation for Southern Kurdistan’s capacity to defend itself against external attacks.


A 35-year security architecture is coming to an end


The period that began with the declaration of the no-fly zone in April 1991 and continued in subsequent years under the security umbrella of US-led forces played a decisive role in Southern Kurdistan’s strategic position. However, this security architecture of roughly 35 years is entering a new phase with the withdrawal of coalition forces from Iraq.


This transformation is not limited to the military sphere. The constitutional, financial and security powers of the Kurdistan Regional Government have also become increasingly contested in recent years through decisions made in Baghdad and a series of rulings by the Federal Supreme Court.


The effective narrowing of Southern Kurdistan’s administrative, financial and security powers, granted under the federal status established by the 2005 Iraqi Constitution, points to a process of increasing the region’s dependence on Baghdad. Disputes over the budget, oil revenues and security are among the central issues driving these tensions.


Pêşmerge forces and the security question


The four-year Memorandum of Understanding renewed in 2022 between the US Department of Defense and the Kurdistan Region’s Ministry of Pêşmerge Affairs is due to expire on 30 September 2026, making it another important element of this transformation. With the coalition’s withdrawal, the future of funding, training and military equipment support mechanisms for the Pêşmerge forces is also being reshaped.


At the same time, the division of the Pêşmerge forces along the lines of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) has long been a subject of debate regarding Southern Kurdistan’s collective defence capacity. As discussions in Iraq over bringing weapons under state authority extend to the Pêşmerge forces, the future of this structure is becoming even more significant at a time when external …

title: Two PKK guerrillas, whose remains were relocated from Garzan to Kilyos, identified after nine years
content:
The identities of PKK guerrillas Zehra Kısaoğlu (Raperin) and Süheyla Kaya (Zilan), whose remains were exhumed from Garzan Cemetery in Bitlis and later buried beneath a pavement at Kilyos Cemetery in Istanbul, have been confirmed through DNA matches with samples taken from their families.


The families of Zehra Kısaoğlu and Süheyla Kaya, who died in 1999, were informed on September 17 that the DNA samples had matched. The families then applied to the Zincirlikuyu Cemeteries Directorate in Istanbul before proceeding to Kilyos Cemetery.


According to Zehra Kısaoğlu’s brother, Abdullah Kısaoğlu, his sister left home after completing high school. The family provided DNA samples at various mass grave sites over the years. Kısaoğlu said they learned four days ago that his sister’s remains were in Kilyos.


The remains are expected to be collected from Kilyos Cemetery today and taken to the Karlıova district of Bingöl.


What happened at Garzan Cemetery?


In December 2017, the Turkish state ordered the destruction of the Garzan Cemetery of Martyrs in the province of Bitlis in North Kurdistan. The cemetery is located near the village of Oleka Jor (Upper Ölek), where hundreds of members of the Kurdish guerrilla organisations HPG and YJA-Star and the YPG and YPJ were buried. Their bodies were exhumed after the destruction of the cemetery on the order of the Istanbul public prosecutor's office and taken to the local forensic department. They were then buried in the Jewish cemetery of Kilyos not far from the seaside resort of the same name at the European entrance to the Bosporus. The remains of Kurdish fighters were buried in a section for “the nameless”.


Until now, it was assumed that the bodies of 267 fallen fighters buried in Garzan were exhumed by Turkish security forces and taken to Istanbul. According to research by the Mezopotamya news agency (MA), the bodies turned out to be the remains of 282 people. Only 21 bodies were subsequently handed over to relatives. The bodies of 261 dead are still buried in Kilyos. However, not in regular graves, but packed in plastic boxes and stacked on top of each other under a pavement.


Case taken to ECtHR


In 2022, the Istanbul Branch of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) took the case to the European Court of Human Right (ECtHR).


The families had previously filed a criminal complaint with the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office through their lawyers on charges of "insulting the memory of the dead" and "torture and persecution", but the prosecutor's office did not give permission to launch an investigation. The application made to the Turkish Constitutional Court (AYM) yielded no results, either.


After the AYM's refusal, the ÖHD lawyers have taken the case to the ECtHR on behalf of the families following the exhaustion of domestic remedies. The lawyers cited Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR) which provides “a right to respect for one's private and family life, his home and his correspondence.” The lawyers also accused Turkish authorities of not conducting an effective investigation.

author: Dan DiMaggio
title: Video Game Workers Win First Contract at Microsoft-Owned Blizzard
content:
Workers who make some of the world’s most popular video games, including World of Warcraft and Diablo, won their first union contracts in early September, in an important step forward for organizing in the tech industry.


The 1,900 workers are employed by Blizzard, which was acquired by Microsoft in 2023 in the largest deal ever in the video game industry.


Their new Communications Workers (CWA) contracts include recall rights and guaranteed severance packages for laid-off workers—significant wins, since tech and video game workers have seen waves of layoffs in the last few years.


Workers on various Activision Blizzard teams have voted to join CWA since 2022. It started with quality assurance testers at Raven Software—when Raven abruptly laid off a dozen testers in December 2021, they went on strike and launched a union drive.


Soon after the Raven workers voted the union in,

Microsoft signed a neutrality agreement with CWA

, pledging to remain neutral in organizing campaigns and to allow workers and union representatives to communicate openly. In exchange, the union agreed to support the software giant’s purchase of Activision Blizzard, which was facing antitrust scrutiny.


Activision Blizzard had also faced employee walkouts and a lawsuit by the California Civil Rights Department in 2021 over claims of misconduct and discrimination against women and a “frat boy” company culture.


Next to unionize were quality assurance testers at Blizzard’s offices in Albany, New York, and Austin, Texas. A wall-to-wall unit of 500 World of Warcraft workers unionized in 2024, followed by units of 200 game developers at Overwatch, 160 members of Blizzard’s story and franchise team, and 450 Diablo designers, engineers, artists, and support staff in 2025.


RECALL RIGHTS


Blizzard workers won the right to be recalled for 14 months after being laid off. This right extends to any open positions they are qualified for across the 1,900-worker Blizzard bargaining units. The contracts have separate expiration dates but the same terms across all these units. (The Raven workers, who are part of Activision, already bargained a separate contract.)


“We know we are at the start of a labor movement in video games and tech at large,” said Mahreen Fatima, a senior environment artist on Diablo. “So it weighed heavily on us to make sure we set a strong precedent.”


CWA has organized 4,000 video game workers at Microsoft, and has another 550 members in its

industry-wide United Video Game Workers affiliate

. The latter is a pre-majority union: it allows video game workers to directly join before winning a union election, a model CWA has employed in organizing public sector and higher education workers in Southern states. Another 100 game developers behind Magic: The Gathering Arena

voted to join CWA in June

.


In

a survey of U.S. video game workers by the Game Developers Conference

 early this year, 82 percent of respondents supported unionizing. Organizers hope that the protections and job security provisions won at Blizzard will convince more game workers to organize.


At Blizzard, laid-off workers will get a minimum of four weeks’ severance plus an additional week for every six months’ tenure, up to 39 weeks. The contract also includes just cause protections, a grievance procedure, and a three-day in-office hybrid workweek. And the union fought hard to put other existing benefits and policies in writing, from weather-related policies to money Blizzard workers are given to spend on the company’s games—all now enforceable through the contract.


Blizzard workers also won language that requires the company to discuss, evaluate, and bargain over the impact of artificial intelligence on their work. “Now we have a seat at the table to be part of the conversation when it comes to A.I. implementation,” said Fatima. “The contract gives us the ability to critically think about how it’s going to impact our workflow, our skill sets, the quality of our product, our teams.”


The union won a guarantee that existing remote workers, like Fatima, can continue working remotely, which prevents them from being forced to potentially move across the country to keep their job. Remote workers make up around one-fourth of the workforce covered under the new contract.


The contract also includes protections against outsourcing—a Blizzard worker can't be laid off unless the company has let go any contractor hired in the last year doing a similar job, and …

author: dev
title: Économie politique d'un jeune artistauteur d'aujourd'hui #2
content:
Ça commence par un été de canadairs. Y'a des feux un peu partout. On peut les voir sur différentes cartes interactives en ligne. On peut les voir au loin, parfois. On peut voir la fumée. Quelqu'un peut dire : tiens, ça brûle encore. Ça brûle encore.


J'entends la phrase à voix haute et je repense au magnifique livre de Sol Netra,

Au-delà du feu

, que j'ai lu avant l'été, et notamment à ce passage où quelqu'un s'adresse directement à lae narrateur

·

ice, pour qui la scarification représente parfois comme une libération du feu intérieur — à travers les veines, le sang chaud, la colère et la tristesse, et les cicatrices en mémoire. «

Soudain, quelqu'un se penche sur moi, caresse mon bras et ces mots viennent : “C'est joli, c'est fait exprès ? On dirait un petit feu.” Je porte en moi le feu.

 »


Je pense : on ne voit pas la fumée s'échapper de tous les gens qui souffrent et qui brûlent en cachette.


Je pense aussi : il y a eu d'autres feux, cet été — on parle aussi de

départs de feux

. J'ai lu des livres, je veux en rendre compte, mais avant ça, je veux parler de ces quelques départs de feux multiples. Comme si j'avais réalisé récemment que les choses de la vie se

chevauchaient

, finalement, plus qu'elles ne pouvaient s'additionner ou se suivre tels les évènements sur une frise chronologique.


*


Dans

un article précédent publié sur lundimatin

, j'écrivais ce paragraphe, au conditionnel.


Imaginons. Une petite maison d'édition indépendante apprendrait que son distributeur est en cessation de paiements et s'apprête à faire faillite — conséquence, entre autres, du placement en redressement judiciaire de plusieurs grandes librairies clientes (Gibert Joseph en avril 2026, le Furet du Nord et Decitre en mai 2026) qui lui devaient des sommes importantes. Ce seraient des dizaines de milliers d'euros de créances irrécouvrables pour cette maison d'édition — une part significative d'un chiffre d'affaires annuel. Les droits d'auteur

·

ices seraient suspendus, les impressions décalées, les sorties plus qu'incertaines. Et ce ne serait pas un accident isolé. Ce serait l'effet de ce que décrit depuis des années Thierry Discepolo : un marché du livre structurellement verrouillé, où les indépendants naviguent à flux tendu, sans filet, dans un écosystème dont les grands groupes contrôlent non seulement l'édition mais la diffusion et la distribution — autant dire les conditions mêmes de survie de ceux qui tentent de faire autrement. (Imaginons, une minute.)


Quelques jours après la parution de cet article, de nombreuses maisons d'édition indépendantes (dont Blast, la maison qui a publié mes romans, ma maison, ma

house

) ont communiqué sur leur situation : Makassar, leur distributeur commun, était en faillite — entraînant dans sa chute des dizaines de maisons qui lui confiaient la gestion de leurs commandes, de leur stock, de leur facturation. Des cagnottes ont été lancées. Des communiqués publiés. Le paragraphe avait été écrit au conditionnel parce qu'il me semblait que ce n'était pas à moi de parler de cette situation en premier, que les maisons d'édition, en première ligne, devaient pouvoir le faire elles-mêmes, à leur rythme. La situation n'était pas hypothétique : il s'agissait déjà bien de la réalité.


La rédaction de lundimatin, après avoir reçu mon article et l'avoir publié, m'écrit : « […] Sinon pour l'anecdote du monde du livre, notre distributeur est en train de faire faillite avec tout notre fric et celui de la moitié de l'édition indépendante. Les temps qui viennent s'annoncent intéressants pour ceux qui ne seront pas engloutis. »


Entre-temps, une cinquantaine de maisons d'édition indépendantes — Blast, lundimatin, La Dispute, Trou Noir, Remue-ménage, La Variation, et bien d'autres — se sont regroupées sur le site

sauvonslesindes.fr

 pour appeler à un soutien massif : acheter leurs livres directement sur leurs boutiques, faire des tables en librairies, donner sur les cagnottes de celles qui en ont lancé une.


*


Premier chevauchement.


Pour reprendre les mots de Gramsci, j'ai envie de dire qu'il faudrait s'atteler urgemment à rendre les gouvernés intellectuellement indépendants des gouverneurs. Si les concentrations se multiplient, Boldurée en tête, il faut jeter un œil aussi du côté des élus qui déprogramment et des coupes budgétaires de plus en plus drastiques et ciblées.


Souvent, quand on parle de l'actualité récente, ma mère finit toujours par dire que le fascisme s'attaque toujours et …

Dossier

Die Teamsters Local 362 beantragte eine Abstimmung über die gewerkschaftliche Vertretung im Amazon YEG 1 Fulfillment Centre in Nisku, AB. Ob es um Arbeitsplatzsicherheit, Arbeitstempo, Diskriminierung, Günstlingswirtschaft oder Löhne geht, das Unternehmen hat bewiesen, dass es zutiefst arbeitnehmerfeindlich ist. (…)

Das Alberta Labour Relations Board (ALRB) muss den Antrag zunächst prüfen. Sobald dies geschehen ist, werden alle Amazon-Beschäftigten in YEG 1, die seit gestern angestellt sind, die Möglichkeit haben, über die Vertretung durch die Teamsters Local Union 362 abzustimmen

…“ So beginnt die engl.

Mitteilung vom 14. September 2021 bei Teamster Canada

Angesichts des Drucks durch den ersten Tarifvertrag, der den Beschäftigten am Standort YVR2 in Delta (British Columbia) in Kürze gewährt werden soll, hat Amazon eine plötzliche Lohnerhöhung für alle seine kanadischen Standorte angekündigt – ähnlich wie Walmart im Jahr 2024.

Meldung vom 16. September 2026 bei der Gewerkschaft Unifor

:


Die Amazon-Lagerarbeiter:innen in Delta/Kanada haben nach Urteil der Arbeitsbehörde der Provinz über Einmischung des Unternehmens die gewerkschaftliche Zulassung durch Unifor erhalten


„

Die Amazon-Lagerarbeiter in Delta, British Columbia, haben eine gewerkschaftliche Zulassung erhalten, nachdem die

Arbeitsbehörde


 der Provinz

sich auf die Seite von Unifor gestellt


 hat und feststellte, dass das Unternehmen in den Gewerkschaftsbildungsprozess eingegriffen hat. Diese bahnbrechende Entscheidung sichert nicht nur die gewerkschaftliche Vertretung der Beschäftigten in Kanada, sondern könnte auch die Organisierungsbemühungen in Amazon-Standorten auf der ganzen Welt beeinflussen.

title: Akbay: The fundamental task of the youth is to convey the new paradigm to society
content:
ANF spoke with Ibrahim Akbay, a member of the Youth Assembly of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), about the role of youth in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the obstacles encountered during the process, and ideological transformation.


What is the fundamental role assumed by young people in the Peace and Democratic Society Process?


As the constitutive and leading force of society, young people face a historical responsibility in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Today, it is not possible to limit the role of youth merely to carrying out existing party activities or routine youth organizing. In this period, when the construction of a democratic society, democratic nation, and communes is at the center, the practical leading role of youth is intertwined with ideological leadership.


The greatest responsibility for enabling society to understand the values being defended, the struggle being waged, and the life being envisioned falls to the youth, young women, and the women’s movement. Youth continue to occupy the position of being the leading dynamic of society, both specifically in this historical process and independently of the process in every period.


Alongside positive expectations regarding the process, there are also a number of practices that do not conform to the principles and fundamentals of the Peace and Democratic Society Process. How do you assess this situation?


After a struggle lasting nearly 50 years, practices that do not accord with the spirit of peace and a democratic society continue to exist in the process entered through the steps taken by Abdullah Öcalan. The failure to implement the “Right to Hope,” the continuation of the trustee regime, elected politicians being kept in prison, ecological destruction, and repression and detentions targeting young people stand out as the most prominent obstacles to the process.


Even if the process results in political normalization, social and political struggle will continue by taking on a new dimension. Although an end to armed conflict may be achieved, it is clear that the state has not abandoned its special war policies or its culture of impunity. We need to look not only at today but also at yesterday. For example, Selçuk Mızraklı was released after seven years, simply because he represented the political will of the Kurdish people. There are many other elected officials who remain imprisoned.


Keeping figures who represent the political will of the people in prison for years demonstrates that the political sphere has still not been opened to the Kurds. We are confronted with a state reality that has not confronted unsolved murders, massacres, and villages that were burned. While the Saturday Mothers have been searching for the remains of their children for 30 years, I do not believe it is possible to build a lasting peace without prosecuting those responsible and conducting a genuine reckoning with the past.


What concrete steps need to be taken for peace to become socially rooted and for the process to move forward?


The Kurdish Freedom Movement clearly demonstrates that it will not remain in the position of a passive petitioner and that it will build its own social model independently of the state’s position. For example, there is a demand for Kurdish to be a language of education in the mother tongue and an official language; but there is also a perspective of organizing its own Kurdish-language education initiatives and perhaps developing an educational model. There is a demand for local democracy and status; but at the same time, there is a paradigm of building communes and creating a commune of communes throughout Kurdistan.


For the process to succeed and for peace to become socially rooted, the way must be opened for political participation. In addition, Kurds must be included as founding partners in the democratic structure to be established; this is possible through constitutional guarantees, recognition of Kurdish law, and the restoration of all democratic rights that are inherent from birth. Furthermore, the ongoing ecological destruction in Kurdistan must be brought to an end as soon as possible, and the Kurdish people must have rights over their own resources.


On the other hand, the framework law passed by Parliament is, in its current form, of course inadequate. The law still defines the PKK as a “terrorist organization” and excludes prisoners serving aggravated life sentences …

title: 10th Diyarbakır Book Fair to kick off this weekend
content:
The Diyarbakır (Amed) Book Fair will start on Saturday 26 September. Prominent figures from the world of literature and publishing will celebrate the 10th year of the fair. Organized by Tüyap Fairs in cooperation with the Turkish Publishers Association and with the support of the Diyarbakır Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the fair will welcome visitors for nine days at the Mesopotamia International Fair and Congress Centre until 4 October 2026.


Yeni Özgür Politika wrote that the Diyarbakır Book Fair will bring together 125 publishing houses and civil society organizations, and will host a rich cultural programme over nine days. Alongside panels, talks and workshops, the fair will feature activities for children, while hundreds of authors will meet readers at book-signing events. Offering book lovers of different age groups an experience centred on books and literature, the fair will also contribute to the social and cultural life of Diyarbakır and the surrounding region.


73 events


The 10th Diyarbakır Book Fair will host 73 events over nine days, bringing together book lovers with figures from the worlds of literature, culture and art. In addition to talks and panels, the programme will feature theatre performances, music and poetry recitals, and workshops covering literature, history, culture, art, education and social issues. Writers, academics, artists and guests from various fields will take part, while activities for children and young people will appeal to book lovers of different age groups.


Exhibition


Around 30 works will be presented in an exhibition curated by painter and educator Mehmet Altuntaş. Featuring portraits of writers and poets from Diyarbakır alongside works inspired by the city’s historical and natural beauty, the exhibition will create a connection between books and visual arts, offering children and young people in particular a different artistic experience.


The fair will also host the exhibition “What Is Amida Telling Us?” Featuring photographs taken in 1910 and included in the book Amida, the exhibition will be presented to visitors.

title: Asrın Law Office responds to campaign against Öcalan: “The question of status is important”
content:
The Asrın Law Office has strongly responded to the latest campaigns targeting Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan. It said that various circles were attempting to detach the Kurdish question from its historical and political context and reduce the Peace and Democratic Society Process to a sensationalist tabloid debate.


“We are aware that this mentality, which seeks to obscure the historical and political significance of the Kurdish question and reduce the ongoing process to cheap tabloid topics, knows no moral boundaries. These statements reflect an attitude aimed at obstructing society’s pursuit of peace and democracy, as well as discomfort with the prospect of conflict and violence coming to an end.”


According to the Asrın Law Office, which represents Öcalan and his fellow prisoners on the prison island of Imrali, there is currently an opportunity to move the Kurdish question, which has existed for around two centuries, beyond the logic of conflict and violence and address it at the political and legal level. Öcalan, it said, is focusing his efforts on transforming this opportunity into lasting peace and a democratic solution.


“The clearest expression of profiting from blood”


Asrın responded particularly sharply to statements contrasting Öcalan’s conditions on Imrali with the impoverished housing conditions of the families of Turkish soldiers who were killed: “Those who stir up nationalist sentiment over ‘unplastered houses’ without giving up any of their own comforts expect the people living in those houses to pay the price once again. This is the clearest expression of profiting from blood.” According to Asrin, the circles in question assume that society in Turkey can be “easily manipulated with a few slogans, distorted information, and provocative statements.”


Asrın also addressed misogynistic attacks against Öcalan: “Those who speak about Mr. Öcalan, who in a region such as the Middle East views women’s freedom as a fundamental component of social freedom through the philosophy of ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ [Woman, Life, Freedom] and has built a struggle on this basis, should at least be expected to possess a certain degree of knowledge and judgment. However, this could not be expected from a mentality that“goes from door to door checking on refugees, fuels xenophobia, and is racist and misogynistic.”


Debate over accommodation on Imrali


The law office described the discussion surrounding an “accommodation facility” on Imrali as another area of manipulation. “This structure arose from a requirement stemming from processes of conflict resolution and is necessary to enable the political and legal work of the process to move forward.” The conditions provided, it said, still fall short of comparable international examples.


“Undoubtedly, the denial imposed on the Kurds for a century, the image of Öcalan constructed by the state over the past 50 years, and the Imrali regime practiced for the past 27 years have given these circles the freedom to act with such impunity. For decades, the struggle of the Kurds for their rights has also been targeted through attacks on Öcalan. We reject such attempts, which violate Öcalan’s personal rights, demean the Kurdish people through him, attack their dignity, and reflect a racist and colonial perspective.”


“That is precisely why the question of status is important”


The demand for a status for Öcalan occupies a central place in the statement published on Monday: “That is precisely why the discussion about status is important and valuable. The necessary conditions must be created for Mr. Öcalan, who has been deprived to such an extent of the means to express and defend himself, so that he can show the way toward peace.” The law office directly defines what it means by this demand: “The demand for status is a demand to create the conditions necessary for everything society needs to know to be explained transparently, firsthand, and directly by the person concerned.” In this way, the Asron Law Office explicitly links the question of status to Öcalan’s ability to publicly address the ongoing process himself.


"Criticism must take place on a minimum moral and humane foundation"


Asrın Law Office also criticized the judiciary for frequently ignoring racist and hateful statements against Kurds, as well as similar attacks targeting Öcalan. It said it would continue to pursue legal action against such statements. The law office explicitly distinguished these from political …

title: Patrichor: We will hold those who damaged the mass graves in Shengal accountable
content:
In Shengal, Iraqi forensic experts have begun work to open a burial site containing the remains of victims of the ISIS genocide. According to Iraqi authorities, the remains of 76 people are believed to be buried in the area.


The remains were recovered from mass graves discovered in the Xanesor (Khanasor) area after Shengal was liberated from the “Islamic State” (ISIS). In 2016, KDP authorities in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq had the remains exhumed and subsequently reburied in the Şerfedîn area, even though the necessary DNA testing had not yet been completed.


Relatives who still had no certainty about the fate of their missing family members subsequently called for the burial site to be reopened. After years of efforts, Iraq’s Directorate for Mass Graves and Missing Persons and the forensic authorities began the exhumation work.


The bones now being recovered will be taken for forensic examination. DNA samples will be collected and compared with those of relatives in order to identify the victims.


Xêrî Elî, head of the Petricor Human Rights Organization, spoke to ANF about the opening of the mass grave in Şerfedîn area.


After three years of work, efforts began to open the mass grave located between Xanesor (Khanasor) and Sinûnê. Xêrî Elî said that the Petricor Human Rights Organization had examined numerous mass grave cases, but this particular case was regarded as the most difficult due to outside interference, particularly by the KDP.


Xêrî Elî stated: “The families who lost their loved ones and faced great difficulties throughout the process leading up to the opening of the mass grave have spent 12 years not knowing whether their loved ones were held in prisons or buried in mass graves. With the opening of this mass grave, everyone will be able to learn the fate of their relatives and finally obtain answers.”


Emphasizing that their work would not be limited to the process of opening the mass graves, Xêrî Elî said they would also continue their efforts to ensure that those who damaged or interfered with the graves are brought to justice. He pointed out that the fate of the 67 people buried in the mass grave had remained unknown since 2015.


Xêrî Elî stated that some parties that established themselves in Shengal while leaving the population defenseless had damaged numerous mass graves. Some graves, he said, were opened without authorization before the necessary legal procedures were completed, and others were damaged by fire. As a result of this negligence, some bones were swept away by floodwaters while others were carried off by animals, he added.


Xêrî Elî noted that all these violations had been fully documented and that detailed reports would be prepared and submitted to the relevant authorities.
