title: Musa Anter commemorated on the 34th anniversary of his murder in Amed
content:
Kurdish writer and journalist Musa Anter was commemorated in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) on Sunday. The commemoration took place at the site in the Seyrantepe district where the intellectual, known as Apê (Uncle) Musa, was shot dead on September 20, 1992. The memorial event, organized by the Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG), was attended by Anter’s relatives, media workers, and representatives of political parties and civil society organizations.


Anter’s murder is among the most widely known political crimes of the 1990s. The Susurluk Report, later prepared on behalf of the Turkish prime minister, contained extensive information about the activities of state-backed structures and linked Anter’s murder to Mahmut Yıldırım, alias “Yeşil,” and the military intelligence organization JITEM. A full judicial reckoning with the case has yet to take place.


“For peace, the political murders must be solved”


DFG member Fexredin Kılıç stated that even 34 years after Anter’s death, the structures behind the murder have still not been fully exposed. Referring to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, he called for the political murders of the 1990s to be investigated. “In these days when we are talking about peace, we say it once again at the place where Apê Musa was murdered: For there to be peace, the unresolved political murders must be solved.”


Anter’s murder, he said, was not directed solely against a journalist but against bringing the social reality of the Kurdish people to the public. Even after his death, Kılıç noted, members of the free Kurdish press were killed, imprisoned, detained, and threatened; newsrooms were bombed and media outlets banned. In this context, Kılıç commemorated the slain journalists Nagihan Akarsel, Gulistan Tara, Cihan Bilgin, and Nazım Daştan, saying: “The free press has not bowed down and will not bow down. We will continue to write the truth, defend the truth, and carry the voices of the peoples to the world.”


From Apê Musa to Hüseyin Aykol


DFG Co-Chair Selman Çiçek commemorated journalist Hüseyin Aykol, a longtime companion of the Kurdish press, who died on January 1 this year. Despite his age and health problems, Çiçek said, Aykol regularly attended the commemoration in recent years. “Perhaps we did not have the chance to know Apê Musa ourselves. But today we are here as students of Hüseyin, who was shaped by Apê Musa. We learned a great deal from Hüseyin. From Apê Musa to Hüseyin, from Hüseyin to us, and from us to the next generations, we will carry this tradition forward.”


Musa Anter’s son, Dicle Anter, pledged to continue keeping his father’s memory alive at the site where he was killed: “Thirty-four years have passed since Apê Musa was murdered. But we will come here every year and commemorate him.”


Mızraklı: Truth and accountability are indispensable


Former Amed Co-Mayor Adnan Selçuk Mızraklı recalled that Anter’s significance extended far beyond his role as a pioneer of the Kurdish press. “Apê Musa was not only a founding figure and guiding force of the Kurdish press. He left behind a great legacy for all Kurds and all people.” Mızraklı pointed to the many young journalists who continue Anter’s work today. At the same time, he linked Anter’s legacy to the issue of confronting and addressing state crimes.


“Especially in the context of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, uncovering the truth and confronting it are indispensable if peace is to be deepened and a dignified peace established. If those who murdered Apê Musa are still walking free somewhere today, then justice remains incomplete. Without justice, there can be no genuine peace.”


“Today there are thousands of Musa Anters”


Mızraklı also recalled a meeting of the Human Rights Association (IHD) in the early 1990s, where politician Vedat Aydın, who was also killed by JITEM in 1991, delivered a speech in Kurdish. Musa Anter had been sitting behind him. “I remember Apê Musa’s proud stance during that speech—a stance that said: We exist through our language, our culture, and what we have created.” Today, he said, this legacy has long since been embraced by a new generation: “Today there are thousands of Musa Anters. We have thousands of young people who write fearlessly with the pen he left behind and pick up their cameras even in the most difficult moments.”


The necessary process of reckoning, he added, extends far beyond Anter’s murder. Mızraklı drew a line from the state crimes of the 1990s …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Estados Unidos: la centralidad de la tasa de interés
content:
La incertidumbre domina el escenario, nadie sabe cuándo terminará la guerra ya perdida, ¿la suba de la tasa de interés devendrá en una crisis económica o será expresión de que la economía irá al alza?


El presidente de la Reserva Federal, Jerome Powell. Foto: Anna Moneymaker, Getty Images


Finalmente la Reserva Federal de EEUU resolvió subir la tasa de interés de referencia, algo que no sucedía desde 2023. Desoye así las exigencias de Donald Trump que pedía bajarlas. Es una expresión de las complejidades económicas que atraviesa el imperio estadounidense. Complica la toma de deuda en nuestro país.


En una entrega anterior me preguntaba si la Reserva Federal subiría las tasas de referencia, cuando Trump presionaba para que las baje y así estimular el crecimiento económico, la incógnita se reveló este miércoles. La FED (el banco central estadounidense) resolvió por unanimidad una suba de 25 puntos básicos llevándola al rango de 3.75 – 4.0, con lo que afirma una política monetaria más restrictiva, que según el comunicado oficial sería duradera. Hasta ahora la tasa se encontraba en un rango de 3,50% a 3,75% y no se movía desde hace tres años. Sin embargo en las proyecciones de la FED esta decisión no afectaría las tasas de empleo ni del crecimiento del PBI.


Para varios analistas el aumento de las tasas de interés, que es un fenómeno global que está afectando a casi todos los países, tiene que ver con el aumento de la inflación mundial, las necesidades de endeudamiento (que compiten con el aumento de la inversión del capital privado en IA), y la incertidumbre electoral. En estos días debiera agregarse el debate por la regulación de la IA y la desaceleración de la inversión en ese campo.


La inflación


La semana anterior se informó que el índice de inflación de agosto arrojó un incremento del 0.4 mensual, lo que acumulado significa una suba interanual del 3.4%, muy alejada del 2% considerado normal.


La inflación viene en ascenso en el mundo desde los días posteriores a la pandemia, impulsada por los aumentos en los costos de las materias primas y el transporte. Sin embargo en la coyuntura inmediata el alza en EEUU es un resultado directo de la aventura militar en Medio Oriente, a la que Trump fue arrastrado por Netanyahu y a la que no le encuentra salida.


Donald Trump y Benjamin Netanyahu en el aeropuerto Ben Gurion en Tel Aviv. Foto: Chip Somodevilla


La guerra provocó la suba de las cotizaciones del petróleo, que impactó fuerte en el precio de los combustibles, subieron más de un 40% desde fines de febrero pasado cuando EEUU e Israel iniciaron los ataques a Irán. Estas cotizaciones volvieron a tensionarse en estos días cuando se conoció que el paso naval de Bad el Mandeb, una ruta alternativa al Estrecho de Ormuz bajo control iraní, quedó bajo control de los hutíes, aliados de los persas. Además Arabia Saudita informó que por ataques de drones desde Irak, cerró preventivamente el oleoducto Este-Oeste. que va desde los principales yacimientos petroleros hasta el Mar Rojo. El barril cotiza ahora por arriba de los 100 dólares.


La deuda


Hace un par de semanas se conoció que la deuda pública de EEUU alcanzó el nivel histórico de 40 billones de dólares (más del 120% del PBI). El grueso de esta deuda está originado en el extraordinario déficit del comercio exterior, especialmente con China, que el Tesoro de EEUU financia con la emisión de bonos. La carga de los intereses de estos bonos va al presupuesto y alimenta el déficit fiscal, a lo que hay que adicionar los recortes impositivos y el aumento de los gastos militares que de conjunto pudieron más que los mayores ingresos por los nuevos aranceles y los recortes en la administración pública. El resultado es que el déficit fiscal trepó al 5.8% del PBI, lejos del objetivo inicial del 3%. que obviamente se financia con más deuda, que así crece a razón de 7.000 millones diarios y se torna casi inmanejable. Sumados al déficit federal, el de los estados más la seguridad social, el déficit general supera el 7.6% del producto.


Donald Trump habla con Jerome Powell durante un recorrido en la Reserva Federal en Washington el 24 de julio de 2025. Foto oficial de la Casa Blanca por Daniel Torok


En este contexto la cotización de los bonos (tanto de corto como de largo plazo) están en baja mientras que los rendimientos, que ya venían en ascenso desde fines de la pandemia, han pegado un nuevo salto y están en niveles similares a los de 2008-2009 cuando la crisis de las …

author: anred
title: Elecciones en Berlin
content:
17 partidos se han candidateado para las elecciones de la 20 ͣ Cámara de Diputados de Berlín y de las asambleas de Consejales de distrito este Domingo 20 de Septiembre. Las elecciones se celebran en un escenario bastante crítico: La crisis de la vivienda, como uno de los principales problemas, un candidato se baja de su candidatura por duras críticas a su gestión, otro candidato está envuelto en una acusación de soborno. Esto sucede en un contexto de falta de credibilidad en la política, debido a que los gobiernos anteriores no han cumplido con sus promesas y porque el Estado de Bienestar empieza lentamente a desaparecer y se empiezan a visibilizar un menor poder adquisitivo por parte de sus habitantes. Por un lado el gobierno multiplica los subsidios para la seguridad y la armamentística, pero por el lado recorta en educación, salud y cultura. Están llamados a las urnas 2,5 millones de berlineses. Muchos habitantes migrantes están excluídos del derecho a votar. Sólo los ciudadanos de la Comunidad europea, pueden votar, pero solamente, en una de las doce asambleas de consejales de distrito. Estas son algunas de las problemáticas que definirán dondé pondrán su voto las y los habitantes de Berlín.

Por Ana Muro, corresponsal de ANRed en Alemania


Las elecciones se celebran en un escenario bastante crítico:

La crisis de la vivienda

, como uno de los principales problemas, un candidato se baja de su candidatura por duras críticas a su gestión, otro candidato está envuelto en una acusación de soborno.


Con el gran apagón de enero, quedó evidenciado que el alcalde y ex candidato principal de la CDU, Kai Wegner, había mentido y dado datos erróneos sobre su gestión de la crisis. El 10 de Julio, a raiz de las fuertes críticas, Wegner se retiró como candidato principal de su partido CDU. Esto no solo había debilitado gravemente a Wegner a título personal, sino también a su partido.

Varios apagones y sabotages sucedieron en los últimos años, como expresión de disconformidad de la política alemana en relación a su apoyo incondicional al gobierno de Israel.


El grupo anarquista Vulkan y la campaña Switch Off se adjudicaron la autoría de ellos: «Switch off contra la codicia por la energía, Switch off contra la gestión digital de la vida, Switch off contra el progreso de la destrucción». No es la primera vez que los «Grupos Vulcano» y «Switch Off» se citan mutuamente.

El complejo de la megafábrica Tesla también sufrió daños.


Otro hecho que toma parte para la campaña electoral: El 25 de julio, una mujer fallece y muchas otras personas resultan gravemente heridas en la marcha del orgullo Christopher Street Day en pleno centro de Berlín. Una persona devota del Islam es acusada de embestir con un coche a la gente que estaba marchando. El atentado hace que, a corto plazo, el tema de la seguridad interior cobre mayor protagonismo en la campaña electoral.


Las personas candidatas


El Partido CDU cambió a su candidato muy sobre la fecha, luego de que Wagner se retirase de su candidatura, y propuso al senador de Hacienda y Cultura Stefan Evers, que mostró su política antimigrantes sin tapujos. Stefan Evers concedió una entrevista televisiva y realizó polémicas declaraciones sobre el atentado en la marcha del orgullo al acusar a La Izquierda de “negación de la realidad” en lo que respecta al islamismo y también mostró preocupación por el “creciente odio hacia los judíos”. Evers ha encontrado su tema principal para la campaña electoral: su política antimigrantes, la advertencia sobre La Izquierda como “riesgo para la seguridad de la capital del país” y la criminalización a la solidaridad con Palestina.


La candidata principal del partido de izquierda Die Linke, Elif Eralp, puede convertirse en la primera mujer jefa de gobierno de la ciudad autónoma de Berlin de origen migrante. Ella acusó a la CDU de “dividir a la ciudad y preferir mimar a los propietarios codiciosos en lugar de hacer algo para combatir la crisis del mercado inmobiliario”. El partido de izquierda-Die Linke- desde las últimas dos elecciones -defiende el tema que más importa a los votantes de la ciudad: la vivienda y los alquileres y es el partido de los que tienen más chances, según las encuestas. En las elecciones pasadas tuvieron un resultado exitoso e inesperado de más del 9%.


Cada vez se perfila con mayor claridad una pugna por el primer puesto. La CDU y La Izquierda llevan semanas codo con codo, y últimamente La Izquierda lleva una ligera ventaja.

author: infolibre
title: Απάντηση Νίκου Μαζιώτη στην πρέσβειρα των ΗΠΑ Κίμπερλι Γκίλφοϊλ
content:
ΑΠΑΝΤΗΣΗ ΤΟΥ ΝΙΚΟΥ ΜΑΖΙΩΤΗ ΣΤΙΣ ΔΗΛΩΣΕΙΣ ΓΚΙΛΦΟΪΛ


Επ’ ευκαιρίας των δηλώσεων της πρέσβειρας των ΗΠΑ, Κίμπερλι Γκίλφοϊλ, για την αποφυλάκισή μου, θέλω να πω τα εξής: όταν ο εχθρός κάνει τέτοιες δηλώσεις, τότε σημαίνει ότι είμαι στον σωστό δρόμο! Θα άρχιζα να ανησυχούσα αν έκανε επαινετικές δηλώσεις για το άτομό μου!


Πράγματι, δεν έχω θέση σε μια κοινωνία και σε ένα σύστημα που μέσα από την ορολογία του «πολιτισμο» εννοούν την υποταγή, την καταπίεση, την δουλεία, τον ρατσισμό, την ανισότητα, τους πολέμους, τις γενοκτονίες λαών, την καταστροφή της φύσης και της γης. Άτομα όπως η Κίμπερλι Γκίλφοϊλ, αυτά  θεωρούν ως «πολιτισμό» και «δημοκρατία».


Από την άλλη μεριά, είναι υποκρισία να με χαρακτηρίζει «τρομοκράτη» η εκπρόσωπος των πραγματικών αρχιτρομοκρατών, των σφαγέων των λαών, των ιμπεριαλιστών, αυτών που βομβαρδίζουν και δολοφονούν αμάχους στο Ιράν, παλιότερα στο Ιράκ και το Αφγανιστάν, αυτών που εξοπλίζουν το Ισραήλ για να δολοφονεί δεκάδες χιλιάδες αμάχους Παλαιστίνιους στη Λωρίδα της Γάζας.


Είναι οι ίδιοι που παλιότερα βομβάρδιζαν το Βιετνάμ και βρίσκονταν πίσω από κάθε φασιστικό-δικτατορικό καθεστώς, στην Λατινική Αμερική, την Ασία, και την Αφρική, αυτοί που εκπαίδευαν τους βασανιστές και στήριζαν τα τάγματα θανάτου. Είναι οι ίδιοι που βασάνιζαν κρατούμενους στο Γκουαντάναμο και στο Αμπού Γκράιμπ μετά την επίθεση της 11/9/2001 και την κήρυξη του πολέμου κατά της «τρομοκρατίας».


Έχει θράσος η εκπρόσωπος της Αυτοκρατορίας να μιλάει, όταν το κράτος της μέσω του ΔΝΤ επέβαλε στον ελληνικό λαό το απεχθές καθεστώς δουλοπαροικίας μέσα από τα μνημόνια που εξόντωσαν χιλιάδες πολίτες, την ίδια στιγμή που η ίδια έκανε αισχρές δηλώσεις για τον ελληνικό λαό, όπως ότι είμαστε τεμπέληδες.


Η πρέσβειρα των ΗΠΑ θα πρέπει να ξέρει ότι πολλοί σ’ αυτήν τη χώρα δεν ξεχνούν τον βρώμικο ρόλο που έπαιξε το κράτος της στην ιστορία αυτού του τόπου όπως στον εμφύλιο του 1947-’49 και τη δικτατορία του 1967-’74. Και θα πρέπει να λάβει υπόψη ότι παρά πολλοί σ’ αυτόν τον τόπο αλλά και διεθνώς χάρηκαν και επικρότησαν την επίθεση του Επαναστατικού Αγώνα με αντιαρματική ρουκέτα RPG στην πρεσβεία των ΗΠΑ το 2007. Με την επίθεση αυτή είχαμε απαντήσει στον τότε πρόεδρο των ΗΠΑ, Τζώρτζ Μπους τζούνιορ –που στο πλαίσιο του «πολέμου κατά της ‘‘τρομοκρατίας’’» είχε πει ότι «όποιος δεν είναι μαζί μας, είναι εναντίον μας» –ότι ΔΕΝ ΕΙΜΑΣΤΕ ΜΑΖΙ ΣΑΣ, ΕΙΜΑΣΤΕ ΕΝΑΝΤΙΟΝ ΣΑΣ! Όπως και πάρα πολλοί σ’ αυτόν τον τόπο!


Νίκος Μαζιώτης


20/9/2026

infolibre

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Remembering John Coltrane (1926-1967)
content:
Little of beauty has America given the world save the rude grandeur God himself stamped on her bosom; the human spirit in this new world has expressed itself in vigor and ingenuity rather than in beauty. And so by fateful chance the Negro folk-song—the rhythmic cry of the slave—stands to-day not simply as the sole American music, but as the most beautiful expression of human experience born this side the seas. It has been neglected, it has been, and is, half despised, and above all it has been persistently mistaken and misunderstood; but notwithstanding, it still remains as the singular spiritual heritage of the nation and the greatest gift of the Negro people.


W.E.B. Du Bois,

The Souls of Black Folk

, 1903


Whenever I make a change, I’m a little worried that it may puzzle people. And sometimes I deliberately delay things for this reason. But after a while I find there is nothing else I can do but go ahead.


John Coltrane (from J.C. Thomas,

Coltrane: Chasin’ the Trane,

 1975)


John Coltrane was born on the 23rd of September, 1926. The centenary of his birth serves as the occasion – though such an occasion should not be necessary – to remember and celebrate his music, and more. For this, humbly, we cite the writing and artistry of others.


We begin with a selection from writer Fred Moten and his work,

In the Break: The Aesthetics of the Black Radical Tradition

 (University of Minnesota Press, 2003). We follow with Amiri Baraka’s poem “I Love Music (For John Coltrane)”. We then turn to Cornell West and his reflections on a jazz-soaked philosophy and James Baldwin on the radicalness of love, from

The Fire Next Time

 (1962) and Toni Morrison on the immanence of love and grace, from

Beloved

 (1987) . And we close with a link to Coltrane’s album,

A Love Supreme

 (1965).


Fred Moten, from

In the Break: The Aesthetics of the Black Radical Tradition

 (2003)


Here, then, is one such disclosure, famously and infamously made by Frederick Douglass in his 1845

Narrative

. By way of a set of resonant nodal points along the massive trajectory it extends, I want to think about this disclosure as an unavoidable anticipation, the prefigurative response to an epochal counterfactual, the always already belated origin of the music that ought to be understood as the rigorously sounded critique of the theory of value.


I have often been awakened at the dawn of day by the most heart-rending shrieks of an own aunt of mine, whom he used to tie up to a joist, and whip upon her naked back till she was literally covered with blood. No words, no tears, no prayers, from his gory victim, seemed to move his iron heart from its bloody purpose. The louder she screamed, the harder he whipped; and where the blood ran fastest, there he whipped the longest. He would whip her to make her scream, and whip her to make her hush; and not until overcome by fatigue, would he cease to swing the blood clotted cowskin. I remember the first time I ever witnessed this horrible exhibition. I was quite a child, but I well remember it. I shall never forget it whilst I remember anything. It was the first of a long series of such out rages, of which I was doomed to be a witness and a participant. It struck me with awful force. It was the blood-stained gate, the entrance to the hell of slavery, through which I was about to pass. It was a most terrible spectacle. I wish I could commit to paper the feelings with which I beheld it. . . .


Aunt Hester had not only disobeyed his orders in going out, but had been found in company with Lloyd’s Ned; which circumstance, I found, from what he said while whipping her, was the chief offense. Had he been a man of pure morals himself, he might have been thought interested in protecting the innocence of my aunt; but those who know him will not suspect him of any such virtue. Before he commenced whipping Aunt Hester he took her into the kitchen, and stripped her from neck to waist, leaving her neck, shoulders, and back entirely naked. He then told her to cross her hands, calling her at the same time a d——d b——h. After crossing her hands, he tied them with strong rope, and led her to a stool under a large hook in the joist, put in for the purpose. He made her get upon the stool, and tied her hands to the hook. She now stood fair for the infernal purpose. Her arms were stretched up at their full length, so that she stood upon the ends of her toes. He then said to her, “Now, you d——d b——h, I’ll learn you how to …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Isaac Deutscher: Message of the Non-Jewish Jew
content:
The following article by the biographer of Stalin and Trotsky, whose writings on Russia and Eastern Europe appear regularly in periodicals throughout the world, is based on a lecture delivered in London last February during Jewish Book Week to the World Jewish Congress. This text, revised and extended by the author, appeared in 

Universities and Left Review

, and is reprinted here with the author’s permission. A summary of the lecture had previously appeared in the British 

Jewish Observer and Middle East Review.


I REMEMBER that when as a child I read the 

Midrash

 I came across a story and a description of a scene which gripped my imagination. It was the story of Rabbi Meir, the great saint, sage, and the pillar of Mosaic orthodoxy and co-author of the 

Mishna

, who took lessons in theology from a heretic Elisha ben Abiyuh, nicknamed Akher (The Stranger). Once on a Sabbath, Rabbi Meir went out on a trip with his teacher, and as usual they became engaged in deep argument. The heretic was riding a donkey, and Rabbi Meir, as he could not ride on a Sabbath, walked by his side and listened so intently to the words of wisdom falling from heretical lips, that he failed to notice that he and his teacher had reached the ritual boundary which Jews were not allowed to cross on a Sabbath. At that moment the great heretic turned to his pupil and said: “Look, we have reached the boundary—we must part now: you must not accompany me any further—go back!” Rabbi Meir went back to the Jewish community while the heretic rode on—beyond the boundaries of Jewry.


There was enough in this scene to puzzle an orthodox Jewish child. Why, I wondered, did Rabbi Meir take his lessons from the heretic? Why did he show him so much affection? Why did he defend him against other rabbis? My heart, it seems, was with the heretic. Who was he?,


I asked. He appeared to be in Jewry and yet out of it. He showed a curious respect for his pupil’s orthodoxy when he sent him back to the Jews on the holy Sabbath; but he himself, disregarding canon and ritual, rode beyond the boundaries. When I was thirteen or perhaps fourteen I began to write a drama on Akher and Rabbi Meir and tried to find out more about Akher’s character. What made him transcend Judaism? Was he a Gnostic? Was he the adherent of some other school of Greek or Roman philosophy? I could not find the answers, and I did not manage to go beyond the first act of my drama.


The Jewish heretic who transcends Jewry belongs to a Jewish tradition. You may, if you like, view Akher as a prototype of those great revolutionaries of modern thought about whom I am going to speak this evening—you may do so, if you necessarily wish to place them within any Jewish tradition. They all went beyond the boundaries of Jewry. They all—Spinoza, Heine, Marx, Rosa Luxemburg, Trotsky, and Freud—found Jewry too narrow, too archaic, and too constricting. They all looked for ideals and fulfilment beyond it, and they represent the sum and substance of much that is greatest in modern thought, the sum and substance of the most profound upheavals that have taken place in philosophy, sociology, economics, and politics in the last three centuries.


HAVE they anything in common with one another? Have they perhaps impressed mankind’s thought so greatly because of their special “Jewish genius”? I do not believe in the exclusive genius of any race. Yet I think that in some ways they were very Jewish indeed. They had in themselves something of the quintessence of Jewish life and of the Jewish intellect. They were 

a priori

 exceptional in that as Jews they dwelt on the borderlines of various civilizations, religions, and national cultures. They were born and brought up on the borderlines of various epochs. Their minds matured where the most diverse cultural influences crossed and fertilized each other. They lived on the margins or in the nooks and crannies of their respective nations. They were each in society and yet not in it, of it and yet not of it. It was this that enabled them to rise in thought above their societies, above their nations, above their times and generations, and to strike out mentally into wide new horizons and far into the future.


It was, I think, an English Protestant biographer of Spinoza who said that only a Jew could carry out that upheaval in the philosophy of his age that Spinoza carried out—a Jew who was not bound by the dogmas of the Christian churches, Catholic and Protestant, nor by …

title: Musa Anter öldürüldüğü sokakta anıldı: “Yüzleşme kaçınılmaz”
content:
Gazeteci, yazar ve aydın Musa Anter, öldürülmesinin 34. yılında Diyarbakır’da anıldı.


Mezopotamya Ajansı’nın (MA) aktardığına göre Dicle Fırat Gazeteciler Derneği’nin (DFG) düzenlediği anma, Anter’in 20 Eylül 1992’de vurulduğu Yenişehir ilçesine bağlı Seyrantepe semtindeki Cumhuriyet Mahallesi’nde yapıldı.


Anmaya Anter’in ailesinin yanı sıra gazeteciler, siyasi parti ve sivil toplum örgütlerinin temsilcileri katıldı.


“Faili meçhul cinayetler aydınlatılmalı”


Anmada konuşan DFG üyesi Fexredin Kılıç, Anter’in öldürülmesinin üzerinden 34 yıl geçmesine rağmen cinayetin arkasındaki yapıların bütünüyle ortaya çıkarılmadığını söyledi.


Devam eden barış sürecine değinen Kılıç, geçmişteki faili meçhul cinayetlerle yüzleşilmesi gerektiğini belirtti:


Barışı konuştuğumuz bugünlerde, Apê Musa’nın katledildiği yerden bir kez daha ifade ediyoruz; barış için faili meçhul cinayetler aydınlatılmalıdır.


Kılıç, Anter’in ölümünün ardından Kürt basınında çalışan gazetecilerin öldürülme, gözaltı, tutuklama, tehdit ve yayın yasaklarıyla karşı karşıya kaldığını söyledi.


Anter’den Aykol’a


DFG Eşbaşkanı Selman Çiçek de 1 Ocak’ta hayatını kaybeden gazeteci ve yazar Hüseyin Aykol’u andı.


Aykol’un geçmiş yıllarda Anter için düzenlenen anmalara katıldığını belirten Çiçek, gazetecilik geleneğinin kuşaktan kuşağa aktarıldığını söyledi:


“Apê Musa’dan Hüseyin hocaya, Hüseyin hocadan bize, bizden diğer nesillere aktararak bu geleneği sürdüreceğiz.”


Anter’in oğlu Dicle Anter de babasını her yıl öldürüldüğü yerde anmaya devam edeceklerini söyledi.


Mızraklı: Adalet olmadan barış tesis edilemez


8 Eylül’de Edirne Cezaevi’nden tahliye edilen eski Diyarbakır Büyükşehir Belediyesi Eşbaşkanı Selçuk Mızraklı da anmaya katıldı. Mızraklı’nın tahliyesi farklı haber kaynaklarınca da doğrulandı.


Mızraklı, Anter’in Kürt basını ve toplumu açısından bıraktığı mirasa değinerek devam eden barış sürecinde geçmişle yüzleşmenin önemine dikkat çekti.


“Özellikle Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci’yle birlikte barışın derinleşmesi, onurlu bir barışın tesisi için hakikatlerin ortaya çıkarılması ve yüzleşme kaçınılmazdır” diyen Mızraklı, adalet sağlanmadan kalıcı bir barışın kurulamayacağını söyledi.


Mızraklı, Kürtçe üzerindeki baskılara karşı yürütülen mücadeleyi hatırlatarak, “Artık binlerce Musa Anter var. Onun bıraktığı kalemle korkusuzca yazan, fotoğraf makinesini en zor anlarda kullanan binlerce gencimiz var” dedi.


Eren: “Özgür basın susmadı”


DEM Parti Diyarbakır Milletvekili Serhat Eren de Anter’in Kürt dili ve kültürü için verdiği mücadeleye değindi.


Anter’in öldürülmesinin ardından Kürt basınının çalışmalarını sürdürdüğünü söyleyen Eren, gazetecilerin gözaltı, tutuklama ve çeşitli baskılarla karşılaştığını belirtti.


Anma, Musa Anter’in öldürüldüğü yere fotoğrafının ve karanfillerin bırakılmasıyla sona erdi.


Musa Anter cinayeti


Musa Anter, 20 Eylül 1992 gecesi Diyarbakır’da silahlı saldırıya uğradı. Saldırıda Anter hayatını kaybetti, yanında bulunan Orhan Miroğlu ise yaralandı. Amnesty International, cinayetten iki gün sonra yayımladığı açıklamada Anter’in 20 Eylül’de öldürüldüğünü ve olayın koşullarının araştırılması gerektiğini bildirdi.


Cinayete ilişkin daha sonra açılan dava, JİTEM ana davasıyla birleştirildi.


Ankara 6. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi, 21 Eylül 2022’de Musa Anter’in öldürülmesi ve Orhan Miroğlu’nun yaralanmasına ilişkin davanın 30 yıllık zamanaşımı süresinin dolduğu gerekçesiyle düşürülmesine karar verdi. Mahkeme, JİTEM ana davasının ise ayrı bir dosya üzerinden sürmesine hükmetti.


Anter ailesinin avukatı, düşme kararının ardından yaşam hakkının ihlal edildiği gerekçesiyle Anayasa Mahkemesi’ne bireysel başvuruda bulundu.


(NÖ)

title: Iraq begins trial of six French ISIS members
content:
The trial of six French nationals accused of membership in the “Islamic State” (ISIS) began on Sunday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad. The defendants were transferred from northeastern Syria to Iraq earlier this year. Under tight security, armored military vehicles transported the six men to the Karkh Court of Appeal building. Vehicles carrying French diplomats arrived there later. Journalists were barred from attending the proceedings.


The identities of the six defendants have not yet been made public. They are part of a group of 47 French nationals transferred to Iraq from prisons run by the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria. The group also includes Adrien Guihal, who claimed responsibility on behalf of ISIS for the July 14, 2016 attack in Nice, in which 86 people were killed.


Proceedings against thousands of ISIS members


The trials of the French ISIS members are part of a much larger series of legal proceedings. By mid-February, more than 5,700 suspected ISIS members had been transferred from northeastern Syria to Iraq. According to Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, they represent 67 different nationalities, including 474 Iraqis and 3,497 Syrians. In early September, the Iraqi judiciary announced that the interrogations and investigations involving all 5,704 defendants had been completed. Their cases are now being referred individually to the competent courts based on the evidence available in each case.


According to the judiciary, the defendants also include individuals who held leadership positions as well as military, security-related, or media roles within ISIS. In at least six cases, the investigations also uncovered links to the capture, enslavement, abduction, or sale of Yazidi women who were abducted from Shengal during the ISIS genocide in August 2014.

author: Cierra Bettens
title: Looking deep into Canada’s opioid crisis: InFocus
content:
You usually find Karyn Pugliese chasing down politicians on Parliament Hill.


But for the past few months, she’s been digging into Canada’s opioid crisis.


This week on APTN News InFocus, Pugliese and associate producer Raven Brascoupe join me for a behind-the-scenes look at their ongoing investigation.


“You could explore this from the crime issue, like the gangs and the selling of drugs,” Pugliese said. “I wanted to explore it as a medical issue. Because of the stats, First Nations seem to be more vulnerable to opioid addiction–and we ask, why? It could be because of things that we know, like historic trauma from residential schools, the child welfare system; that could very well be true.


“But are there other things as well?”


After interning for APTN News in Ottawa, Brascoupe jumped on the opportunity to join the project.


“Coming on as a new journalist on such a big topic, I’m pretty grateful for it,” Brascoupe said. “[From] living with the lived experience to getting to research it and talk with Karyn every day about it, what we know, what we’re learning, has been really good.”


Over the past few months, the duo has connected with people across the country with firsthand addiction experience. They’ve been on the ground with frontline workers and on the phone with leaders to find out what is and isn’t working.


“What I’m hearing from frontline workers is that there are two values to safe supply. One is that it does save lives because you can watch and prevent an overdose right there,” Pugliese said. “Now, we have people in Ottawa walking down the streets, trying to find people who are using. They’re being chased out of the downtown area so it’s harder to find out where people are gathering.”


“Manitoba is doing quite an incredible job. I was talking to one chief from Manto Sipi Cree Nation, Chief Yellowback,” Brascoupe said. “They have FNSOs, First Nation Safety Officers. They set up checkpoints, and they check people who come in to make sure they’re not bringing illicit drugs or alcohol. And there’s a bylaw they worked on so they could implement these laws.”


Through their investigative reporting, Pugliese and Brascoupe hope to cut through the noise and start having real conversations about how to move forward.


“I don’t know that we’re going to come out of this and say there’s a solution. But I know there is a lot of debate about what path to take,” Pugliese said. “I wanted to better understand how to separate political arguments that are purely political and ideological from the health science.”


Have a story for this project? Reach out to Karyn at

kpugliese@aptn.ca

 or Raven at

rbrascoupe@aptn.ca

.

title: Fon soruşturması: 4 şirket için MASAK'a yeni inceleme talebi
content:
İstanbul Başsavcılığı tarafından yürütülen fon soruşturmasında mali incelemenin kapsamı genişletildi. Terörizmin Finansmanı ve Aklama Suçları Soruşturma Bürosu, Mali Suçları Araştırma Kurulu Başkanlığına (MASAK) resmi yazı göndererek dört aracı kurum ve holding ile alt şirketlerinin yöneticilerine ilişkin ayrıntılı mali verilerin iletilmesini talep etti.

Savcılık talimatında, Pusula Finans Holding AŞ, Tera Yatırım Menkul Değerler AŞ, Hedef Holding AŞ ve Bulls Yatırım Menkul Değerler AŞ ile bağlı şirketlerinin yöneticilerinin kimlik bilgilerinin çıkarılması istendi. İnceleme kapsamında, söz konusu yöneticilerin 2024 yılından bugüne kadar yurt dışına yaptıkları tüm para ve kripto varlık transferleri ile hesaplarındaki nakit akışlarının ham veri olarak dosyaya sunulması talep edildi.

Mali inceleme yalnızca şirket yöneticileriyle sınırlı tutulmadı, yöneticilerin birinci derece yakınlarının para ve kripto hareketleri de kapsama alındı. Soruşturmayla, şüphelilerin doğrudan ya da aile üyeleri üzerinden yurt dışına kaynak aktarıp aktarmadıklarının tespiti amaçlanıyor.

Gizlilik kararı bulunan dosya kapsamında son olarak Pusula Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Serdar Turhan, Tera Yatırım Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Emre Tezmen ile Alper Öztürk, Emre Alkin ve Kerem Alkin gözaltına alınmıştı.

Daha önce Pusula Portföy Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Muhammed Yarız ve Destek Yatırım Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Altunç Kumova’nın da aralarında bulunduğu dört şüpheli tutuklanmış, 51 kişi hakkında ise adli kontrol kapsamında yurt dışına çıkış yasağı getirilmişti.

Öte yandan Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), soruşturmayla bağlantılı yedi portföy yönetim şirketine ait 131 yatırım fonunu TEFAS işlemlerine kapatarak tasfiye sürecini başlatmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: European Kurdish filmmakers meet at workshop
content:
Kurdish filmmakers living in Europe gathered at a workshop in Charleroi, Belgium, to discuss the challenges Kurdish cinema faces in various areas, from production and distribution to festivals and education, and to develop common solutions.


The three-day gathering, attended by around 50 filmmakers, includes directors, screenwriters, producers, actors, cinematographers, editors, and festival organizers.


Explaining the purpose of the workshop, the organizers said: “We want to make films, write screenplays, organize festivals, and distribute films. We face different problems in each area of work. We are holding this workshop to solve these problems.”


Kurdish filmmakers came together at the Çanda Med Cultural Center on September 18. At the reception held on the first day of the gathering, the filmmakers introduced themselves and their work. Filmmakers working in different countries and in different areas thus had the opportunity to get to know one another and share their experiences.


Joint discussion in four areas


Following the introductions, the filmmakers divided into four working groups. The groups were organized around the themes of distribution and festivals, production and financing, education and development, and international solidarity. Each filmmaker joined one of the groups according to their area of work and interest.


The aim of the groups is not merely to list problems, but also to assess the current state of Kurdish cinema in Europe and develop solutions to the challenges being encountered.


The distribution and festivals group is addressing issues including bringing films to audiences, developing festivals, and opportunities for the circulation of Kurdish films. The production and financing group is discussing the economic and structural problems facing film production. The education and development group is focusing on training filmmakers and transferring experience, while the international solidarity group is considering opportunities for partnerships and solidarity among filmmakers in Europe.


Identifying problems, discussing solutions


The working groups held their first meetings on the evening of September 18. The groups will meet again today to deepen the discussions. Each group will assess the current situation in its respective area and identify existing problems, after which they will prepare proposals and possible solutions to address them.


In this way, the workshop is becoming more than simply a gathering of Kurdish filmmakers living in different countries; it is creating a forum in which the problems experienced across different areas of cinema are brought together for collective discussion.


The assessments, proposals, and solutions prepared by the working groups will be presented to all the filmmakers at the workshop meeting on September 20.


Following the discussions conducted over three days, the proposals that emerge are intended to strengthen relations among Kurdish filmmakers in Europe, develop opportunities for joint production and solidarity, and create common responses to the problems Kurdish cinema faces in different areas, from production to festivals and from education to distribution.

author: Unknown
title: Doğan: Roma Alevis’ demands span interconnected areas
content:
Alevis in Turkey have faced repression, massacres and various forms of discrimination for many years. Roma Alevis face these forms of discrimination as well as the additional problem of not being fully accepted within the Alevi community itself.


Ozan Doğan, author of the book Roma Alevis, spoke to ANF about the problems facing Roma Alevis. He said: “The term ‘Roma Alevis’ refers to a diverse range of communities distinguished by their ties to Alevi ocaks and their different social experiences.”


Roma Alevis have different relationships with the Alevi ocak system


Doğan said Roma Alevis have distinct relationships with the Alevi ocak system and continued:


“The term ‘Roma Alevis’ refers to a heterogeneous population with different ethno-cultural characteristics and social experiences. In Turkey, these communities are generally described by outsiders as Roma or Gypsies. However, these groups do not use the term ‘Gypsy’ because of its pejorative connotations. ‘Roma’, meanwhile, is generally used as an umbrella term encompassing different groups such as Rom, Dom and Lom.


An important distinction needs to be made here. Many groups of nomadic origin are regarded as Gypsy or Roma because of factors such as their livelihood strategies, physical appearance, social status or settlement patterns. The homogenising perspective of outsiders tends to obscure the differences between these groups. Abdals, for example, are not a Roma group. Their distinctive languages, historical migration routes, traditional crafts and relationships with the Alevi ocak system clearly distinguish them from Roma groups. Classifying Abdals as Roma would be a reductive approach that disregards the internal dynamics of these communities. There are also other groups of nomadic origin, besides Abdals, that do not belong to Roma communities.


Ultimately, the term ‘Roma Alevis’ refers to a range of communities that share an Alevi world of faith but differ in their languages, including Romanes, Domari and Lomavren, as well as their crafts, historical migration routes, ties to Alevi ocaks and social experiences. These communities number in the hundreds of thousands, yet there had been no academic study of them in Turkey until my doctoral dissertation. Even today, however, our knowledge of the extensive cultural and historical heritage of these large communities remains very limited.”


They preserve their Alevi faith


Doğan said Roma Alevis’ relationship with the Alevi faith has been passed down from generation to generation. Doğan also said: “The relationship between Roma Alevis and the Alevi faith is not a recent development. My field research found that this relationship has historical foundations, passed down through generations and shaped by the Alevi ocak system. For example, the blacksmith communities in Uşak, a group with their own distinct language and history, and the sieve-making communities, who are Lom, have ties to the Kütahya-based Işık Çakır Sultan Ocak and Sarı İsmail Sultan (Uzun Allah Kulu) Ocak. Accounts passed down by ocak dedes and elders within the community indicate that ties with the Işık Çakır Sultan Ocak date back to the 1800s. Roma groups affiliated with other Alevi ocaks can also be found in other regions. There is therefore a continuity of ties to the ocak system that has been maintained across generations.


In terms of religious practices, there is no qualitative difference between Roma Alevis and other Alevi communities. The field data showed that Roma Alevis have not developed a distinct form of Alevism, but rather have preserved the Alevi world of faith under their own specific historical and social conditions. The findings also showed that members of the second and third generations in particular actively participate in cemevi activities and religious practices.”


Cemevis are places of social interaction for Roma Alevis


Doğan said cemevis hold an important place in the lives of Roma Alevis and provide a space for social interaction in everyday life.


Doğan said: “The cemevi occupies an important place in the daily lives of Roma Alevis in Uşak. The historical roots of the Işık Çakır Sultan Cemevi, established in the city in 2013, date back to the 1980s. This means there is a cemevi tradition spanning around forty years. The evolution from a cemevi operating on a recognised basis to one established with municipal support tells us a great deal about the presence of Roma Alevis in Uşak. The cemevi is not merely a …

author: Unknown
title: Bedreddin, Dersim and the Alevi pursuit of justice and equality
content:
The social movements that emerged at different points in Alevi history cannot be regarded as identical. One of the threads running through this history, however, is resistance to injustice. Dersim remains one of the deepest wounds in Alevi memory and continues to hold an important place in discussions about peace today.


Alevi history cannot be confined to the 16th and 20th centuries alone. Social movements that emerged in Anatolia at different periods have found different places in Alevi memory through their pursuit of justice and equality and their opposition to oppression. The movements led by Baba Ilyas and Baba Ishak were among the significant challenges to the social and political inequalities of their time. The movement that developed around Sheikh Bedreddin, meanwhile, has been interpreted in different ways for centuries in debates over sharing, equality and social justice.


“Everything should be shared except the beloved’s cheek” has remained in collective memory as one of the most powerful expressions of the egalitarian interpretation of Bedreddin’s legacy. It may not be historically accurate to define all these movements as modern Alevi movements in today’s sense. Yet it is not difficult to understand why they found a place in Alevi memory. Although they emerged in different periods and under different circumstances, resistance to injustice became a defining element in how these movements were reinterpreted by subsequent generations.


Dersim: One of the deepest wounds in Alevi memory


Then comes Dersim. The years 1937–38 mark a devastating historical period in which Seyit Rıza, Alişer, Zarife and thousands of others were killed, exiled and displaced.


Describing Dersim solely as a “rebellion against the state” leaves out a significant part of the social dimension of what happened. Alongside the armed conflict, there was a world of faith, language, a relationship with the land, ocaks (Alevi spiritual lineages) and distinctive forms of local social organisation. State policies intervened in and affected all of these spheres.


The execution of Seyit Rıza and the killing of Alişer and Zarife did not become events confined to the past in the collective memory of Dersim. What happened left a social trauma carried through the accounts of families, those who were exiled and subsequent generations. Any understanding of Alevi sensitivities regarding the state, security policies, confronting the past and peace would also remain incomplete without taking into account the place Dersim occupies in Alevi memory.


Why is the history of Alevi women forgotten?


One of the major omissions in accounts of Alevi history is the invisibility of women. Telling this history solely through men excludes a significant part of that collective memory. Dersim is one of the most striking examples.


Zarife Hanım (a respectful form of address for women) is often referred to in historical accounts as Alişer’s wife. Defining her solely through that relationship, however, fails to capture her place in the history of Dersim. Zarife was a woman who held her own place in Dersim’s resistance and collective memory through her identity and struggle. The struggle that Alişer and Zarife waged together also became an important part of Dersim’s political and social history.


Zarife’s life also opens the door to a broader discussion about the place of Alevi women in history. Women were not merely those who bore the pain of massacres, exile and repression; they also played a role in building social life, passing on collective memory and taking part in resistance. Accounts of Alevi history should therefore go beyond recording women simply as the wives, mothers or relatives of men and make their own voices, actions and historical roles visible.


Where does all this history lead us?


Hallaj, Nesimi, Hacı Bektaş, Hatayi, Pir Sultan, Bedreddin and Seyit Rıza did not live in the same era or under the same political conditions. Hatayi lived amid the Safavid-Ottoman rivalry, while Pir Sultan’s name endured in the memory of conflicts with Ottoman rule. Bedreddin emerged under very different social circumstances, while Seyit Rıza was confronted with the modern state’s policies towards Dersim.


It would be inaccurate to read these figures as though they were all part of the same historical movement. Yet looking at why Alevi memory has kept them alive for centuries reveals certain common threads: the pursuit of truth, the demand for justice, the value …

title: Şimşek: No solution without an active society and local democracy
content:
The failure to develop local democracy and the exclusion of society from decision-making processes lie at the heart of the ongoing crises in Turkey and the Middle East. Ali Şimşek, a politician with many years of experience in legal democratic politics, spoke to ANF in Lausanne about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, democratic integration and models of local government.


Şimşek compared Switzerland’s experience of direct democracy, based on its 26 cantons, with the power-centred political mentality prevailing in the Middle East, stressing that society must play a direct role in resolving its own problems. Şimşek said, “Submitting to the system and dissolving within it is not integration; it is assimilation,” and arguing that a lasting solution requires democratic integration in which different communities participate while preserving their distinct identities.


 


As you know, the Peace and Democratic Society Process has been under way in Turkey for nearly two years. Democratic integration has also become a subject of debate following Abdullah Öcalan’s call. You were involved in legal democratic politics for many years. For democratic integration to take place, how should local democracy be developed first? What needs to be done to strengthen local democracy?


This is, in fact, an extremely broad and complex issue. It is also one of the fundamental questions facing the entire world. Looking at Europe and the Middle East, two key dimensions of society come to the fore. In Europe, one concerns the relationship between the individual and society, relations within society itself, and the relationship between society or the individual and those in power. These are issues that require hours of reflection, research and discussion.


Similar problems undoubtedly emerge in the Middle East. Yet because the relationships, aspirations, demands and needs of Middle Eastern societies differ considerably from those in Europe, these problems manifest themselves through very different means and methods. In Europe, for example, society’s demands and aspirations are generally pursued through peaceful means, elections and social relations shaped by certain principles. Individuals know the boundaries and principles governing their personal, everyday and social lives and generally act accordingly.


The Middle East, on the other hand, despite having societies with histories stretching back thousands of years, is still searching for a way forward. It has yet to find a solution for building social relations that would allow everyday life to rest on peace and stability. Problems are still addressed through war, conflict and plunder, or societies are expected to resolve them through such means.


The question you raise is therefore extremely important not only for the Middle East as a whole, but specifically for Kurdish, Turkish, Arab and Persian societies. If a positive answer to this question had been found, the wars, conflicts and problems that are damaging social life across the Middle East today could have been resolved. Yet the search for a solution continues to encounter obstacles and remains deeply constrained.


How can we break this deadlock? The crucial question is how strong society can become in relation to those in power so that it can solve its own problems and move beyond the state of “war, conflict and hostility” that ruling forces seek to perpetuate. The ruling powers of the Middle East regard hostilities within society as a means of protecting their own interests and maintaining their power. How can this be overcome? How can society, through individuals and local communities, find solutions to these problems? This is the greatest challenge. We need to reach a point where society recognises that the solution to its problems lies within society itself.


We have seen and experienced a great deal and shared many things with society over the years. For me, the most important lesson is this: as politicians and people seeking to provide leadership to society, we have never left society alone with its own problems. We put ourselves in society’s place and assumed responsibility for solving those problems. But this approach does not work; it does not take us forward. Society must understand that it is itself responsible for finding solutions to its problems and must actively seek those solutions. It must know that social problems cannot be resolved without its participation. Society must take responsibility and actively …

title: Zekiye Dêrazor: I found my courage in the mountains of Kurdistan
content:
The mountains of Kurdistan carry a unique meaning not only because of their grandeur, but also because of the countless stories of lives and struggles they have witnessed. Having witnessed the lives, suffering, joys, and victories of guerrillas, the mountains have become, for those waging a struggle for freedom, not merely a place of struggle but also a place for getting to know oneself and discovering one’s own strength.


One of those who turned toward the mountains of Kurdistan in search of freedom is Zekiye Dêrazor, a YJA Star guerrilla from the Arab people. Raised in a patriotic family, Dêrazor deepened her search for freedom after being influenced by the experiences of martyrdom and struggle within her family.


Dêrazor first came to know the YPJ (Women’s Protection Units) and was influenced by the stance and determination of women in the struggle. Encountering the power of women to change and rebuild life within the ranks of the YPJ, Dêrazor spent some time engaged in the struggle within the YPJ in Rojava.


After joining the YPJ, Dêrazor became acquainted with Abdullah Öcalan’s concept of the democratic nation. She later turned toward the mountains of Kurdistan and decided to join the guerrilla ranks.


Dêrazor expressed her thoughts on the problems faced by women as follows: “As women from the Arab people, we do not have political or military rights. We are always seen as machines for giving birth to children and are kept within a narrow framework. As an Arab woman whose rights had been taken away, I was also influenced by the YPJ movement. The YPJ is not merely a military movement; it is a political movement that struggles for the people and for women. The YPJ was influenced by Önder Apo’s [Abdullah Öcalan] ideas and built itself on this basis. I was particularly affected by the way it expanded its struggle around the approach that ‘if a woman is not free, society is not free either.’”


In memory of martyr Zekiye Alkan


YJA Star guerrilla Dêrazor explains the story behind taking the name “Zekiye” through the struggle of martyr Zekiye Alkan.


Dêrazor said: “After joining the YPJ, I came to know women who struggled like Zekiye Alkan, and I wanted to carry her name. Comrade Zekiye Alkan was one of the women committed to her country and devoted to the struggle. She set her body on fire for the freedom of her people. This had a special meaning for me. I, too, wanted to struggle, like her, to be worthy of my people and to protect them.”


Stating that after changing her name to Zekiye she decided to carry the responsibility associated with that name, Dêrazor added: “I decided that joining the guerrillas was the most appropriate choice if I wanted to uphold my name. For this reason, I joined the YJA Star forces.”


Dêrazor says that when she first came to the mountains of Kurdistan, she was afraid of heights, but that she overcame this fear together with her comrades. Dêrazor continued: “When I came to the free mountains, I was initially afraid of heights. But together with my friends, I overcame this fear and found my courage. After coming to the mountains of Kurdistan, I realized that I could overcome anything.”


Dêrazor underlinde that what affected her most in guerrilla life “was the relationships of comradeship. The help they gave one another and the solidarity that women showed toward each other affected me deeply. This also led me to love life more and to live with greater purposes.”


Saying that becoming acquainted with Öcalan’s ideas brought about an important change in her, Dêrazor states that she was particularly influenced by the fact that his assessments concerning women were not confined to any national boundary.


Dêrazor describes this process as follows: “I came to know Önder Apo’s ideas. I was particularly affected by the fact that his assessments concerning women were not limited to the framework of a single nation. Önder Apo’s ideas gave me courage and created in me a determination that was afraid of nothing. Because within the system, I did not see this strength in myself; I did not feel that I had the right to live freely. But when I came to know Önder Apo’s ideas, I saw my own strength.”


Drawing attention to the importance that Öcalan’s ideas on women’s freedom hold for her, Dêrazor concludes: “We all know that no movement’s leader has created the values that the Leadership has created for women. Therefore, we women will always be grateful to Önder Apo, who has built a free life for …

title: Nurettin Demirtaş: The commune is the spirit of collective life and freedom
content:
Nurettin Demirtaş, a member of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement, spoke to ANF about the concept of the commune as a model of communal life, freedom, and organization.


Demirtaş said that, drawing on the historical experiences of the struggle, they take organization on the basis of communes as their starting point. Defining the commune as a structure representing society’s side in the historical contradiction between society and the state, Demirtaş added that communal life, solidarity, women’s freedom, and social freedom form the basis of communal life.


Emphasizing that communal life does not arise spontaneously, Demirtaş noted that it requires consciousness, organization, and labor. Demirtaş said: “We will resist through communality, and we will become free through communality.”


 


Nurettin Demirtaş made the following assessment: “Based on the immense experiences of our struggle, today we take organization on the basis of communes as our starting point. Throughout history, there have been the state and powers on one side and society on the other. They have always been in contradiction.


The commune represents society’s side in this contradiction. Önder Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] opened up the dichotomy between the state and the commune in the manifesto and, from a historical perspective, illuminated what we need to do today as well. The commune is a spirit.


It is the culture and spirit of communal life. It expresses spirituality, faith, love, respect, and sharing. Can one escape from this? To flee from the commune is to flee from humanity. Capitalism, however, has created such a nightmare that when people hear the word ‘commune,’ it is almost as if they imagine that everything in everyone’s possession will be taken away. That everyone will be reduced to poverty. So let us not be deceived by such propaganda.


Nor should we look only at socialist practice. The societies of the Middle East are filled with immense experiences of communal life. More precisely, humanity lived in communes for millions of years. It is the essence of social life. Philosophies describe this; religions describe this. Zoroastrianism is entirely a social faith. Was Christianity not, in its earliest emergence, a movement of the oppressed? There is a communal essence in Judaism. Communities still living communally in Israel provide examples. Let us look at Islam.


There is an immense sense of sociality. It is immense. Later, the state and various powers took control of many things and corrupted them. But there is undoubtedly a social essence at the core of Islam. Think about it: those whose faith and belief are weak tend toward materialism. Of course, just as there is immense sociality in religions, there is also immense sociality in class struggles.


That culture and spirit of communal life is the greatest source of strength in people. That spiritual strength is also reflected in social life. That is why organization is necessary, consciousness is necessary, and work is necessary. It is not something that will happen spontaneously, because society has been greatly fragmented. Capitalist, colonialist, and genocidal systems around the world are preoccupied with fragmenting society. One of the greatest things they continue to do is distance people from one another, make them apolitical, and turn them into selfish, individualistic people.


So, is a greedy, selfish, individualistic personality who says, ‘Let everything be mine,’ to be preferred? Or is a personality that respects those around them, shares, and shows solidarity to be preferred? One has been shaped by statist and power-oriented influences. The other reflects the character and personality of a democratic, communist society. In the face of such a clear reality, would a person not respect it? Would they not devote their labor to it? Especially today, in the face of a system that both harms nature and stubbornly and persistently seeks to perpetuate a culture of killing and rape against women’s freedom, in the face of the capitalist system, the commune is the only solution.


The commune truly represents women’s freedom, and especially the freedom of society that historically took shape around women as mothers. A society in which women are free is, of course, a communal society. It is based on solidarity, sharing, love, and respect. Women’s will is not excluded there. title: Yapay zeka devlerine ‘rekabet yasasını ihlal’ davası
content:
Fotoğraf: Levart_Photographer/Unsplash

ABD'de dört kişi, Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI ve Google şirketlerinin yapay zeka teknolojilerinin gelişim hızını yavaşlatmak üzere anlaşarak rekabet yasalarını ihlal ettiğini ileri sürerek dava açtı.

California Kuzey Bölgesi Federal Mahkemesinde açılan davada, ChatGPT, Claude, Grok ve Gemini'nin ücretli aboneleri olan dört kişi, şirketlerin yapay zeka teknolojilerinin gelişimini koordineli şekilde yavaşlatma konusunda anlaştığını savundu.

Davacılar, böyle bir anlaşmanın rekabeti sınırlandıracağını ve rekabet yasalarını ihlal edeceğini, aynı zamanda ücretli yapay zeka hizmetlerinden yararlanan tüketicilerin aldıkları hizmetin değerini azaltacağını ileri sürdü.

Davacıların avukatı Nick Rowley, yapay zeka güvenliğine ilişkin kararların teknoloji şirketlerinin kendi aralarında yapacağı anlaşmalara bırakılmaması gerektiğini belirterek, "Yapay zeka güvenliği ve kurallarının, dünyanın en güçlü ve kar amacı güden teknoloji şirketleri arasında kendi çıkarlarına hizmet eden anlaşmalarla belirlenmesine izin verirsek yapay zeka hızla insan kontrolünden çıkabilir" dedi.

ABD'de yapay zekanın yaygınlaşmasıyla birlikte, teknolojinin gelişiminin yavaşlatılmasına yönelik çağrılar son günlerde yoğunlaştı.

Anthropic CEO'su Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO'su Sam Altman ve SpaceXAI CEO'su Elon Musk'ın da aralarında bulunduğu teknoloji sektöründen isimler, yapay zeka geliştirme çalışmalarının yavaşlatılması yönünde çağrı yaptı.

ABD yönetimi ise yapay zekanın geliştirilmesini yavaşlatacak yeni düzenlemeler yerine inovasyonu teşvik eden bir yaklaşım benimsiyor.

ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, yapay zeka teknolojisinin kontrolden çıkması yönünde "hastalıklı bir komplo yürütüldüğünü" ileri sürerken, bu alandaki çalışmaların yavaşlatılmasının Çin'e avantaj sağlayacağını savundu.

title: Sanatçı Müfit Can Saçıntı 'kayyım' şakası sonrası ifadeye çağrıldı
content:
Oyuncu Müfit Can Saçıntı | Fotoğraf: Evrensel

Oyuncu ve yönetmen Müfit Can Saçıntı, temsili Nasreddin Hoca olarak görev aldığı 67. Uluslararası Akşehir Nasreddin Hoca Şenliği kapsamındaki konuşması gerekçe gösterilerek hakkında yapılan suç duyurusu üzerine ifadeye çağrıldı.

Sosyal medya hesabından açıklamada bulunan Saçıntı, şikayetin tören sırasında tepki göstererek alanı terk eden AKP Konya Milletvekili Mehmet Baykan tarafından değil, başka bir şahıs tarafından yapıldığını kaydetti. İlk çağrıda sağlık sorunları sebebiyle gidemediği Kadıköy Rıhtım Polis Karakolu'na daha sonra başvurduğunu belirten oyuncu, ilgili memurun izinli olması nedeniyle ifade işlemlerinin pazartesi gününe kaldığını bildirdi.

Saçıntı, temmuz ayında Akşehir Belediyesi öncülüğünde düzenlenen festivalin göle maya çalma merasimi sırasında kayyım uygulamalarını eleştiren ifadeler kullanmıştı. Konuşmasında "Nasreddin Hoca'nın eşeğine kayyım olarak atandım" diyen Saçıntı, kayyım kavramını yabancı konuklara aktarırken kurduğu evlilik benzetmesiyle dikkat çekmişti.

Açıklamaların ardından etkinliği terk eden AKP Konya Milletvekili Mehmet Baykan, Nasreddin Hoca figürünün siyasi polemiklere alet edilmemesi gerektiğini belirterek söz konusu ifadelerin törenin ruhuyla bağdaşmadığını söylemişti.

title: Avrupa Konseyi Türkiye'den Kavala için somut adım istedi
content:
Avrupa Konseyi Bakanlar Komitesi, Osman Kavala dosyasında Türkiye'ye yeni bir takvim verdi.


Agos'un aktardığına göre Komite, Türkiye'den Kavala'nın serbest bırakılması için atılan ya da planlanan somut adımları 14 Ekim'e kadar bildirmesini istedi.


Karar, Avrupa Konseyi Bakanlar Komitesi'nin Strasbourg'da düzenlenen 1569'uncu İnsan Hakları toplantısında alındı. Avrupa Konseyi'nin resmi takvimine göre toplantı 15-17 Eylül tarihlerinde AİHM kararlarının uygulanmasını denetlemek üzere yapıldı.


Komite, Türkiye'den gelecek bilgilerin ardından Kavala dosyasını 1-3 Aralık'taki İnsan Hakları toplantısında yeniden ele alacak.


Osman Kavala kimdir?


12 Haziran 2024


AİHM: Kavala serbest bırakılmalı


Bakanlar Komitesi'nin kararı, Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi (AİHM) Büyük Dairesi'nin 25 Ağustos'ta verdiği Kavala/Türkiye (No. 2) kararının ardından geldi.


AİHM'nin resmi açıklamasına göre Büyük Daire, Türkiye'nin Kavala'nın mümkün olan en kısa sürede serbest bırakılmasını sağlaması gerektiğine hükmetti. Mahkeme ayrıca Kavala hakkındaki ceza mahkûmiyetinin Avrupa İnsan Hakları Sözleşmesi bakımından "hükümsüz ve geçersiz" kabul edilmesi gerektiğini belirtti.


Dava, AİHM'nin 2019'daki ilk kararının ardından Kavala'nın devam eden tutukluluğu, Gezi davasındaki yargılama ve hakkında verilen ağırlaştırılmış müebbet hapis cezasıyla ilgiliydi.


Büyük Daire; insanlık dışı veya aşağılayıcı muamele yasağı, özgürlük ve güvenlik hakkı, adil yargılanma hakkı, ifade özgürlüğü ile toplantı ve örgütlenme özgürlüğünün de aralarında bulunduğu birden fazla Sözleşme maddesinin ihlal edildiğine karar verdi.


Osman Kavala’nın Gilel Storch Ödülü’nü Ayşe Buğra aldı


15 Eylül 2026


Mahkûmiyetin sonuçlarının da kaldırılması istendi


Bakanlar Komitesi'nin gündeminde yalnızca Kavala'nın cezaevinden çıkarılması bulunmuyor.


Agos'a göre Komite, AİHM'nin mahkûmiyetin Sözleşme hukuku bakımından geçersiz kabul edilmesi gerektiği yönündeki kararı doğrultusunda, mahkûmiyetin diğer sonuçlarının ortadan kaldırılması için alınan ya da planlanan önlemler konusunda da Türkiye'den bilgi istedi.


Türkiye'deki yeniden yargılama yollarının da bu kapsamda değerlendirilmesi bekleniyor.


2019'dan bu yana serbest bırakma çağrısı


AİHM ilk olarak 10 Aralık 2019'da Kavala'nın tutukluluğunun Avrupa İnsan Hakları Sözleşmesi'nin özgürlük ve güvenlik hakkını düzenleyen 5'inci maddesini ve haklara getirilen sınırlamaların amacı dışında kullanılmasını yasaklayan 18'inci maddesini ihlal ettiğine karar verdi.


Mahkeme, Kavala'nın serbest bırakılması için gerekli tedbirlerin alınmasını istedi.


Kavala'nın serbest bırakılmamasının ardından Bakanlar Komitesi Şubat 2022'de Sözleşme'nin 46/4'üncü maddesi kapsamında ihlal prosedürünü işleterek dosyayı yeniden AİHM'ye taşıdı.


AİHM Büyük Dairesi de 11 Temmuz 2022'de Türkiye'nin 2019 tarihli Kavala kararını yerine getirme yükümlülüğünü ihlal ettiğine hükmetti.


Mahkeme, Adalet Bakanlığı’na AİHM’nin Osman Kavala kararını sordu


10 Eylül 2026


Mart 2027'ye kadar eylem planı


Bakanlar Komitesi ayrıca Türkiye'den yalnızca Kavala'ya ilişkin bireysel tedbirleri değil, AİHM kararlarında ortaya konulan daha geniş yapısal sorunları da ele almasını istedi.


Karara göre bunlar arasında makul şüphe bulunmadan tutuklama, ceza ve terörle mücadele mevzuatının uygulanması, ceza hukukunun muhalifler, insan hakları savunucuları ve gazeteciler açısından kullanılması, yargının bağımsızlığı ve tarafsızlığı ile mahkeme kararlarının uygulanması bulunuyor.


Türkiye'nin bu alanlarda atılması planlanan somut adımları içeren yeni eylem planını Mart 2027'ye kadar sunması istendi.


Kavala dosyasında bundan sonraki üç tarih öne çıkıyor: Türkiye'nin somut adımlara ilişkin bilgi vermesi için 14 Ekim, Bakanlar Komitesi'nin dosyayı yeniden ele alacağı 1-3 Aralık 2026 ve yapısal sorunlara ilişkin yeni eylem planı için Mart 2027.

author: Diana Felix da Costa
title: What South Sudan’s mothers teach us about political authority
content:
South Sudan is approaching a critical moment in its

political transition

.

Elections are scheduled for December 2026

, while questions around

constitutional reform, political inclusion

 and the

faltering implementation

 of the

2018 peace agreement

continue to shape debate about the country’s future. As South Sudan considers what legitimate and accountable governance might look like, the experience of a group of mothers and grandmothers in its

eastern borderlands

 offers another place to look for political authority.


‘If you want to kill each other, you must kill us first.’


These were the words of a Murle grandmother describing the message that mothers and grandmothers carried into their communities across

Greater Pibor

 in 2017. Their sons and grandsons were caught in escalating cycles of violence between competing

youth age-sets

 — socially recognised generations of young men. The women responded by deploying not weapons, but

their voices and bodies

: through song, dance, public shaming and, ultimately, the threat of maternal nudity.


Years of conflict and militarisation

 have transformed relations between generations.

Cattle-raiding, revenge killings and child abductions have intensified

 and become increasingly brutal.

Chiefs and elders continue to play important roles

, but the scale and intensity of violence demanded new forms of collective action.


The women formed the

Kabarze

 — translated as ‘the virgins’ or ‘unmarried girls’

 — an evocative name for a movement composed largely of mothers and grandmothers. The name echoed songs and dances traditionally associated with young unmarried women, which the

Kabarze

 drew upon as they confronted violence. As one woman explained: ‘We formed the

Kabarze

 so our children would survive all this fighting. Boys weren’t listening to the old men […] so we formed our group. If they are to beat us, they’ll know we carried them for nine months and gave birth to them.’


Beginning organically in one locality, the movement spread across Greater Pibor as women in other villages established their own

Kabarze

 groups. Moving collectively between the homesteads of armed youth, they sang, danced and confronted those involved in fighting. Their songs identified those

responsible for violence, invited reconciliation and exposed responsibility to public scrutiny

. Their performances interrupted attacks, demanded cattle compensation and compelled young men to surrender weapons. When necessary, the women invoked the powerful moral force of

maternal nudity

, a practice that carried profound significance within Murle society, as in other

African contexts

.


The

Kabarze

drew their authority from motherhood, kinship, collective responsibility and cultural forms of intervention that young men and the wider community already recognised. Their story offers an important lesson about governance itself: where political authority comes from, how it is communicated, and what this could mean for the future of governance and peacebuilding in South Sudan.


Kabarze women performing in Manyirany Payam, Pibor, in October 2017, the year the movement first emerged. Photographs by Diana Felix da Costa.


Where does political authority come from?


South Sudan’s political future continues to be imagined through debates about

constitutional reform, elections, political inclusion and the implementation of peace agreements

. These remain central to both South Sudanese political debate and international engagement. Communities, however, experience governance through a

much broader and tangible landscape of authority.

 Across South Sudan

chiefs, elders, churches, spiritual authorities, kinship networks, clans and sections, age-set hierarchies, youth leaders and women’s collectives all shape social life

. Their legitimacy and influence stem from

long-standing social and spiritual relationships and shared understandings of responsibility, obligation and belonging.


For the

Kabarze

,

motherhood

 connected women to the young men engaged in violence. Acting collectively through shared repertoires of song and dance gave that relationship public and political force their sons and communities understood.


Song

 is central to how women communicate that authority. As one elder woman explained: ‘We women don’t have

rii

 and so to express what we have in mind, we sing.’

[3]


Rii

 are communal spaces

 where men gather to discuss public affairs. Through song …

author: Sicilia Libertaria
title: La punta dell’iceberg
content:
I fatti sono noti ai più: il 19 luglio 2026 Abderrahim Fakir, 42 anni, è stato ammazzato dalla polizia a Bologna. Viveva in Italia da quando aveva sette anni ed era titolare di una ditta di trasporti e facchinaggio. La dinamica dell’uccisione è evidente dai video, la verità davanti ai nostri occhi: legato dai poliziotti con l’ausilio di solerti cittadini, schiacciato e soffocato a morte davanti a numerosi testimoni e agli uomini del 118 che assistono immobili, intimoriti dall’intervenire o forse complici anch’essi.


Il caso è tipico

, nel senso che è uno tra innumerevoli altri più o meno simili tra loro. È emerso, a differenza di tanti rimasti nascosti, grazie ai video e all’indignazione che ha portato una fetta di città in piazza sia il giorno stesso sia in quelli successivi e che si è manifestata anche con qualche tafferuglio, al solito etichettato dai media mainstream come “guerriglia urbana”, ma che è stato un minimo segno simbolico della rabbia che sconvolge i nostri animi.


Questo perché qui nessuno e nessuna si sente al sicuro. Quattro giorni dopo il caso di Fakir, a Cosenza il 25enne Mohamed Amin Bessioud è morto dopo essere precipitato dal balcone della sua abitazione al terzo piano, con le manette ai polsi, durante una perquisizione dei carabinieri. L’omicidio bolognese è accaduto a 25 anni esatti dall’uccisione di Carlo Giuliani a Genova, dalle torture e dalle umiliazioni incancellabili di quei giorni, a loro volta anticipati dalla prova generale della repressione al global forum di Napoli pochi mesi prima. Il centro sinistra apre la strada e la destra prosegue il lavoro, anche in questo campo.


25 anni

 in cui si sono succeduti i morti ammazzati nelle strade, nelle carceri, nei CPR, nei commissariati e nelle caserme. Troppi i nomi:  Federico Aldrovandi, Stefano Cucchi, Giuseppe Uva, Aldo Bianzino, Massimo Casalnuovo, Michele Ferrulli, Dino Budroni, Franco Mastrogiovanni, Andrea Soldi, Riccardo Rassman. ecc. Il collettivo antipsichiatrico Artaud di Pisa in un suo comunicato un mese dopo i fatti ha ricordato ulteriori omicidi provocati dal cosiddetto “contenimento”. Riccardo Magherini morto schiacciato a terra a Firenze nel 2014, soffocato dai carabinieri, mentre chiedeva aiuto, proprio come Fakir; Luigi Marinelli, schiacciato da un ginocchio sulla schiena durante l’intervento della polizia nella sua abitazione a Roma il 5 settembre 2011; Giacomo Zotti, morto a Urago d’Oglio in provincia di Brescia durante un TSO e bloccato dai carabinieri il 26 ottobre 2011; Vincenzo Sapia, soffocato a terra da un carabiniere a Mirto Crosio in provincia di Cosenza il 24 maggio 2014; Andrea Soldi, immobilizzat durante un TSO da tre vigili urbani e uno psichiatra il 5 agosto 2015 a Torino; Arafet Arfaoui, morto a Empoli il 17 gennaio 2019 ammanettato e schiacciato a terra dai carabinieri; Igor Squeo, morto a 33 anni tra l’11 e il 12 giugno 2022 a Milano in seguito a un intervento di polizia e sanitari nel suo appartamento; M.M, soffocata a 39 anni all’interno di una chiesa di Vigevano dopo essere stata ammanettata e bloccata a due vigili urbani il 3 novembre 2023.


Ma l’abuso

 di potere delle divise si consuma ancor di più nei tanti luoghi di reclusione. In carcere sono morte oltre 5.500 persone dal 1992 a oggi di cui circa 2000 per suicidio e circa 3500 per malattia, overdose, omicidio o cause “da accertare”. Nel carcere di S. Anna a Modena nel marzo 2020 la rivolta scoppiata lì come in altri istituti italiani si è conclusa con nove morti, attribuite a un’overdose di farmaci ma le cui reali cause sono evidentemente altre. Nei CPR negli ultimi anni sono decine le persone in regime di detenzione amministrativa (quindi senza condanna penale) deceduti in mezzo al degrado e senza assistenza sanitaria. A oggi non ci sono dati ufficiali e sistemi di rilevazione trasparenti ed efficienti per fare la conta dei morti in questi luoghi.


L’uccisione di Fakir è quindi la punta dell’icebrg di una prassi consolidata e diffusa, che va di pari passo con depistaggi e insabbiamenti. Tutti questi omicidi sono infatti accompagnati e seguiti  da costanti tentativi di occultare la verità, in piena continuità con quanto praticato sai servizi segreti nel lungo periodo della strategia della stagione delle stragi da piazza Fontana del 1969 a inizio anni Novanta. Fakir è stato infatti da subito denigrato in maniera evidentemente razzista da parte dei sindacati della polizia e della stampa, mentre dei due poliziotti ripresi nel video, protetti …

“I don’t like this expression “First World problems.” It is false and it is condescending....
content:
vruba

:


“I don’t like this expression “First World problems.” It is false and it is condescending. Yes, Nigerians struggle with floods or infant mortality. But these same Nigerians also deal with mundane and seemingly luxurious hassles. Connectivity issues on your BlackBerry, cost of car repair, how to sync your iPad, what brand of noodles to buy: Third World problems. All the silly stuff of life doesn’t disappear just because you’re black and live in a poorer country. People in the richer nations need a more robust sense of the lives being lived in the darker nations. Here’s a First World problem: the inability to see that others are as fully complex and as keen on technology and pleasure as you are.”


—

Teju Cole
