author: Unknown
title: Avrupa Konseyi, Demirtaş ve Yüksekdağ için ‘derhal serbest bırakma’ çağrısını yineledi
content:
Avrupa Konseyi Bakanlar Komitesi, 15-16 Eylül’de düzenlenen 1569. İnsan Hakları toplantısında, Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi’nin (AİHM) Selahattin Demirtaş ve Figen Yüksekdağ hakkında verdiği kararların uygulanmasını yeniden ele aldı.


“Selahattin Demirtaş (No. 2)” dava grubu, Komite’nin Türkiye’den incelediği dosyalar arasında yer aldı. Avrupa Konseyi, toplantıya ilişkin açıklamasında Avrupa İnsan Hakları Sözleşmesi’nin (AİHS) 46. maddesi uyarınca AİHM’nin kesinleşmiş kararlarının ilgili devletler açısından bağlayıcı olduğunu hatırlattı. AİHM kararlarının uygulanmasını Bakanlar Komitesi denetliyor.


AİHM’den Selahattin Demirtaş’ın tutukluluğuna dair yeni ihlal kararı


8 Temmuz 2025


“Mevcut tüm imkânlar kullanılsın”


Komite, Türkiye’ye Demirtaş ve Yüksekdağ’ın derhal serbest bırakılmasını sağlamak için “mevcut tüm imkânları” kullanma çağrısını yineledi. Kamuoyunda ‘çerçeve yasa’ olarak bilinen ve 18 Ağustos’ta yürürlüğe giren 7595 sayılı Millî Dayanışma ve Toplumsal Bütünleşmenin Güçlendirilmesine Dair Kanun’un uygulanmasını da bu imkânlar arasında saydı.


Çerçeve yasa Resmi Gazete'de: Kurul, 24 Ağustos'ta toplanacak


18 Ağustos 2026


Türkiye’den Demirtaş dava grubundaki başvurucuların ‘çerçeve yasa’ kapsamına girip girmediğini açıklamasını isteyen Komite, yasanın uygulanma usulü, öngörülen sonuçları ve yürürlüğe giriş sürecine ilişkin bilgi de talep etti.


Komite’nin “Selahattin Demirtaş (No. 2) grubu” adı altında denetlediği dosya, tek bir davadan ya da yalnızca cezaevindeki başvuruculardan oluşmuyor. Grupta Demirtaş hakkında verilen “Demirtaş (No. 2)” ve “Demirtaş (No. 4)” kararlarının yanı sıra “Yüksekdağ ve diğerleri” ile “Tuğluk/Türkiye” kararları bulunuyor. “Yüksekdağ ve diğerleri” kararı 13 başvurucuyu kapsıyor: Figen Yüksekdağ, İdris Baluken, Besime Konca, Abdullah Zeydan, Nihat Akdoğan, Selma Irmak, Ferhat Encü, Gülser Yıldırım, Nursel Aydoğan, Çağlar Demirel, Ayhan Bilgen, Burcu Çelik Özkan ve Leyla Birlik. Demirtaş ve Yüksekdağ dışındaki başvurucuların tamamı tahliye edildi.


Türkiye’nin 22 Temmuz 2026’da Komite’ye sunduğu eylem planına göre, Ankara Bölge Adliye Mahkemesi 22. Ceza Dairesi, Demirtaş ve Yüksekdağ hakkındaki davayı istinafta inceliyor. 


Komite, Türkiye’den diğer başvuruculara ilişkin devam eden yargı süreçleri ve AİHM’nin tespit ettiği ihlallerin sonuçlarını gidermek için aldığı bireysel tedbirler hakkında bilgi istedi.


Süleyman Demirtaş: Türkiye AİHM’ye uysun yeter, gerisini toplum ilmek ilmek işler


25 Ocak 2026


Milletvekillerinin siyasi ifadeleri için güvence istedi


Avrupa Konseyi Bakanlar Komitesi, bireysel tedbirlerin yanı sıra milletvekillerinin siyasi faaliyet ve ifadelerine ilişkin genel önlemleri de ele aldı.


Komite, Türkiye’den milletvekillerinin siyasi ifadelerine yönelik anayasal güvenceleri AİHS ile uyumlu biçimde uygulamasını istedi. Anayasa’nın 83. maddesindeki güvencelerin yanı sıra milletvekillerinin demokratik süreçteki rol ve statülerinin de gözetilmesi gerektiğini vurguladı.


Komite ayrıca Türkiye’den, milletvekillerinin dokunulmazlıklarının kaldırılması için Meclis’e gönderilen fezlekelerin sayısını ve bunların kaçının muhalefet milletvekilleri hakkında olduğunu bildirmesini istedi.


Demirtaş ve Yüksekdağ’a ilişkin bireysel tedbirleri ise Aralık 2026’daki toplantısında yeniden ele alacak.


BÜYÜK DAİRE TAHLİYE KARARINI KESİNLEŞTİRDİ


AİHM Ankara'nın itirazını reddetti: "Demirtaş'ı serbest bırakın"


3 Kasım 2025


Demirtaş ve Yüksekdağ’ın yargı süreci


4 Kasım 2016:

Dönemin Halkların Demokratik Partisi (HDP) Eş Genel Başkanları Selahattin Demirtaş ve Figen Yüksekdağ tutuklandı.


22 Aralık 2020:

 AİHM Büyük Dairesi, Demirtaş (No. 2) kararında ifade özgürlüğü, kişi özgürlüğü ve güvenliği ile serbest seçim hakkı dahil çeşitli hakların ihlal edildiğine hükmetti. Mahkeme, tutukluluğun siyasi çoğulculuğu bastırma ve siyasi tartışma özgürlüğünü sınırlama amacı taşıdığı sonucuna vardı ve Demirtaş’ın derhal serbest bırakılması için gerekli tüm tedbirlerin alınmasını istedi.


8 Kasım 2022:

title: Colloque Martin Luther King à Lyon : 60 ans après Mémoire, transmission et enseignements pour les luttes contemporaines
content:
Il y a soixante ans, le 29 mars 1966, Martin Luther King s'est rendu à Lyon pour participer à une réunion de soutien à son combat pour les droits civiques. Trois mille personnes ont ainsi eu l'occasion d'entendre le pasteur noir d'Atlanta lors de ce rassemblement organisé à la Bourse du Travail, place Guichard.


King a adressé aux lyonnais aux lyonnais.es un message appelant à une mobilisation contre le fléau du racisme et à une solidarité avec le mouvement pour les droits civiques des Noirs américains. Les personnes présentes ont été profondément marquées par cet événement.


Dans le contexte actuel, alors que la plupart des protagonistes de cette rencontre ne sont plus de ce monde, il nous semble important de rappeler que Lyon a accueilli cette figure de la lutte contre le racisme et les discriminations aux États-Unis, porteur d'un message universel, comme en témoigne le Prix Nobel de la Paix qui lui a été attribué en 1964.


Il s'agit par ce colloque, à partir d'un retour historique sur les combats portés par Martin Luther King, de montrer comment il fut un penseur de l'émancipation par-delà les droits civiques et comment son héritage reste toujours bien vivant.


Ces combats nous permettent de comprendre la profondeur historique de la question des inégalités raciales et sociales aux États-Unis et la puissance des résistances populaires non-violentes face à l'injustice.


Enfin, cette journée a l'ambition de montrer comment l'engagement de Martin Luther King et les stratégies d'action non-violentes déployées inspirent aujourd'hui les luttes pour la justice sociale aux États-Unis comme ici en France.


Programme :

9h10 : Mot des représentants institutionnels – Molly Mayfield Barbee (Consule des États-Unis d'Amérique à Lyon), Grégory Doucet, maire de Lyon.


9h20 : “Il y a 60 ans, je me souviens” – Rappel sur la venue de Martin Luther King à Lyon – Christian Delorme


9h35 : Intermède : interprétation de gospels par Matomswé Sabine

KOULI

10h30 : Pause

11h15 : L'influence de

MLK

 lors de la Marche de 1983 – Djamel Attalah


11h30 : Voyage des jeunes de la compagnie Second Souffle aux

USA

 sur les pas de

MLK

 – Azdine Benyoucef et quelques danseurs


12h00 : 13h30 : Déjeuner – Buffet


13h30 : Présentation de l'exposition “Martin Luther King” – Serge Perrin, Marc Ronzière, Gaëlle Dakan


14h00 : Enseignement philosophique de

MLK

 : “Peut-on s'opposer sans se déchirer

 

?” – Marie Grand

 nourrit les luttes actuelles aux États- Unis (Black Lives Matter….) – Henry Cervantes

author: Tainah Ramos
title: Plano climático de Salvador “copia” São Paulo e ignora problemas locais, diz pesquisador
content:
Nesta semana, o rio Tietê, em São Paulo,

transbordou

. A vazão do rio chegou a mais de duas vezes o limite máximo normal, causando alagamentos na capital e no interior.


No

Jardim Pantanal

, bairro historicamente afetado pelas enchentes do Tietê, o alagamento assustou os moradores pela intensidade e velocidade da água, ainda de madrugada. “Veio a chuva que não parou, foi incessante, chuva forte […] e acabou enchendo o rio. O rio transbordar foi até natural, porque foi devagar, mas aí veio a pressão da água, por volta das 6 da manhã, muito rápida […] Parecia uma cachoeira, quem estava andando tinha que estar apoiado em alguém pra não ser levado pela água. Foi uma correria, uma gritaria, para tirar os carros e depois, tirar os móveis”, conta o morador do bairro desde 1994 e jornalista Rafael Tavares.


Os alagamentos em São Paulo, apesar de serem um problema histórico, têm se intensificado devido às mudanças climáticas e falta de adaptação das cidades. “É a primeira vez que acontece isso em setembro. Normalmente, acontece no final de dezembro, janeiro, fevereiro, raramente em março, mas em setembro é a primeira vez”, relembra Tavares.


Moradores dos bairros Jardim Helena e Jardim Pantanal, na periferia da capital paulista, convivem com histórico de enchentes


Apesar da gravidade do problema, a

Agência Pública

 apurou que o plano de ação climática da cidade, que tem orientações de como o poder público deve agir para proteger a população, ainda tem metas genéricas de ação. E pior: está sendo usado quase como um copia e cola para outra capital, Salvador, na Bahia.


Leia o plano de ação climática de São Paulo

aqui

aqui

.


Segundo a

Pública

São produções alinhadas a métricas globais e financeirizadas voltadas a agentes externos, e não para a população local.


Essas são as críticas do professor e pesquisador da Universidade Federal da Bahia (UFBA) Paulo Zangalli, líder do Grupo de Pesquisa Colapso – Natureza e Sociedade e membro do Conselho Deliberativo da Associação Brasileira de Climatologia. Zangalli pesquisa o capitalismo climático e como a agenda climática foi incorporada a práticas nada igualitárias, como especulação imobiliária e gentrificação do espaço urbano.


Segundo o pesquisador, o plano de Salvador inclui as mesmas diretrizes padronizadas do de São Paulo.


“Nos dois planos, há apenas o retrofit de prédios antigos como diretriz de uso do solo para redução de vulnerabilidade. O princípio em si não é um problema se pegássemos os edifícios que tenham possibilidade de serem recuperados, por exemplo, […] retirando as pessoas das áreas de risco e inserindo em uma área com valor e algum tipo de sociabilidade e proximidade aos locais de trabalho. Mas, na prática, tanto em São Paulo quanto em Salvador, isso significa que vamos usar o clima para fazer retrofit de prédio antigo, recuperá-los, torná-los energeticamente mais eficientes, colocar aproveitamento de água da chuva e outras soluções – que inclusive estão nas políticas e nas ações do plano, como desconto no IPTU – e expulsar as pessoas que moram ali e são indesejadas do ponto de vista da incorporação imobiliária”, explica.


Zangalli participou do Plano de Mitigação e Adaptação para Mudança Clima da capital baiana, cuja versão final é de novembro de 2020, e relata o esvaziamento da participação da sociedade, desde reuniões online com microfone silenciado. “Na verdade, fomos usados para validação dos documentos que vinham sendo produzidos por esse consórcio estranho ao território.”


Para ele, o documento revelou também falta de vontade de fazer mudanças estruturais. A adaptação – que tem impacto real na vida da população – foi tímida e sequer tinha financiamento garantido, dependendo de ativos do mercado financeiro.

title: Outcry over statute of limitations ruling in Rıdvan Karakoç case
content:
Rıdvan Karakoç disappeared after being taken into custody on 15 February 1995. His body was found around three months later at the Altınşehir Cemetery for the Unclaimed and was identified by his family.


A statement was issued outside the Istanbul Anatolian Courthouse, calling for the investigation to continue and for those responsible to be brought to justice.


Oya Ersoy, Co-Chair of the Human Rights Association (IHD), said the autopsy report indicated that Karakoç’s death bore signs of violence and torture.


Ersoy said that although Karakoç’s clothes had been registered as evidence in the case, they were never examined or subjected to DNA analysis. She added that witnesses identified by the family had provided important information concerning Karakoç’s enforced disappearance in custody.


The IHD said enforced disappearance is a continuing offence and that statutes of limitations cannot apply to crimes against humanity, announcing that it would appeal the decision. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the association said it would take the case to the Constitutional Court and the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR).


Karakoç’s brother, Hasan Karakoç, said the case had remained unresolved for 31 years and called for the witnesses and police officers serving at the time to be investigated. He criticised the use of the statute of limitations as grounds for closing the case.

title: Amed march calls for status and education rights for Kurdish
content:
A march calling for education in the mother tongue was organised in Amed under the leadership of the Mesopotamia Language and Culture Research Association (MED-DER). Representatives of political parties and civil society organisations, along with many residents, joined the march from NCity shopping centre to Koşuyolu Park.


Participants carried a banner in Kirmanckî and Kurmancî reading “Status for Kurdish, education in Kurdish” (“Statuya Kurdî, perwerdehiya bi Kurdî”), as well as placards bearing the message “Education in the mother tongue is a fundamental right” (“Perwerdehiya bi zimanê dayikê mafekî bingehîn e”). The crowd marched to Kurdish songs and chanted slogans including “There is no life without language” (“Bê ziman jiyan nabe”), “Our language is our existence” (“Zimanê me hebûna me ye”), “Bê Serok Apo” and “Woman, Life, Freedom, freedom for Öcalan” (“Jin, jiyan, azadî, azad bike Rêbertî”).


Demand for status for Kurdish and the right to education


A statement was issued in front of the Human Rights Monument at Koşuyolu Park at the end of the march. MED-DER executive Şükran Yakut said that although the new academic year had begun, Kurdish children continued to be denied the right to education in their mother tongue.


Yakut said the Kurdish people are demanding official status for their language and the right to education in their mother tongue, describing Kurdish as “a vast repository of memory” and one of the fundamental elements of identity. She warned that assimilation policies were endangering the transmission of Kurdish to new generations and said recognition of the language and the right to education in Kurdish should no longer be delayed.


Yakut said, “Kurdish is our future,” and adding that one of the Kurdish people’s broadest demands is for the Kurdish language to be protected, developed and more widely used.


Elective courses are not enough


Yakut said elective courses alone were not sufficient for Kurdish-language education. She said, “As a people, we want education in Kurdish from primary school through to university.”


Yakut stressed that recognition of Kurdish and the right to education in the language are among the fundamental elements of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, adding that language rights are universal rights.


Yakut said the “century-long policy of assimilation” must be abandoned. She added that elective Kurdish courses could be regarded as a starting point, but were insufficient to ensure the language’s survival and development and safeguard its transmission from one generation to the next.


Support for Kurdish-language education in Rojava


Şükran Yakut said the steps taken by Syria’s transitional government in the field of education threaten the gains achieved by Kurds in Rojava, where Kurdish-language education has been provided at different levels for the past 14 years.


Yakut said this experience had produced important results and stressed that they rejected any approach that treated Kurdish merely as part of a folkloric heritage or confined its teaching to a symbolic number of hours.


Yakut expressed support for the ongoing struggle for Kurdish-language education in Rojava and said: “Official status for Kurdish and education in Kurdish are at the heart of our struggle.”


Kurdish must become a main language of public life


Yakut said Kurdish language and democratic institutions would intensify their efforts to protect, develop and expand the use of Kurdish, with the aim of increasing its presence in public life.


Yakut said that, in line with the decisions of the Kurdish Language Conference, they aim to make Kurdish one of the founding pillars of democratic national will and to establish a public sphere for the Kurdish language.


Kurdish must be recognised for a dignified peace


Serhat Eren, Amed MP for the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), said Kurds in Rojava and Northern Kurdistan (Bakur) want Kurdish to be a language of education.


Eren said a dignified peace would not be possible without recognition of the Kurdish language and stressed that the right to education in Kurdish must be constitutionally guaranteed.


Eren said, “Either the constitution must be amended during this process or a new constitution must be adopted. The existence of every language must be recognised in the constitution.”

author: Unknown
title: What does Alevi history tell us?
content:
A debate sparked by a declaration signed by 53 Alevi intellectuals and writers has once again raised the question of how Alevi history should be understood. Rather than carrying the hostilities of the past into the present, there is a need to reconsider the Alevi understanding of truth, justice, consent and humanity.


The debate sparked by the declaration signed by 53 Alevi intellectuals and writers has once again brought the question of how Alevi history should be approached in Turkey to the forefront. On one side are references to the historical memory of Alevis through Sultan Selim I and Idris-i Bitlisi; on the other is a broader reading of Alevi history extending from Shah Ismail Hatayi and Pir Sultan Abdal to Bedreddin and Seyit Rıza.


Reducing the issue to a debate over “Sultan Selim or Shah Ismail?” overlooks the much broader social and spiritual heritage of Alevi history. Alevi history is not merely a history of sultans, wars and struggles for power. Alevi spiritual lineages, cem (Alevi communal worship ceremony), deyiş (Alevi devotional song), women, exiles, massacres and resistance are also part of this history. Running through all of them is a powerful search for truth that has been passed down from generation to generation.


The question of what Alevis have struggled against throughout history and what kind of life they have sought to defend is important for understanding the shared values that connect different periods. Tracing these values leads us first and foremost to the human being.


The first word of Alevi memory: The human being


One of the strongest currents in Alevi thought places the human being at its centre. Mansur al-Hallaj’s words “Ana al-Haqq” (“I am the Truth”), Seyyid Nesimi’s life sacrificed in pursuit of truth, Hacı Bektaş Veli’s human-centred teachings, the words of Kaygusuz Abdal and Yunus Emre’s love of humanity all bear traces of a common intellectual tradition stretching across different periods to the present day.


The flaying of Nesimi is remembered in Alevi memory as more than a story of torture; it also represents the price that words and ideas have paid in the face of power. The maxim “Even if you are hurt, do not hurt others” belongs to the same moral world.


Alevi teachings regard the human being as a “can”, a soul or living being. A person’s language, faith, identity or origin does not determine their worth. This perspective takes on even greater significance in periods when war, hostility and social polarisation are turned into instruments of politics. There is a clear contradiction between an understanding that regards every human being as a “can” and a politics that sets communities against one another on the basis of identity.


Karbala is not merely the past


Karbala holds a very special place in Alevi memory. The killing of Imam Hussein is not remembered simply as a historical event that occurred centuries ago and was left in the past. The story of Karbala has been passed down from generation to generation as a lesson in refusing to submit to oppression, standing with the oppressed and rejecting the idea that political power determines what is true and just.


The works of poets such as Fuzuli, Yemini and Virani have also played an important role in preserving and transmitting this memory. In the story of Karbala, what matters is not so much who the oppressor is, but where one stands in the face of oppression. Times, rulers and names change, but the principle of resisting oppression continues to live on in Alevi memory.


Turning Karbala into an instrument for creating new hostilities among today’s peoples or faiths also contradicts this memory. The legacy of Karbala is not about reproducing a conflict from the past, but about the position one takes in the face of injustice.


Hatayi: Ruler and poet


Shah Ismail Hatayi occupies a particular place in the current debate. Treating Hatayi solely as a Safavid ruler leaves out a significant part of his place in Alevi memory. At the same time, separating him entirely from the political and military conflicts of his era would leave the historical picture incomplete.


Shah Ismail ruled amid the harsh political conditions of the 16th century, fought in wars and governed a state. The poetry he wrote under the pen name Hatayi, however, followed a different path from his political identity and has continued to live on within Alevi-Bektashi culture.


For an Alevi who reads Hatayi’s deyiş poems today or hears them …

author: Unknown
title: Kurt: Families of different faiths united in mourning
content:
The Kurdish Freedom Movement has announced the names of guerrillas whose martyrdoms could not be made public in previous years because of wartime conditions. Following the announcements, collective condolences and commemorations were held in many cities across Kurdistan and Turkey.


Ilhami Kurt, Co-Chair of the Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture for Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilisations (MEBYA-DER), has been informing families in Istanbul of the martyrdoms and helping organise condolences and commemorations. Kurt spoke to ANF about the process of contacting the families and what lies ahead.


More than 100 martyrs have been announced in Istanbul


Kurt said that the number of martyrs announced in Istanbul has exceeded 100: “I offer my condolences to all our people, to the families of our martyred comrades and to their mothers. Announcements were first made for Istanbul’s first and third districts, followed by the second district. More than 100 martyrs were announced. Together with all our institutions, we visited the families and established contact with them. As the process was also being covered in the press, we stood by our families.”


Kurt said that since the beginning of the process, families have been applying particularly to MEBYA-DER in the hope of receiving news about their children. He continued: “The condolence process has been continuing for around a month. Since the peace/solution process began, families have been applying through the party, MEBYA-DER, other institutions and lawyers in the hope of hearing their children’s voices or at least seeing a gravestone. One family who came to us said they wanted to hear their child’s voice, see a photograph or receive some news. The following day, we learned from the press that the comrade had been martyred, and it was extremely difficult for us to share that news with the family. The families are grieving, mourning their loved ones and holding condolences, but they have shown that they believe the path taken was the right one and that they stand by the martyrs.”


Families of different faiths came together under one roof


Kurt said they had initially been unsure how families would respond to the decision to hold joint condolences, but the families embraced the initiative. He said they stood together with Alevi, Sunni and families of different faiths.


Kurt also said: “We initially thought this would be the most difficult issue because the families came from different cities, such as Diyarbakır (Amed) and Bitlis (Bedlîs), and had different faiths and cultural backgrounds, including Alevi and Sunni. However, the families came together under one roof and reached a common decision. Condolences for both Alevi and Sunni comrades were held in the same place, and the families showed that they were companions on the same path, without making any distinction. All institutions and socialist parties gathered around the same condolence table. This is an important achievement made possible by collective organisation.”


Families seeking their children’s remains can apply to MEBYA-DER


Kurt also discussed the process that will follow the condolences, saying that families now want to reach their children’s graves and that efforts will be made towards this goal.


Kurt continued: “Even though the condolences have ended and the families have returned home, this is not an end but a new beginning. All the families of the martyrs are waiting and want to reach their children’s graves. The next stage will involve identifying these graves, gathering the available information and sharing it with the families. The families will not wait passively at home; they will come together even more strongly and work to find their children’s remains and graves.


Families will apply to us, political parties and relevant non-governmental organisations. MEBYA-DER is the most appropriate central point of contact in this process. Applications will be made through MEBYA-DER, DNA tests will be requested through lawyers, and legal efforts will be pursued regarding places where martyrs lost their lives in different regions, including Rojava.”

title: Sarıtaş: Process must advance towards a democratic republic
content:
Political scientist Mehmet Zahir Sarıtaş said the Democratic Society and Peace Process, which has been under way for nearly two years, has created an important platform for discussion on resolving the Kurdish question. He said a lasting solution depends on establishing a new political and social framework based on freedom, human rights, justice and equality. Sarıtaş noted that the abandonment of the strategy of armed struggle has placed democratic politics at the centre, stressing that the state must respond by changing and transforming its own approach.


Sarıtaş said discussions on resolving the Kurdish question cannot be confined to ending the conflict. He noted that both the debates that have emerged over the course of the Kurdish struggle during the past 50 years and the universal values developed around democracy and democratic society across the world provide an important framework for a solution. He said the fundamental question is whether these values will be taken as the basis of the current process.


Sarıtaş stressed that universal values must be embraced in order to build democratic governance and a democratic society. He said the emergence of the Kurdish question itself is linked to the failure to adequately uphold these values in relations between the state and society. Freedom, justice and equality, he added, are fundamental conditions for societies to live together. In their absence, social problems remain unresolved and relations between the state and society become a source of conflict.


Sarıtaş drew attention to the relationship between freedom, human rights, justice and equality and said: “Without freedoms, there can be no human rights; without the recognition and protection of human rights, there can be no justice; and without justice, there can be no equality.”


These values are not specific to the Kurdish question but are universal principles relevant to all societies, Sarıtaş said. He added that the central issue is whether the state will make these values the fundamental criteria for a solution. Democracy cannot be considered separately from these principles, he stressed, adding that democratic mechanisms must function if societies are to resolve their own problems. Sarıtaş highlighted the direct relationship between resolving the Kurdish question and democratisation, stressing that democratisation forms the fundamental basis for a solution to the Kurdish question.


The solution must be legally guaranteed


Sarıtaş stressed that a solution must not be limited to declarations of political intent and said relations between the state and society need to be rebuilt on the basis of a new social contract. He noted that a democratic constitution would provide the legal guarantee for this relationship and continued: “Accepting this approach is not enough; it must be given legal guarantees. There needs to be a social contract consistent with this approach. In the modern era, that means a democratic constitution. The Peace and Democratic Society Process must therefore reach a solution based on these universal values and the discussions that have emerged through the Kurdish struggle.”


Sarıtaş also stressed that resolving the Kurdish question cannot be separated from the process of democratisation and said: “Genuine democracy can only be achieved if the Kurdish question is approached on the basis of justice, freedom and equality, and the Kurdish question itself can only be resolved on the basis of genuine democracy.”


Öcalan’s framework shows the path to a democratic solution


Sarıtaş said Abdullah Öcalan’s approach to the process is not limited to ending the armed struggle but also sets out the political basis on which the next phase should proceed. He explained Öcalan’s perspective on a solution and its significance today as follows: “Abdullah Öcalan made clear at the beginning of the process that the strategy of armed struggle had been abandoned. At the same time, a strategy centred on democratic politics was adopted. This was put into effect with the dissolution of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). From now on, the strategy is based on democratic politics. Mr. Öcalan is proposing an approach aimed at establishing a strategic partnership with Turkey on the basis of freedom and equality. The conceptual and theoretical framework he has put forward is highly significant. It includes the concepts of democratic nation, democratic integration, democratic constitution and democratic republic. Each …

title: Cumartesi Anneleri’nin 1121'inci hafta eylemi: Cemil Kırbayır nerede?
content:
Eylem Nazlıer [email protected]

İstanbul - Cumartesi Anneleri/İnsanları, gözaltında kaybettirilen yakınlarının akıbetini sormak ve faillerin yargılanması talebiyle sürdürdükleri eylemlerinin 1121’incisi İstanbul Beyoğlu’nda bulunan Galatasaray Meydanı’nda gerçekleştirdi. Açıklamaya çok sayıda hak savunucusu katıldı. Bu haftaki eylemde gözaltında kaybedilişinin 46. yılında Cemil Kırbayır’ın akıbeti soruldu.

Bir insan gözaltında kaybedildiğinde devletin görevinin, onun akıbetini ortaya çıkarmak, gerçeği araştırmak, sorumluları belirlemek ve adaletin önünü açmak olduğunun altı çizilen açıklamada; “Eğer gözaltında kayıp dosyalarında olduğu gibi etkin soruşturmalar yapılmaz, tanıklar dinlenmez, deliller toplanmaz, sorumlular hesap vermeden yıllar geçirilir ve ardından “zamanaşımı doldu” denilerek dosyalar kapatılırsa, burada yalnızca bir hukuk kuralının uygulanmasından söz edilemez. Bu durum, zamanaşımı kurumunun devletin yıllarca yerine getirmediği soruşturma yükümlülüğünün üzerini örten bir kalkan haline getirilmesidir” denildi.

Zamanın kalkan olarak kullanıldığı örneklerden birinin de Cemil Kırbayır olduğu vurgulanan açıklamada; “26 yaşındaki Kars Eğitim Enstitüsü öğrencisi Cemil Kırbayır, 13 Eylül 1980 tarihinde Ardahan’ın Okçu Köyü’ndeki evinden güvenlik güçleri tarafından gözaltına alındı. Önce Göle’deki 247. Piyade Alayı’na götürüldü ve burada yaklaşık bir hafta tutuldu. Ardından Kars Emniyet Müdürlüğü’ne, oradan da gözetimevi olarak kullanılan Kars Eğitim Enstitüsü’ne sevk edildi. Ailesi, Cemil’in gözaltında tutulduğu süre boyunca onu görebilmek ve ihtiyaçlarını karşılayabilmek için bu merkezlere gidip geldi. Ancak 8 Ekim’den sonra gittiklerinde, “Oğlunuz firar etti, bir daha onu sormaya gelmeyin.” cevabını aldılar. O günden sonra Cemil’den bir daha haber alınamadı” ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Baba İsmail Kırbayır’ın ve Türkiye Barolar Birliği’nin yaptığı suç duyurularının sonuçsuz bırakıldığı, devletin, Cemil’in akıbetini ortaya çıkarmak için etkili bir soruşturma yürütmediği ifade edilen açıklamada şunlar söylendi; “Kırbayır Ailesi Cemil’i aramaktan vazgeçmedi. Cemil’in annesi Berfo Kırbayır, oğlunun akıbetini öğrenebilmek için yıllarca mücadele etti. 5 Şubat 2011 tarihinde, dönemin Başbakanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan ile Dolmabahçe Sarayı’nda görüşen 103 yaşındaki Berfo Anne, yaşadıklarını anlattı ve tek bir talepte bulundu: ‘Ben ölmeden oğlumu bul.’”

Bu buluşmanın ardından Meclis Araştırma Komisyonunun kurulduğu, komisyonun, döneme ilişkin belgelere ulaştığı belirtilan açıklamada; “Cemil Kırbayır’ı sorguda gören tanıklarla, sorgulamayı yapan emniyet ve MİT mensuplarıyla görüştü.Titiz bir çalışmanın ardından 350 sayfalık bir rapor hazırlandı. Raporda, Cemil Kırbayır’ın gözaltında işkence sonucu hayatını kaybettiği ve bedeninin, ölümüne sebebiyet veren kamu görevlilerince ortadan kaldırıldığı tespit edildi. Böylece Cemil Kırbayır’ın gözaltında kaybedildiği, devletin kendi kurduğu Meclis Araştırma Komisyonu tarafından ortaya konuldu.

Komisyonun Kars Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’na suç duyurusunda bulunduğu ve dosyanın yeniden açıldığının altı çizilen açıklamada; “Tam da burada, hakikate ve adalete ulaşma umudu yeniden doğmuşken, devletin cezasızlık pratiği bir kez daha devreye girdi. Uzun bir belirsizlik döneminin ardından, 25 Şubat 2020 tarihinde Adalet Bakanlığı Yargıtay’a başvurarak dosyada zamanaşımı bakımından “kanun yararına bozma” kararı verilmesini talep etti. Yargıtay 8. Ceza Dairesi bu talebi kabul etti. Böylece Cemil Kırbayır’ın kaybedilmesine ilişkin ceza soruşturmasının önü zamanaşımı gerekçesiyle kesildi. Oysa devletin görevi, kendi ihmalleri nedeniyle geçen zamanı gerekçe göstererek adaletten vazgeçmek değil; etkili soruşturma yükümlülüğünü yerine getirmektir” diye belirtildi.

Gözaltında kaybetme suçunda zamanaşımının işletilemeyeceği vurgusu yapılan açıklamada şu ifadelere yer verildi; “Devletin etkin soruşturma yapma yükümlülüğünü yerine getirmeyip yıllarca dosyaları sürüncemede bırakması, ardından “zamanaşımı doldu” diyerek soruşturma ve kovuşturmaları kapatması yalnızca bir usul sorunu değildir. Bu, hukukun inkârıdır. Cezasızlığın kurumsallaştırılmasıdır. Cemil Kırbayır’ın akıbeti açıklanana, onu gözaltında kaybedenler yargılanana kadar, Berfo Annemizin bıraktığı yerden sormaya devam edeceğiz: Cemil Kırbayır nerede? Cemil’i kaybedenler neden korunuyor? Kaç yıl geçerse geçsin; Cemil Kırbayır için, tüm kayıplarımız için, adalet istemekten ve devletin hukuk normları içinde hareket etmek zorunda olduğunu …

author: Unknown
title: Aydın'da mera maden sahası açıldı: 3 bin hayvan merasız kalacak
content:
Aydın’ın Karpuzlu ilçesine bağlı Ömerler Mahallesi’nde Dinçler Madencilik A.Ş. tarafından işletilmek istenen feldspat ocağı ve kırma-eleme tesisi kapasite artışı projesine ÇED olumlu kararı verildi.

25,2 hektarlık ruhsat sahasına sahip projenin 12,76 hektarlık ÇED alanında yürütülmesi planlanıyor. Aydın-Muğla-Denizli Planlama Bölgesi 1/100.000 ölçekli Çevre Düzeni Planı’nda mera ve kısmen sulama alanı olarak görünen bölgenin kullanım amacı, İl Mera Komisyonu kararı ve Valilik oluru ile değiştirildi.

Bu değişiklikle köylülerin ortak kullanımındaki yaklaşık 1200 dönümlük mera alanı maden faaliyetlerine açılmış oldu. Köyde 3 binin üzerinde hayvan bulunduğunu belirten yöre halkı, meranın kaybedilmesinin hayvancılığı doğrudan etkileyeceğini söylüyor.

Proje Tanıtım Dosyası’ndaki bilgilere göre maden sahası Ömerler Mahallesi merkezinin yaklaşık 1 kilometre kuzeyinde bulunuyor. En yakın konutun maden alanına uzaklığı ise 300 metre.

Proje alanına en yakın mezarlık 300, cami 500, okul ise 650 metre mesafede. Tarımsal sulama açısından önem taşıyan Karpuzlu Sulaması ana kanalına 20 metre çekme mesafesi bırakıldığı belirtiliyor. En yakın zeytinlik alanın uzaklığı ise 445 metre olarak veriliyor.

Maden faaliyetinin yaratacağı toz ve gürültünün tarım alanları, zeytinlikler ve su kaynakları üzerindeki etkileri ise yöre halkının temel itirazları arasında.

Projenin ekosistem üzerindeki etkileri konusunda hazırlanan raporlarda da farklı değerlendirmeler bulunuyor.

Bölgeye özgü endemik bitki türlerinden gargan otunun madencilik faaliyetleri nedeniyle yok olma tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya kalabileceği belirtiliyor. Şirket tarafından hazırlatılan Ekosistem Değerlendirme Raporu’nda ise proje alanında 27 familyaya ait 41 bitki türü tespit edildiği, ancak nadir, endemik ya da koruma altındaki türlere rastlanmadığı savunuluyor.

Köylüler ve çevre örgütleri ise maden faaliyetinin yalnızca belirli türler üzerindeki etkisiyle sınırlı değerlendirilemeyeceğini, mera ve tarım alanlarının bir bütün olarak ekolojik ve ekonomik işlevinin göz önünde bulundurulması gerektiğini belirtiyor.

Ömerler Mahallesi sakinleri, meranın maden sahasına dönüştürülmesinin bölgede hayvancılığı tehdit ettiğini ifade ediyor. Köylüler, 3 binin üzerinde hayvanın bulunduğu bölgede ortak meranın kaybedilmesiyle hayvancılığın sürdürülemez hale geleceğini belirtiyor.

Madenden kaynaklanacak tozun zeytinliklere ve tarım ürünlerine zarar vereceğini dile getiren yöre halkı, hava kirliliğinin sağlık açısından da risk oluşturabileceği endişesini taşıyor.

Proje kapsamında yalnızca 12 kişinin istihdam edileceğinin belirtilmesi de köylülerin tepkisini artırıyor. Yöre halkı, binlerce hayvanın beslendiği meranın madenciliğe açılmasına karşılık yaratılacağı belirtilen sınırlı istihdamın bölge ekonomisi açısından bir karşılık oluşturmadığını savunuyor.

Projenin geçmişinde daha önce verilmiş bir yargı kararı da bulunuyor. Aydın Valiliğinin proje için verdiği “ÇED gerekli değildir” kararına karşı Ömerler köylüleri ve çevre örgütleri tarafından dava açılmıştı.

Aydın 1. İdare Mahkemesi, bilirkişi keşif raporunu esas alarak söz konusu kararı iptal etmiş ve projenin önünü kapatmıştı.

Ancak şirketin projeden vazgeçmek yerine ÇED sürecini yeniden başlatmasıyla süreç tekrar gündeme geldi. Yeni süreçte proje için ÇED olumlu kararı verilirken, köylülerin ve çevre örgütlerinin maden faaliyetine karşı mücadelesi de yeniden başladı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: groundxero
title: Activists Targeted in Mumbai Over Kites Flown in Solidarity with Children in Gaza
content:
Kites flown by activists in solidarity with Palestinian children in Gaza have become the latest reason for police crackdown in Mumbai.


 


Groundxero Desk


19 SEP 2026


 


Even as the government of India under Narendra Modi publicly supports

Palestinian sovereign statehood

 and calls for an immediate halt to violence and forced displacements in Gaza, the BJP ruled state governments across the country are criminalizing acts of solidarity to Palestine.


 


The Mumbai Police allegedly raided a woman activist’s home and detained two other after they participated in a global kite-flying campaign in solidarity with Gaza’s children, This came days after India hosted a BRICS summit that reaffirmed support for Palestinian statehood and opposed the forced displacement of Palestinians.


 


The Indian People in Solidarity with Palestine (IPSP) has alleged that Mumbai Police on Friday riaded the home of a pro-Palestine and IPSP activist, Harshada Borade — a student and an artist — for flying kites in solidarity with Palestinian children, as part of the Global Gaza Kite Weekend 2026. The organisation said plainclothes police personnel entered the home of the volunteer, Harshada, and subsequently conducted a search without producing a warrant, written notice or other authorisation.


 


The search continued for more than 9 hours, and the police officials only left the premises after 2:30 AM on September 19, Saturday. In the ensuing period, they searched and photographed her books and literature, posters, and personal belongings.


 


“More than nine hours – and counting – for ‘searching’ a person’s place of residence

without a warrant

 merely for flying kites in solidarity with Palestinian children!” the Palestine solidarity group said in a social media post on Saturday.


 


According to IPSP, earlier in the week, Mumbai Police had identified two other volunteers who had participated in IPSP’s Kite Campaign, harassed them and forced them into “complying” with their demands, without providing any notice stating the said need for compliance. They also used intimidation tactics to threaten them and their families.


 


As per the panchnama, the action was undertaken in response to a September 15 pro-Palestine Kite campaign that Harshada had participated in, which the police referred to as a “protest”. Among the list of items found inside the house, as per the panchnama, were books and quotations by Bhagat Singh and Savitribai Phule. The panchnama also states that the search was authorised by senior police officials only after the police personnel found Harshada’s behavior to be “suspicious” in nature.


 


The crackdown came days after activists across the world participated in the Global Gaza Kite Weekend, a campaign intended to express solidarity with children in Gaza. The global campaign followed Israeli warnings over kites and balloons being flown by children from Gaza. The Israeli military has said that it would treat kites and balloons flown from Gaza as a security threat on par with drones and act accordingly.


 


The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry has documented the enormous toll of the Israeli military assault on Palestinian children in Gaza. Its June 2026 report recorded at least 20,179 Palestinian children killed and 44,143 injured between 7 October 2023 and 7 October 2025. The Commission concluded that Israeli authorities and security forces had deliberately targeted Palestinian children and said such acts formed part of the genocide it had previously found to have been committed by Israel against Palestinians in Gaza.


 


The Mumbai police action on Palestine solidarity activists has acquired a sharper political significance because of the timing.


 


On September 12–13, India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. The New Delhi Declaration, adopted by the BRICS countries, expressed concern over continuing violence in Gaza, called for an end to policies aimed at forcibly displacing Palestinians from Gaza, opposed demographic or geographical changes to the territory, and reaffirmed support for the establishment of a

sovereign, independent and viable State of Palestine

 within the internationally recognised 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital. The declaration also backed Palestine’s full membership of the United Nations.

author: groundxero
title: Quashing the Questions: The Crisis of Press Freedom in Contemporary India
content:
When journalists ask questions to powerful figures, be it from the Congress or AAP or BJP, there is a concerning trend of social or legal backlashes against them for doing their job.


 


Debasree Sarkar 


 


On September 12, 2026, during a press meet held in Lucknow, just as the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Yogi Adityanath, finished his address and walked away from the podium, journalist Divya Srivastava from 4PM News stood up and called out, “Mr. Chief Minister, this is a press conference, and you are not even responding to a question. Why did you call for a press conference? Only, so that we get to hear what you are saying?” But this simple act of ‘questioning’ changed everything. Speaking to

The Pioneer

, journalist Srivastava said she asked questions during the press interaction, after which the Yogi smiled and left. Srivastava can be seen as holding a mobile phone trying to record this face-off herself as CM Adityanath and other BJP leaders begin leaving the stage after addressing a ‘press conference’ on the

Sewa Sankalp Abhiyan

—a month-long itinerary comprising various events chalked out by BJP in states such as Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Haryana, and Assam between September 17 and October 17, marking 25 years of Honourable Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s public life ever since he took oath as the Chief Minister of Gujarat. A Lucknow-based reporter told 

The Wire

, “Usually 

such press conferences

 (emphasis mine) at the party’s office are meant for passing on the government memo with 

reporters hardly asking questions

.” Naturally, Srivastava’s actions marked a separation from the 

general trend of contemporary climate.


 


Srivastava said that while she was leaving, people identifying themselves as Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) supporters began shouting at her and allegedly behaved rudely, including questioning which channel she represented. Srivastava also pointed out that a narrative was being pushed on social media, alleging that she had been sent by the Samajwadi Party or the Congress. Denying these claims, calling herself an independent journalist, Srivastava said the allegations were an attempt to create a false political narrative around her questions. Srivastava alleged that she has since received threats on social media and is now afraid to leave her home. She said her family is also worried, with relatives questioning whether she became a journalist to face such treatment.


 


In an interview with journalist Abhishek Upadhyay, Srivastava said, “When I tried asking a question, the chief minister made a bye-bye gesture and left. Thereafter I was surrounded by BJP workers… alleging that I’m misbehaving. There is a difference between asking questions and misbehaving with someone. I didn’t use any foul language, I just requested the chief minister to respond to my query.” “One BJP member who also happens to be a spokesperson for the party insisted on knowing my name and the channel I worked for. He kept on asking about this 10-12 times during which he forced me to switch off my mobile camera and upon my refusal misbehaved with me,” Srivastava told Upadhyay in the interview. Srivastava also expressed that the experience has made her question whether the spirit of journalism—the freedom to question those in power—is still alive in India, as the controversy has left her wondering whether her years of education in journalism were “a waste of time”!


 


This also reminds us of the press meet of May 2026 in which our Honourable PM Narendra Modi refused to take questions from another brave young journalist, Helle Lyng of Norway, who asked uninhibitedly, “Prime Minister Modi, why don’t you take some questions from the freest press in the world?” Lyng wrote on her X account later that “Norway has the number one spot on the World Press Freedom Index, India is at 157th, competing with Palestine, Emirates & Cuba.” Even during Honourable PM Modi’s visit to New Zealand in July 2026, a Kiwi journalist asked the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) officials why PM Modi did not conduct a press conference or take unscripted questions from the local press during his political visits.


 


Interestingly, even though in the latest report India’s position is undoubtedly deplorable, India has a fascinating history when it comes to press conferences. author: Sebastian Lotzer
title: The Last Day Of Summer – Für Achim [Part lll] To Have Or To Have Not
content:
“Darauf kamen die drei Landesflüchtigen an einem Hof vorbei, da saß auf dem Tor der Haushahn und schrie aus Leibeskräften. ‘Du schreist einem durch Mark und Bein’, sprach der Esel, ‘was hast du vor?’ ‘Da hab ich gutes Wetter prophezeit’, sprach der Hahn, ‘weil unserer lieben Frauen Tag ist, wo sie dem Christkindlein die Hemdchen gewaschen hat und sie trocknen will. Aber weil am Sonntag Gäste kommen, so hat die Hausfrau doch kein Erbarmen und hat der Köchin gesagt, sie wolle mich in der Suppe essen und da solle ich mir heute Abend noch den Kopf abschneiden lassen. Nun schrei ich aus vollem Hals, solang ich noch kann.’ ‘Ei was, du Rotkopf’, sagte der Esel, ‘zieh lieber mit uns fort, wir gehen nach Bremen, etwas Besseres als den Tod findest du überall. Du hast eine gute Stimme, und wenn wir zusammen musizieren, so wäre dies wohl fantastisch.‘ Der Hahn ließ sich den Vorschlag gefallen und sie gingen alle zusammen fort.”


Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten


„Es ist nicht das Bewusstsein der Menschen, das ihr Sein, sondern umgekehrt ihr gesellschaftliches Sein, das ihr Bewusstsein bestimmt.“


Karl Marx – Zur Kritik der Politischen Ökonomie


Nun also zwei Jahre. 671 Tage. So viele Stunden. Keine Nachrichten mehr mitten in der Nacht von dir, keine seitenlange Zitate, keine abenteuerlichen, betörenden Ausführungen. Nichts. Nur die Stille. Die Stille deiner Abwesenheit. Diese schreckliche Stille, in der alle einfach irgendwas daherreden, ohne dass es wirklich etwas zu bedeuten hätte. Du findest keine drei Zeilen mehr, die es wirklich wert sind, gelesen zu werden. Jedenfalls in diesem Land. Am Ende machen sie selbst im Goldenen Hahn Wahlkampf für die Tiktok Linke. Gut, dass Bernd Kramer das nicht mehr erleben muss. Überhaupt, du und all die anderen, die uns wirklich etwas zu sagen hatten. Die Ihr nicht mehr da seid. Pohrt wurde auch erst wirklich geliebt, als er schon tot war. Der ‘Brother in Crime’. Eigentlich war ja schon seit dem Corona Ausnahmezustand da dieses Schweigen, das zur Akklamation mutierte, nur so Wenige, die begriffen und benannten, wie dieses Generalstabsmanöver die Permanenz des generalisierten Ausnahmezustand vorwegnahm. Die neue Weltordnung, die diesmal praktisch niemand framte. Und auch hier wieder, die Einschränkung: In diesem Lande. Und nun kommen sie nicht mehr heraus aus dem Loch, in dem sie sich selber eingebuddelt haben, die sozialen Verhältnisse schreien nach Revolte und zähen Widerstand, Krieg, Inflation, Überwachungsstaat, ein korrupte Politikerkaste deren Halbwertszeit in den verantwortlichen Posten nicht mal mehr eine Legislaturperiode beträgt. Alle sehen es: “Der Kaiser ist nackt”. Ein System am Abgrund, im Sommer brennen die Wälder im Süden Europas, während hier die Alten und Kranken auf Intensivstationen und in Pflegeheimen in der Hitze einfach krepieren, weil es keine Klimaanlagen gibt. Und nun, da alles Gesellschaftliche reif ist für die Umwälzung, hängen die Linken in ihren Blasen, unfähig zum Diskurs, die Grabenkriege untereinander sind das einzige, was dem Kadaver noch Leben einhaucht. Und die rechten Populisten fischen die Wut und Ohnmacht ab.


Ich kann mich noch erinnern, als wir uns das erste Mal getroffen haben. Muss vor einem guten Jahrzehnt gewesen sein. Du hast mit Frankfurter Genossen u.a. eure Thesen zur generellen Tendenz der staatlichen Faschisierung vorgestellt im Mehringhof in Kreuzberg und ich habe widersprochen und fand, dass das nicht die damalige Entwicklung auf den Punkt brachte. Aber du hast Recht gehabt, du hast früher begriffen, wohin die Reise geht. Dann habe ich einen kurzen Beitrag, ‘Schanzenblues’ [1], für das Buch [2] nach den G 20 Riots in Hamburg beigetragen, das du u.a. mit Dellwo herausgebracht hast. Da wurden wir dann eingeladen nach Friedrichshain zu irgendwelchen “Widerständigen Tagen” (ich kann mich beim besten Willen nicht mehr an den genauen Titel erinnern), der Saal war rappelvoll, wir haben was vorgetragen und dann gab es Fragen und Diskussion. Das war, als wenn sich Menschen aus völlig fremden Kulturen begegneten, es war schwierig, überhaupt eine gemeinsame Sprache zwischen dem Podium und dem Saal zu finden: Die Abgründe waren schon da so tief und eigentlich nicht mehr zu überwinden, wir redeten eigentlich die ganzen Zeit aneinander vorbei. Dann haben wir uns lange nicht gesehen, aber immer mehr ausgetauscht, der Corona Ausnahmezustand hat uns natürlich nochmal enger zueinander gebracht, auch wenn das eine Zuneigung auf räumliche Distanz war …

author: Evanilton Gonçalves
title: Tudo parece tão calmo
content:
Nestes tempos de velocidade e de acúmulo de carros nas ruas, abri a janela de casa e observei um estranho silêncio no centro de Salvador. Eu nunca havia visto algo assim. O vento parecia ter sumido junto com as pessoas. No canto de uma praça que não existe mais, a árvore que costuma dançar majestosa estava imóvel. Dentro dela, entre seus galhos cheios de folhas, vi pássaros inquietos. O que isso queria dizer? De repente, o vento apareceu e se espalhou. Soprou com muita força. Como alguém perdido, levantou poeira, revirou lixo e empurrou folhas. Em casa, estou sempre ouvindo música. Mas, diante da janela, minhas pálpebras se abriram ao máximo quando soaram estes versos na caixa de som: “Sou a chuva que lança a areia do Saara / Sobre os automóveis de Roma”.


Com muita fúria, a chuva grossa caiu e revelou a mesma paisagem sob um aspecto diferente. Agora um som aquoso corria pelas ruas inundadas e se sobrepunha ao silêncio. As fachadas dos prédios ficaram cada vez mais escuras e saturadas. Teimoso diante da janela, fui atingido também pela chuva, senti meu cabelo crespo molhado, certamente com gotículas cintilantes. O frio no meu rosto desceu para o peito por causa da camisa encharcada. Então me dei conta de que estava vestindo minha velha e confortável camisa que um dia foi branca, cuja estampa mostra o excêntrico protagonista do livro “Uma Confraria de Tolos”, de John Kennedy Toole.


Resolvi fechar a janela e busquei uma toalha para me enxugar. Enquanto trocava de blusa, lembrei da notícia que li faz pouco tempo: a história do peixe-leão capturado por pescadores no Porto da Barra. Apesar do nome majestoso, a espécie é de pequeno porte, o que não significa que não possa agir como um predador vigoroso. Vejo o bicho erguido na mão bronzeada do pescador, suas longas nadadeiras em forma de leque e sua coloração listrada em tons de vermelho, marrom, branco e preto. Assim, parece inofensivo. Então o jornal avisa que não devemos tocar diretamente no peixe, pois seus espinhos continuam venenosos mesmo após a sua morte. Também dizem que o peixe-leão não costuma atacar pessoas. Por fim, fico sabendo: o tal peixe venenoso é originário do oceano Indo-Pacífico e vem aparecendo na Bahia desde o ano passado. É, como sentencia o jornal, uma espécie exótica e invasora, que ameaça a nossa biodiversidade.


Depois que troquei a camisa molhada por uma limpa e seca, veio uma sensação gostosa de conforto e tranquilidade. A Capital da Alegria estava educadamente silenciosa, em estado de espera. A chuva provocou em mim um sentimento de introspecção. No conforto térmico de minha casa, me senti protegido dos perigos e dos barulhos do mundo. Quero ficar assim, sossegado, bebericando uma xícara fumegante de café enquanto leio um bom livro. Por curiosidade, alterno o olhar para a chuva agora fina que cai sobre este dia.


Tudo muda tão rápido. Tudo parece tão calmo. Nem parece que um Super El Niño se aproxima com seu efeito devastador sobre todos nós.

author: Politisches Cafe in der K9
title: Black British Cinema, Pressure (Horac Ove, UK 1975, 120 Minuten, OME
content:
Mittwoch, der 23. September um 19.30 Uhr in der K9, Kinzigstr. 9, 10247 Berlin (Friedrichshain), Nähe U-Bahnhof Samariters.


Runde Jahrestage werden ja eigentlich gern zur Identitätsvergewisserung genutzt. Etwas mag es da schon überraschen, dass es im Fall von 50 Jahre Punk, so der Eindruck nicht täuscht, doch eher ruhig geblieben ist. Sicher, auf arte und anderswo wird die für die Subkultur charakteristische rebellische Haltung abgefeiert und die üblichen Verdächtigen verlegen auf die musikalische Dimension fokussierte Erinnerungsliteratur. Blass bleiben hingegen die gesellschaftlichen Kontexte von Punk. Wir laden, mit dem bekannten Hintergrundbild des alten Clash-Promovideos zu ‚White Riot‘ aus dem Jahr 1976 im Hinterkopf, das randalierende Polizisten während des Notting Hill Carnivals im August 1976 zeigt, zu zwei kleinen Ausflügen in die ‚Kulissen‘.


Film: Black British Cinema


Pressure (Horace Ové, UK 1975, 120‘, OmE)


„Pressure“ wurde anlässlich seiner Uraufführung auf dem Londoner Filmfestival im Herbst 1975 in der dem schwarzen Marxisten C.L.R. James nahestehenden Zeitschrift „Race Today“ als „first full length feature film in Britain – inspired, scripted, directed and acted in the main by black people“ begrüßt – als ein Film, der trotz aller Schwächen, die eine derartige Pionierarbeit aufweisen müsse, erstmals „the inner soul of the black condition in Britain“ aufzudecken versuche. Horace Ovè (1936-1923), wie sein Co-Autor Samuel Selvon (1923-1994) in den 1950ern von Trinidad nach London migriert, beschreibt in seinem dokumentarisch-realistisch gehaltenen, von Neorealismus und Surrealismus inspirierten Low Budget-Film Lebens- und Erfahrungswelten sowie Selbstfindungsprozesse schwarzer Jugendlicher v.a. der dritten Generation im Vorfeld der Riots der späten 1970er und 1980er Jahre. „Pressure“ fungiert als solches als Klassiker nicht nur des „black british cinemas“ und Subtext späterer Filme wie bspw. Isaac Juliens (sich kritisch mit ‚Subkultur’ und ‚Rock against Racism‘ auseinandersetzendem) „Young Soul Rebels“ (1992) oder Steve McQueens Miniserie „Small Axe“ (2020).

author: Kreuzberg solidarisch gegen rechts/Café No Pasaran
title: Café No Pasaran: Analoger Treffpunkt gegen digitale Angriffe
content:
Mit der Entscheidung, das Tech-Kollektiv Autistici/Inventati auf die US-Terrorliste zu setzen, hat die Trump-Administration einen Angriff auf linke Infrastruktur gestartet. Mit noblogs.org hostete das Kollektiv mehrere hundert Blogs weltweit, die auch vielen emanzipatorischen, antifaschistischen Gruppen und Kollektiven die Möglichkeit boten, der rechten Diskursverschiebung entgegenzuwirken.


Auch unser Blog von Kreuzberg solidarisch gegen rechts war bei noblogs.org gehostet. Und das aus guten Gründen: Noblogs bot eine einfache und vor allem anonyme Möglichkeit, unsere Inhalte ins Netz zu stellen und für unsere Aktivitäten zu werben. In Zeiten des Rechtsrucks, in denen die Räume für emanzipatorische Politik enger werden und Antifaschist*innen zunehmend Bedrohungen von staatlicher und vor allem von faschistischer Seite ausgesetzt sind, ist Anonymität im Internet eine Voraussetzung dafür, auf der Straße antifaschistisch präsent sein zu können.


Mit A/I (bzw. noblogs.org) verschwindet eine der wenigen Möglichkeiten dafür ein für allemal aus dem Netz. Es wird zwar gerade nach Alternativen gesucht, den Verlust aufzufangen. Emanzipatorische, antifaschistische Politik sollte sich aber nicht alleine auf das Internet verlassen.


Antifaschismus ist und bleibt im wesentlichen eine Haltung, die sich vor allem im Alltag zeigt und dort auch praktisch wird. Der Angriff auf A/I hat auch gezeigt, dass es neben dezentralen Strukturen im Netz auch konkrete Orte in der realen Welt nötig sind, an denen Menschen sich kennenlernen und austauschen können.


Das Café No Pasaran der Initiative Kreuzberg solidarisch gegen rechts ist so ein Ort und genau aus dieser Idee geboren. Es öffnet jeden dritten Sonntag im Monat die Türen im RegenbogenCafé und lädt alle ein, die sich rechten Tendenzen in den Weg stellen wollen, vorbeizukommen.


Die nächste Gelegenheit ist am Tag der Wahlen zum Berliner Abgeordnetenhaus. Bei Kaffee und Kuchen kann sich über die zu erwartenden Ergebnisse und deren Konsequenzen ausgetauscht werden. Ab 18 Uhr werden die ersten Hochrechnungen geguckt und diskutiert.


Sonntag, 20.9.2026, ab 15 Uhr


Café No Pasaran


im RegenboganCafé


Lausitzer Str. 22 – Berlin-Kreuzberg

author: CNT Colmenar Viejo
title: 20 de septiembre. El crédito mutuo: una alternativa anarquista
content:
Este próximo

domingo 20 de septiembre a las 18:00 h, en el local del sindicato, calle Carrilejos 37 de Colmenar Viejo,

 nos juntamos realizar una charla-debate sobre el crédito mutuo como una alternativa anarquista.


El acceso obrero a crédito libre de usura ha sido una parte del programa revolucionario del anarquismo desde prácticamente los orígenes del movimiento con la propuesta de Proudhon del Banco del Pueblo en 1848. Este banco establecería un sistema de crédito mutuo que permitiera a la clase obrera establecer sus propias cooperativas para, de ese modo, tomar el control de los medios de producción en sociedad.


Junto al socorro mutuo y el apoyo mutuo, el crédito mutuo es uno de los ejes principales de la teoría mutualista de Proudhon y sus sucesores. Para profundizar en este sistema, en la CNT de Colmenar Viejo vamos a proyectar el próximo domingo 20 de Septiembre a las 18:00 para ver un pequeño video explicativo del divulgador Andrew Sage y realizar un coloquio posterior para discutir los pros y contras del modelo y su viabilidad como herramienta revolucionaria.

author: Unknown
title: Rencontre avec Magali Bessone autour de son nouvel ouvrage « Ce que nous devons à Haïti »
content:
Magali Bessone sera l'invitée de la librairie Le Monte-en-l'air (2 rue de la Mare, 75020 Paris), le vendredi 25 septembre à 19h30 à l'occasion de la sortie de son nouvel ouvrage «

 

Ce que nous devons à Haïti, réflexions philosophiques sur la justice réparatrice

 

» aux éditions La Découverte.


La rencontre sera animée par Pierre Tenne.


Présentation de l'ouvrage par la maison d'édition :


Un livre qui articule ambition théorique et portée politique : élaborer une philosophie de la domination postcoloniale et définir les contours d'une communauté politique occidentale (un

 

» nous «

 

) tenue par des exigences de la justice à l'égard des anciens pays colonisés.


À l'heure où les réparations pour les injustices héritées de l'esclavage et de la colonisation s'imposent comme un enjeu mondial, Magali Bessone propose, à partir du cas d'Haïti, une réflexion ambitieuse sur la justice réparatrice. Premier État issu d'une insurrection d'esclaves, Haïti fut contraint en 1825 de verser à la France une

 

» indemnité

 

» colossale pour obtenir la reconnaissance de son indépendance. Imposée sous la menace, cette rançon obligea le pays à souscrire des emprunts dont les effets pèsent encore dramatiquement sur le destin haïtien.


En articulant analyses juridiques, enquêtes historiques et réflexion philosophique, l'autrice montre que la justice réparatrice doit combiner trois dimensions indissociables : une réparation épistémique, contre l'effacement des faits et les stéréotypes persistants, une réparation économique, fondée sur la restitution de la

 

» double dette

 

» imposée au peuple haïtien, et une réparation politique visant la transformation des asymétries héritées du passé colonial.


Au-delà de l'analyse d'une injustice historique, le livre se distingue par son ambition transformatrice. Il invite à repenser nos obligations collectives et la possibilité d'un

 

» nous

 

» politique. Qui décidons-nous d'être, en France et dans le monde, face à cet héritage colonial

 

? Comment les réparations peuvent-elles fonder des relations internationales plus justes, au-delà de la charité ou de l'aide au développement

 

? En répondant à ces questions, ce livre offre une boîte à outils conceptuelle et pratique pour repenser la justice globale à l'ère postcoloniale.


Magali Bessone est professeure de philosophie politique à l'Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne et membre de l'Institut Universitaire de France. Ses travaux portent sur les théories de la justice ainsi que sur la philosophie critique de la race et des racismes.

content:
La librairie Le Monte-en-l'air (2 rue de la Mare, 75020 Paris) accueillera la Revue des livres et des idées pour le lancement de son premier numéro papier le jeudi 24 septembre à 19h30.


Sera prévue une présentation du projet, quelques interventions de contributeurices du premier numéro, et un moment convivial pour fêter cette superbe nouvelle

 

!


Présentation de la Revue :


Essentiellement composée de longues recensions d'essais et d'articles de fond, la Revue des livres et des idées travaille le domaine de l'idéologie. Elle a pour ambition de redonner ses lettres de noblesse à la critique et de nourrir les débats théoriques à gauche, en proposant des textes approfondis et agréables à lire.


Son premier numéro, illustré par une série photographique de Bruce Gilden, réunit onze articles d'Eyal Weizman, Verónica Gago, Emily Witt, Matthieu Renault, Benjamin Bürbaumer, Claude Serfati, Laleh Khalili, Jean-François Hamel, Selim Nadi, Benjamin Gizard et Nathalie Quintane.


De l'Argentine de Milei à la reconstruction de Gaza, des réseaux masculinistes à l'ascension de la Chine, de l'

OTAN

 aux réseaux logistiques, il analyse les tensions et contradictions du système-monde. Il revient sur l'histoire communiste à travers la photographie ouvrière et la trajectoire de Dionys Mascolo, tout en interrogeant la fonction politique de l'utopie et les potentialités de la poésie contemporaine.

author: Anneke Demanuele
title: Ed Sheeran is a spineless twat
content:
“I just have a little message for you: there are two kinds of people in this world, Ed. There’re people who do the right thing—the rapper Macklemore would be one of those people. And there’re people—many of them, sadly little f ... excuse me, I nearly used the F-word then ... pricks—like you who do the wrong thing!”

So said Roger Waters, former Pink Floyd frontman and long-term supporter of the Palestinian people, via social media to singer Ed Sheeran, who has just committed a generational flop.

Bowing to the pressure of billionaires in a bid to stay “neutral”, Sheeran recently dropped rapper Macklemore from his

Loop

 tour due to Macklemore’s pro-Palestine stance. In solidarity with Macklemore, all of the supporting artists, including Ed’s own band, dropped out of the tour.

The controversy began when billionaire New England Patriots stadium owner Robert Kraft phoned Sheeran with a clear demand: Macklemore would be removed from the show, or the show would not go on.

Macklemore drew the ire of Kraft after declaring his support for Palestine and performing his song “Hind’s Hall” at a concert at MetLife Stadium. “Hind’s Hall” was written when the campus encampments in solidarity with Gaza were at their height in the US. It is a tribute to 5-year-old Hind Rajab, who was killed along with five family members and two paramedics by the Israeli military in January 2024 while fleeing Gaza City. Hind survived an initial attack on the family’s car, after which she spent hours on the phone to the Red Crescent, begging for help. Her body, and the remains of the paramedics sent to rescue her, were found weeks later, along with the car the family had been travelling in, which had been shot at more than 300 times.

With the words “Free Palestine” emblazoned behind him, Macklemore told the MetLife audience:

“The truth is, a big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I can stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine. I want those words to be loud and clear so the people all the way in Gaza, to the occupied West Bank, know that we have not forgotten about them.”

After the performance, singer P!NK criticised Macklemore on social media, reposting a meme that attacked the rapper for his pro-Palestine stance. In response, a group of stadium owners banded together to cancel Macklemore. Their ownership of stadiums across the US gave them a power that most of us don’t have—to decide who gets to say what and where.

Macklemore has used his music to highlight questions of oppression for decades. His 2012 hit “Same Love” was a declaration of support for marriage equality when same-sex marriage was banned in most of the world, including the United States and Australia. During the marriage-equality plebiscite in Australia, Macklemore performed at the NRL grand final, in what was seen as an implicit endorsement of equality. Macklemore has also been openly proclaiming his support for Gaza and the Palestinian people throughout the last three years of Israeli genocide.

In the last few years, many artists have been attacked for their support for Palestine. Irish rap group Kneecap were dragged through the courts on trumped-up terrorism-related charges due to their support for Palestine. The rap duo Bob Vylan was attacked by the media and cancelled from tours, and had their US visas cancelled, for chanting “Death to the IDF” at the Glastonbury festival.

As with Kneecap and Bob Vylan, Macklemore’s stance has drawn support from other decent musicians and celebrities who also oppose genocide. Finneas, the brother of Billie Elish, was also an act on the

Loop

 tour and pulled out in solidarity. His post declaring “Artists must not be silenced when they speak for the oppressed ... I stand with Palestine and its people” has more than 2 million likes on Instagram. Sheeran, on the other hand, has been left without support acts, without a backing band, and with just one ageing billionaire stadium-owner willing to associate with him. And Boy George.

Sheeran has also been exposed as having no spine and limited brains. The singer’s pathetic post responding to the controversy emphasised his desire to be “apolitical” and his concern not to corrupt the youth: “There is a reason I don’t use my professional platform for politics—my audience includes young people”. Someone should tell Sheeran that young people are affected by politics, particularly Palestinian …
